citation: Kosmicki/Kaplanis-type aggregate analysis: Large-scale discovery of novel neurodevelopmental disorder-related genes through a unified analysis of single-nucleotide and copy number variants (PMID: 35468861)
variant_detail: Recurrent de novo damaging missense variants (affecting the same amino acid positions) in KIAA0100; specific substitutions not given in the text provided
phenotype: Neurodevelopmental disorder (unspecified, aggregated NDD cohort)
diagnostic_reason: Recurrent de novo damaging missense (d-MIS) variants affecting the same amino acids; KIAA0100 is listed among 26 candidate genes (with PSMC3, PIP5K1C, SEPT2, KBTBD7, REST, MAST3) whose recurrence is taken to suggest pathogenicity and NDD association. Gene-level enrichment in 41,165 NDD cases (including DDD and denovo-db data).

citation: Multiple interactions recruit BLTP2 to ER-PM contacts to control plasma membrane dynamics (PMID: 40899996)
summary: BLTP2/KIAA0100 is a bridge-like lipid transfer protein that localizes to ER-PM contacts. It tethers the ER to tubular endosomes only after they become continuous with the PM, and to macropinosomes that are fusing with the PM. This supports a role in bulk ER-to-PM lipid transport. Loss of BLTP2 causes accumulation of intracellular vacuoles, many connected to the PM, which points to a role in PM dynamics.

citation: Multiple interactions mediate the localization of BLTP2 at ER-PM contacts to control plasma membrane dynamics (PMID: 39974967)
summary: BLTP2 binds the PM through phosphoinositides, the adaptor proteins FAM102A/FAM102B, and N-BAR domain proteins at membrane-connected tubules. These interactions recruit it to ER-PM contacts.

citation: KIAA0100 Modulates Cancer Cell Aggression Behavior of MDA-MB-231 through Microtubule and Heat Shock Proteins (PMID: 29867023)
summary: siRNA silencing of KIAA0100 in MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells reduced aggregation, reattachment, metastasis and invasion. It sensitized suspended cells to anoikis. IP-mass spectrometry and immunofluorescence suggest KIAA0100 binds and stabilizes microtubules and interacts with HSPA1A to promote anoikis resistance.

citation: Bioinformatic prediction and functional characterization of human KIAA0100 gene (PMID: 29404013)
summary: CRISPR/Cas9 knockdown of KIAA0100 in U937 acute monocytic leukemia cells inhibited proliferation and promoted apoptosis, suggesting an anti-apoptotic role. Bioinformatics placed the gene at 17q11.2 and predicted a secretory pathway protein with a signal peptide, a transmembrane region and FMP27 domains.

citation: Circ_0000520 interacts with miR-512-5p to upregulate KIAA0100 to promote malignant behaviors in lung cancer (PMID: 35866672)
summary: KIAA0100 is a direct target of miR-512-5p, shown by dual-luciferase assay. The circ_0000520/miR-512-5p/KIAA0100 axis drives lung cancer proliferation, migration, invasion and angiogenesis, and tumor growth in xenografts. miR-512-5p suppresses these malignant behaviors by downregulating KIAA0100.

citation: Preparation of monoclonal antibody against human KIAA0100 protein and Northern blot analysis of human KIAA0100 gene (PMID: 29404037)
summary: A mouse monoclonal antibody was generated against KIAA0100 (residues 1557-2234). In U937 cells, Western blot suggested two protein products (254 kDa and <250 kDa). Northern blot showed two mRNA species (6000-10000 bp and 5000-6000 bp).

citation: Identification of BCOX1, a novel gene overexpressed in breast cancer (PMID: 16289875)
summary: BCOX1, highly homologous to KIAA0100 at 17q11.2, is overexpressed in breast carcinoma. It is cytoplasmic in carcinoma epithelial cells but absent in normal epithelium, stroma and lymphocytes. Expression rises from DCIS to a peak in invasive and metastatic carcinoma.

citation: Profiling the Somatic Mutational Landscape of Breast Tumors from Hispanic/Latina Women (PMID: 37145128)
summary: A recurrent 17q11.2 copy-number amplification in Hispanic/Latina breast tumors was associated with high KIAA0100 expression. This amplification was more prevalent than in tumors from White women in TCGA.

citation: Bioinformatics-based modeling of lung squamous cell carcinoma prognosis and prediction of immunotherapy response (PMID: 39724502)
summary: KIAA0100 is one of 11 genes in a Cox prognostic risk model for lung squamous cell carcinoma built from GEO and TCGA expression data. Its expression is associated with patient survival.

citation: A de novo missense variant in MIDEAS results in increased deacetylase activity of the MiDAC HDAC complex causing a neurodevelopmental syndrome (PMID: 41290615)
variant_detail: p.Tyr654Ser (de novo heterozygous; cDNA notation not given in abstract)
phenotype: delayed speech development; joint contractures; dysmorphic features; gut dysmotility; multisystem disorder
diagnostic_reason: Same de novo heterozygous missense variant in two unrelated individuals. Located in a conserved auto-inhibitory loop covering the deacetylase active site (cryoEM structure). Predicted to displace the loop and increase MiDAC deacetylase activity. Patient fibroblasts show gene expression changes reciprocal to those seen after rapid MiDAC degradation.

citation: Bantscheff/Millard et al. 2020 - The MiDAC histone deacetylase complex is essential for embryonic development and has a unique multivalent structure (PMID: 32591534)
phenotype: Late embryonic death, with a phenotype identical to Dnttip1 knockout mice; Heart malformation; Haematopoietic failure; Perturbed gene expression in embryos

citation: Clinical genetics/structural study 2025 - A de novo missense variant in MIDEAS results in increased deacetylase activity of the MiDAC HDAC complex causing a neurodevelopmental syndrome (PMID: 41290615)
summary: Two unrelated individuals with a multisystem neurodevelopmental disorder (delayed speech, joint contractures, dysmorphism, gut dysmotility) carry the same de novo MIDEAS p.Tyr654Ser variant. CryoEM places Tyr654 in an auto-inhibitory loop covering the HDAC active site, so the variant is proposed to displace the loop and raise MiDAC deacetylase activity. Patient fibroblasts show gene expression changes reciprocal to those seen after rapid MiDAC degradation.

citation: 2020 - The MiDAC histone deacetylase complex is essential for embryonic development and has a unique multivalent structure (PMID: 32591534)
summary: Mice lacking MIDEAS or DNTTIP1 die with identical late-embryonic phenotypes, including heart malformation and haematopoietic failure, linked to perturbed gene expression. MiDAC is also important for chromosome alignment in mitosis in cancer cell lines. The cryoEM structure shows four HDAC1 copies at the periphery with outward-facing active sites.

citation: 2020 - The histone deacetylase complex MiDAC regulates a neurodevelopmental gene expression program to control neurite outgrowth (PMID: 32297854)
summary: MiDAC regulates a neurodevelopmental gene expression program. It upregulates SLIT3 and NTN1, probably by removing H4K20ac at promoters and enhancers, and represses negative regulators of neurogenesis by reducing H3K27ac. MiDAC loss causes neurite outgrowth defects that SLIT3 and/or NTN1 supplementation rescues.

citation: 2025 - Mutations on the surface of HDAC1 reveal molecular determinants of specific complex assembly and their requirement for gene regulation (PMID: 40966515)
summary: Comparing the MIDEAS:HDAC1 and MTA1:HDAC1 structures identified HDAC1 surface residues needed for complex binding. The HDAC1 Y48E mutation disrupts binding to all complexes except SIN3. The E63R mutation markedly reduces binding to NuRD and MiDAC, and both mutants perturb gene expression and histone acetylation in cells.

citation: 2015 - Structural and functional characterization of a cell cycle associated HDAC1/2 complex reveals the structural basis for complex assembly and nucleosome targeting (PMID: 25653165)
summary: MIDEAS is a corepressor in a cell cycle-associated complex with HDAC1/2 and DNTTIP1 that is upregulated in mitosis and associated with cyclin A. The DNTTIP1 N-terminal dimerization domain mediates assembly of the HDAC1:MIDEAS complex. Its C-terminal domain binds DNA and nucleosomes, so DNTTIP1 acts as a dimeric chromatin-binding module.

citation: 2024 - Mitotic deacetylase complex (MiDAC) recognizes the HIV-1 core promoter to control activated viral gene expression (PMID: 38781120)
summary: DNA-affinity chromatography identified MiDAC as selectively recognizing the HIV core promoter TASHET element. DNTTIP1 binds TASHET directly and co-immunoprecipitates with MIDEAS and HDAC1/2. Gene silencing of MIDEAS, DNTTIP1 or NAT10 altered HIV expression in cells, implicating MIDEAS in Tat-activated transcription and latency.

citation: 2023 - Long non-coding RNA MIDEAS-AS1 inhibits growth and metastasis of triple-negative breast cancer via transcriptionally activating NCALD (PMID: 37770991)
significance: correlated with poor OS and PFS (p-values not given in abstract)
summary: The antisense lncRNA MIDEAS-AS1 (not the MIDEAS protein) is downregulated in TNBC, and low levels correlate with poor OS and PFS. It interacts with MATR3 to activate NCALD transcription, which inactivates NF-κB signaling and suppresses tumor growth and metastasis.

citation: 2025 - DNA methylation in peripheral blood leukocytes in late onset Alzheimer's disease (PMID: 40343304)
summary: Differential methylation analysis of public blood datasets (GSE59685, GSE53740) listed MIDEAS among differentially methylated genes in late-onset Alzheimer's disease patients versus controls. This is an epigenetic association rather than a GWAS.

citation: Identifying Novel Osteoarthritis-Associated Genes in Human Cartilage Using a Systematic Meta-Analysis and a Multi-Source Integrated Network (PMID: 35457215)
summary: ARPC4-TTLL3 was identified as one of five novel osteoarthritis-associated proteins. It emerged from a ranked multi-source network of 1689 genes built from a meta-analysis of differentially expressed mRNAs and miRNAs, miRNA targets and SNP datasets. Mass spectrometry of superficial, middle and deep zones of human osteoarthritic cartilage compared with normal controls confirmed it at the protein level, alongside PPIB, ASS1, LHDB and TPI1. The abstract does not state the direction of change or any mechanism for ARPC4-TTLL3.

citation: Wang et al. 2020 - Large-scale targeted sequencing identifies risk genes for neurodevelopmental disorders (PMID: 33004838)
variant_detail: Not specified; de novo missense variants (dnMIS) enriched in H2AC6 in the NDD cohort. No individual variant notations provided in the available text.
phenotype: Neurodevelopmental disorder (NDD)/autism cohort; no per-patient phenotypes reported
diagnostic_reason: Statistical excess of de novo missense mutations in H2AC6 (dnMIS q = 0.053, FDR 5%) in a large NDD trio cohort; gene was also selected as a CNV candidate. No per-patient clinical evaluation was provided.

citation: Tribulus terrestris L. protects glomerular endothelial cells via the miR155-H2AC6 interaction network in hypertensive renal injury (PMID: 34926670)
summary: In an AngII-induced hypertensive renal injury model in glomerular endothelial cells, integrated miRNA/mRNA profiling and qRT-PCR showed that miR-155-5p expression was negatively correlated with H2AC6. TrT treatment raised miR-155-5p, which negatively regulates H2AC6 expression, so H2AC6 is proposed as a candidate therapeutic target.

citation: Unveiling the Therapeutic Potential of Baicalin in Intervertebral Disc Degeneration: Integrative Bulk and Single-Cell Transcriptome Analysis with Experimental Validation of PANoptosis Inhibition (PMID: 40463856)
significance: significantly upregulated (exact p-value not given in abstract)
summary: H2AC6 was one of five core PANoptosis-related genes (with FOS, CASP1, H1-2, BCL2L11) significantly upregulated in degenerated discs. This was validated in clinical samples, an IL-1β-induced NPC model and a rat puncture IVDD model. Baicalin downregulated H2AC6 at the mRNA and protein levels.

citation: Inhibition of lactylation by LRP1 expression increases the risk of intervertebral disc degeneration: A multi-omics summary-based Mendelian randomization analysis (PMID: 40988222)
summary: In SMR analysis using eQTL and IVDD GWAS data, higher genetically predicted H2AC6 expression was positively associated with IVDD risk. H2AC6 is a lactylation-related gene. It did not remain among the final mQTL-eQTL-integrated genes (KAT5, CEACAM6, LRP1).

citation: Global comparative transcriptomes uncover novel and population-specific gene expression in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (PMID: 37641095)
sample_size: six global populations (microarray datasets); TCGA for survival
summary: H2AC6 was identified as a novel differentially expressed gene in ESCC across populations. TCGA survival analysis marked it as one of three genes (with CHRM3 and CREG2) critical for ESCC survival, making it a potential diagnostic or prognostic biomarker.

citation: Mitochondrial metabolism and succinylation-related gene signatures for predicting prognosis and drug resistance in colon adenocarcinoma (PMID: 42176930)
summary: H2AC6 is one of two hub genes (with MC1R) in a prognostic model for COAD. It was an independent prognostic factor, and its expression pattern was consistent across single-cell sequencing and qRT-PCR. The model's gene set was enriched for protein heterodimerization and neutrophil extracellular trap formation.

citation: Serum extracellular vesicle RNA profiles in long COVID: insights from exercise-induced gene modulation (PMID: 41588020)
summary: After exercise training, H2AC6 transcript in serum extracellular vesicles was among the top 5 downregulated genes at peak exercise compared with rest in long COVID patients. The downregulated genes were linked to inflammation and metabolism.

citation: Molecular characterization of FAM222B as a novel disease gene for dominant cardiovascular laterality defects (PMID: 42632841)
variant_detail: c.899G>A, p.Arg300His (de novo in two unrelated families)
phenotype: cardiovascular laterality defects; situs inversus totalis; heterotaxy; congenital heart defects
diagnostic_reason: Recurrent de novo c.899G>A (p.Arg300His) in two unrelated families, identified by trio exome sequencing and exome survey of 2,109 individuals. Structural modelling suggests Arg300 is involved in NLK recognition. Zebrafish double-knockout fam222ba/bb showed aberrant cardiac looping, and injection of the human mutant mRNA perturbed cardiogenesis.

citation: Molecular characterization of FAM222B as a novel disease gene for dominant cardiovascular laterality defects (PMID: 42632841)
variant_detail: Five additional FAM222B variants (not specified in abstract)
phenotype: cardiovascular laterality defects; situs inversus totalis; heterotaxy; congenital heart defects
diagnostic_reason: Recurrent de novo c.899G>A (p.Arg300His) in two unrelated families, identified by trio exome sequencing and exome survey of 2,109 individuals. Structural modelling suggests Arg300 is involved in NLK recognition. Zebrafish double-knockout fam222ba/bb showed aberrant cardiac looping, and injection of the human mutant mRNA perturbed cardiogenesis.

citation: FAM222B Is Not a Likely Novel Candidate Gene for Cerebral Cavernous Malformations (PMID: 27587990)
variant_detail: Autosomal dominantly inherited frameshift mutation in FAM222B (C17orf63); exact notation not given in abstract
phenotype: cerebral cavernous malformations
diagnostic_reason: Identified by exome sequencing in CCM patients negative for CCM1-3, segregating dominantly in a family. Authors ultimately concluded FAM222B is not likely a CCM gene, since zebrafish double mutants and HUVEC siRNA assays showed no phenotype.

citation: Molecular characterization of FAM222B as a novel disease gene for dominant cardiovascular laterality defects (PMID: 42632841)
phenotype: aberrant cardiac looping in double-knockout larvae; enlarged atrium and ventricle in adult double-knockout zebrafish; perturbed cardiogenesis after injection of human mRNA carrying the c.899G>A (p.Arg300His) variant into Tg(kdrl:EGFP) wild-type embryos
knockout_type: full knockout (double knockout of fam222ba/fam222bb paralogs); human c.899G>A mRNA overexpression injections in Tg(kdrl:EGFP) wild-type embryos

citation: FAM222B Is Not a Likely Novel Candidate Gene for Cerebral Cavernous Malformations (PMID: 27587990)
phenotype: no phenotype resembling existing CCM models (e.g., ccm1/ccm2/ccm3 mutants) in the double mutant zebrafish; no vascular phenotype reported in the double mutants; in vitro siRNA knockdown of FAM222B in HUVECs showed no sprouting phenotype (human cells, not an animal model)

citation: Molecular characterization of FAM222B as a novel disease gene for dominant cardiovascular laterality defects (PMID: 42632841)
sample_size: 16 case-parent trios; 2,109 individuals in exome survey
summary: Exome sequencing of 16 case-parent trios and a survey of 2,109 individuals with situs inversus totalis, heterotaxy, or isolated CHD found six FAM222B variants. The p.Arg300His variant (c.899G>A) arose de novo in two unrelated families. Structural modelling places Arg300 in NLK recognition, and NLK is linked to left-right axis determination. Human p.Arg300His mRNA injected into Tg(kdrl:EGFP) zebrafish perturbed cardiogenesis.

citation: Molecular characterization of FAM222B as a novel disease gene for dominant cardiovascular laterality defects (PMID: 42632841)
summary: A fam222ba/bb double-knockout zebrafish line showed aberrant cardiac looping in larvae and enlarged atrium and ventricle in adults. This supports a role for FAM222B in heart laterality and morphogenesis. The study also examined WISH expression patterns and genomic context of the zebrafish homologues fam222ba, fam222bb, and fam222aa.

citation: FAM222B Is Not a Likely Novel Candidate Gene for Cerebral Cavernous Malformations (PMID: 27587990)
summary: A yeast 2-hybrid screen showed FAM222B interacting with the tubulin cytoskeleton and with STAMBP, which is associated with microcephaly-capillary malformation syndrome. A frameshift mutation in FAM222B was found in an autosomal dominant CCM family by exome sequencing.

citation: FAM222B Is Not a Likely Novel Candidate Gene for Cerebral Cavernous Malformations (PMID: 27587990)
summary: siRNA knockdown of FAM222B in HUVECs did not alter in vitro sprouting. TALEN-generated fam222bb/fam222ba double-mutant zebrafish also showed no CCM-like phenotype, arguing against a role in CCM formation.

citation: Delphinidin upregulates microRNA-let-7b expression through family with sequence similarity 222 member B (PMID: 40789939)
summary: A genetic functional screen in melanoma cells identified Fam222B as a mediator of delphinidin's anti-proliferative effect, which acts through upregulation of let-7b and suppression of cyclin D1. Fam222B siRNA in B16 cells altered miRNA expression, implicating Fam222B in regulating miRNA expression.

citation: Evolutionary analysis through structural modeling of FAM222 proteins reveals a novel disordered conserved domain in vertebrates that interacts with NLK (PMID: 41365991)
summary: FAM222B contains the conserved intrinsically disordered domain DCD222, which AlphaFold3 predicts binds NLK through a reverse docking motif and β-hairpin/β-sheet insertions. Molecular dynamics simulations showed the interface is stable. The catalytic site is not obstructed, so FAM222A/B are proposed to be NLK modulators rather than simple substrates.

citation: Evolutionary analysis through structural modeling of FAM222 proteins reveals a novel disordered conserved domain in vertebrates that interacts with NLK (PMID: 41365991)
summary: Through its interaction with NLK, FAM222B is linked to NLK-regulated signaling (WNT, NOTCH, VEGF, mTOR, TGF-β). DCD222 is conserved from cyclostomes to humans, indicating strong evolutionary constraint.

citation: Exploration of signature-related FAM genes and correlation between FAM50A expression and the pathogenesis and prognosis of hepatocellular carcinoma (PMID: 40950660)
summary: Pan-database analysis (TCGA, GTEx, ICGC, GEO, HPA, CPTAC) identified FAM222B as one of five overexpressed, signature-related FAM genes in HCC, validated at mRNA and protein levels. The study's functional follow-up focused on FAM50A rather than FAM222B.

citation: Genomic analysis of 116 autism families strengthens known risk genes and highlights promising candidates (PMID: 38519481)
phenotype: Autism spectrum disorder (ADOS-2 autism, score 8; CARS2-ST 34.5); Atypical language; Normal IQ (Leiter-R B-IQ 111)
diagnostic_reason: Classified as VUS (ACMG criteria PS2, PP3, BS4); de novo, predicted damaging, but not considered diagnostic

citation: Large-scale discovery of novel neurodevelopmental disorder-related genes through a unified analysis of single-nucleotide and copy number variants (PMID: 35468861)
variant_detail: Recurrent de novo damaging missense variants affecting the same amino acid(s) (specific variants not given in the text)
phenotype: Neurodevelopmental disorder
diagnostic_reason: Recurrent de novo damaging missense variants at the same amino acid positions in NDD cases, which supports pathogenicity and gene association. KBTBD7 is one of 26 candidate genes.

citation: An exome sequencing study of Moebius syndrome including atypical cases reveals an individual with CFEOM3A and a TUBB3 mutation (PMID: 28299356)
variant_detail: NM_032138.4 c.1496C>G, p.Pro499Arg (rs754048481), heterozygous
phenotype: Moebius syndrome (congenital facial and abducens nerve palsies)
diagnostic_reason: Not considered diagnostic. The variant was inherited from an unaffected parent, so it was judged unlikely to cause disease. Rare variants in KBTBD7 were shared by two individuals.

citation: Wang et al. 2020 - The KBTBD6/7-DRD2 axis regulates pituitary adenoma sensitivity to dopamine agonist treatment (PMID: 32572597)
phenotype: KBTBD7 KO mice generated by CRISPR-Cas9; Elevated steady-state DRD2 protein in pituitary gland, thalamus, and heart compared to WT mice; Supports KBTBD7 as an E3 ligase adaptor controlling DRD2 degradation in vivo

citation: Regulation of Wnt/PCP signaling through p97/VCP-KBTBD7-mediated Vangl ubiquitination and endoplasmic reticulum-associated degradation (PMID: 33990333)
phenotype: KBTBD7 regulates convergent extension during zebrafish gastrulation (in vivo evidence of a Wnt/PCP-related gastrulation defect upon KBTBD7 perturbation); Consistent with increased Vangl stability upon KBTBD7 loss

citation: Genau et al. 2015 - CUL3-KBTBD6/KBTBD7 ubiquitin ligase cooperates with GABARAP proteins to spatially restrict TIAM1-RAC1 signaling (PMID: 25684205)
summary: KBTBD6 and KBTBD7 act as substrate adaptors for a CUL3 RING ubiquitin ligase that ubiquitylates TIAM1 (a RAC1 GEF) and targets it for proteasomal degradation. They bind GABARAP proteins through ATG8-interacting motifs, and TIAM1 degradation depends on this binding. Depleting KBTBD6/7 raises RAC1 activity, alters actin morphology, reduces focal adhesions and proliferation, and increases invasion.

citation: Regulation of Wnt/PCP signaling through p97/VCP-KBTBD7-mediated Vangl ubiquitination and endoplasmic reticulum-associated degradation (PMID: 33990333)
summary: KBTBD7 is an E3 ligase recruited by p97/VCP through its UBA-UBX adaptors. It promotes ubiquitination and ERAD of the Wnt/PCP components Vangl1 and Vangl2. In vivo, KBTBD7 regulates convergent extension during zebrafish gastrulation and acts as a tumor suppressor in breast cancer by promoting Vangl degradation.

citation: The KBTBD6/7-DRD2 axis regulates pituitary adenoma sensitivity to dopamine agonist treatment (PMID: 32572597)
summary: A yeast two-hybrid screen identified KBTBD7 as a DRD2-interacting protein. KBTBD6/7 are CUL3 substrate adaptors that ubiquitinate DRD2 at five lysines (K221, K226, K241, K251, K258). KBTBD7 knockout mice had elevated DRD2 in pituitary, thalamus and heart. KBTBD7 is highly expressed in dopamine-resistant prolactinomas, and its knockdown sensitizes cells to cabergoline.

citation: KBTBD7 promotes non-small cell lung carcinoma progression by enhancing ubiquitin-dependent degradation of PTEN (PMID: 35499228)
summary: KBTBD7 is highly expressed in NSCLC tissue compared with paired normal tissue by IHC. Expression correlates with histological type, TNM stage, lymph node metastasis and tumor size. Knockdown reduced NSCLC cell proliferation and invasion. KBTBD7 promotes ubiquitin-dependent PTEN degradation, which activates EGFR/PI3K/AKT signaling.

citation: MicroRNA-21 prevents excessive inflammation and cardiac dysfunction after myocardial infarction through targeting KBTBD7 (PMID: 29991775)
summary: miR-21 directly targets KBTBD7. KBTBD7 interacts with MKK3/6 and promotes their activation, which enhances p38 and NF-κB signaling and DAMP-triggered inflammatory cytokine production in macrophages after MI.

citation: Targeting of ubiquitination and degradation of KLF15 by E3 ubiquitin ligase KBTBD7 regulates LPS-induced septic brain injury in microglia (PMID: 39489209)
summary: KBTBD7 interacts with KLF15 by co-IP and acts as an E3 ligase that ubiquitinates KLF15 for proteasomal degradation. KBTBD7 is upregulated in CLP rat microglia and in LPS-treated microglia. Its knockdown reduces cytokine release and NLRP3/NF-κB activation, and this effect depends on KLF15.

citation: Knockdown of KBTBD7 attenuates septic lung injury by inhibiting ferroptosis and improving mitochondrial dysfunction (PMID: 38652964)
summary: KBTBD7 is highly expressed in LPS-treated human alveolar epithelial cells. Knockdown reduced inflammation, ROS, ferroptosis and mitochondrial dysfunction. KBTBD7 interacts with FOXA1 and promotes its expression, which indirectly represses SLC7A11 transcription. Knockdown also improved lung injury in septic mice.

citation: New TFII-I family target genes involved in embryonic development (PMID: 19527686)
summary: Kbtbd7 (1110008P08Rik) was strongly down-regulated in Gtf2i and Gtf2ird1 mutant mouse embryos, and its promoter has conserved TFII-I binding sites, so it is a likely direct TFII-I target. It encodes a BTB/BACK/Kelch adapter, and its expression pattern suggests a role in brain development. It is a candidate contributor to Williams syndrome.

citation: A transcriptome-wide association study of uterine fibroids to identify potential genetic markers and toxic chemicals (PMID: 36174000)
summary: A TWAS integrating uterine fibroid GWAS data with eQTL data identified KBTBD7 as a novel candidate susceptibility gene for uterine fibroid.

citation: A Robust 8-Gene Prognostic Signature for Early-Stage Non-small Cell Lung Cancer (PMID: 31417870)
sample_size: GSE31210, GSE37745, GSE50081 and TCGA cohorts
summary: KBTBD7 expression was associated with overall survival in early-stage NSCLC across GEO and TCGA cohorts. It is one of eight genes in an independent prognostic risk signature.

citation: ASHG 2018 - Systematic scoring of candidate genes for neurodevelopmental disorders has a higher yield than large meta-analyses (Jamra et al.)
variant_detail: Not specified; FBXL19 listed among top-scoring candidate genes with potentially causative variants in trio exome sequencing of undiagnosed NDD cases
phenotype: neurodevelopmental disorder
diagnostic_reason: Candidate gene variant prioritized by a 13-parameter scoring system (inheritance, gene and variant attributes, literature); FBXL19 was in the top 10% of scores. No variant-level detail is provided.
center_country: Germany (Leipzig/Jamra group, with collaborating German centers; exome sequencing by Centogene, Rostock, and CeGaT, Tübingen)

citation: Williamson et al. 2018 - FBXL19 recruits CDK-Mediator to CpG islands of developmental genes priming them for activation during lineage commitment (PMID: 29809150)
phenotype: Recognition of CpG islands by FBXL19 (via its CxxC zinc finger domain) is reported to be essential for mouse development; The abstract does not give details of the in vivo phenotype (e.g. the stage of developmental failure); In ES cells, loss of FBXL19 CpG island binding impairs CDK-Mediator recruitment to developmental gene promoters and priming of these genes for activation during lineage commitment

citation: Posttranslational regulation of CREB-binding protein expression by F-box leucine-rich repeat-containing protein 19 and ubiquitin-specific peptidase 14 in the paraventricular nucleus participates in chronic stress-induced symptomatology via the modulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis (PMID: 41028568)
phenotype: Genetic knockdown of FBXL19 in the paraventricular nucleus (PVN) of naive mice mimicked chronic stress and produced a similar symptomatology; This was mediated by increased CRH biosynthesis, which required the CBP-CREB interaction and CBP acetyltransferase activity; Genetic knockout of FBXL19 aggravated chronic stress-induced symptomatology (depression-like/neuropsychiatric behaviors); Overexpression of FBXL19 or TAT-FBXL19 infusion in the PVN reversed chronic stress-induced symptomatology; Chronic social defeat stress and chronic unpredictable mild stress altered the FBXL19-USP14-CBP system in the PVN

citation: Turberfield et al. 2019 - FBXL19 recruits CDK-Mediator to CpG islands of developmental genes priming them for activation during lineage commitment (PMID: 29809150)
summary: FBXL19 was identified as a CpG island-binding protein in mouse ES cells that associates with the CDK-Mediator complex. It recruits CDK-Mediator to CpG island promoters of non-transcribed developmental genes, priming them for activation during lineage commitment. CpG island recognition by FBXL19 is essential for mouse development.

citation: Identification and characterization of FBXL19 gene in silico (PMID: 15547684)
summary: Bioinformatic identification of human FBXL19 (CXXC11) as a 674-aa protein encoded by 10 exons at 16p11.2, paralogous to FBXL10 and FBXL11 and sharing the FBXHA (containing CXXC) and FBXHB (containing F-box) domains. Human FBXL19 shows 97.5% amino-acid identity with mouse Fbxl19.

citation: FBXL19 in endothelial cells protects the heart from influenza A infection by enhancing antiviral immunity and reducing cellular senescence programs (PMID: 39150394)
summary: In a mouse model of influenza A infection, EC-specific FBXL19 overexpression reduced viral titers and M1 protein. It increased IFN-α/β/γ and RANTES, restored IRF3 protein (not mRNA) levels, and reduced cardiac inflammation. It also partially reversed IAV-induced senescence markers (p16/p21 up, lamin-B1 down).

citation: Epigenetic Regulation of Immune and Inflammatory Responses in Rheumatoid Arthritis (PMID: 35479077)
summary: An integrative epigenetic network analysis of RA datasets (GEO) identified FBXL19 as one of five hub genes (with CHD3, SETD1B, SMARCA4, SETD1A) associated with immune cells and inflammatory responses.

citation: ASHG 2011 - Meta-analysis of genome-wide association studies identifies additional susceptibility loci for psoriasis
summary: A meta-GWAS of three European cohorts showed support for the FBXL19 locus as a known psoriasis susceptibility locus.

citation: The pathogenesis and genetics of psoriasis (PMID: 23369832)
summary: This review places FBXL19 among psoriasis-associated genes involved in innate immune responses and NF-κB signaling, together with TNFAIP3, TNIP1, NFKBIA, REL, TYK2, NOS2 and CARD14.

citation: ASHG 2022 - Glucocorticoids unmask silent non-coding genetic risk variants for common diseases
summary: Obesity-associated SNPs mediated cortisol-responsive (glucocorticoid receptor-dependent) expression of FBXL19, described as an adipogenesis-controlling gene, in a GR-mediated eQTL analysis in B-lymphoblastoid cell lines.

citation: Long Noncoding RNA FBXL19-AS1 Expedites Cell Growth, Migration and Invasion in Cervical Cancer by miR-193a-5p/PIN1 Signaling (PMID: 33116834)
summary: The antisense lncRNA FBXL19-AS1 is upregulated in cervical cancer. It sponges miR-193a-5p to raise PIN1 expression, and its knockdown reduces proliferation, migration and invasion and induces apoptosis. This concerns the antisense lncRNA rather than the FBXL19 protein.

citation: LIN28A-stabilized FBXL19-AS1 promotes breast cancer migration, invasion and EMT by regulating WDR66 (PMID: 31140103)
summary: FBXL19-AS1 interacts with and is stabilized by the RNA-binding protein LIN28A (RIP assay) and promotes WDR66 expression, driving breast cancer migration, invasion and EMT.

citation: Analysis of associations of FBXL19-AS1 with occurrence, development and prognosis of acute pancreatitis (PMID: 33378025)
summary: Serum FBXL19-AS1 is elevated in severe acute pancreatitis and predicts severity (AUC 0.9177). Overexpression upregulated IL-1β, TNF-α and IL-6 mRNA in AP cells, and knockdown had the opposite effect.

citation: Whole-exome sequencing in individuals with obsessive-compulsive disorder and chronic tic disorders identifies 36 large-effect risk genes (PMID: 42680906)
variant_detail: Not specified in the abstract. BRWD1 is reported as a high-confidence risk gene (FDR < 0.1) on the basis of an excess of de novo and rare protein-damaging variants in cases.
phenotype: obsessive-compulsive disorder; chronic tic disorders
diagnostic_reason: Gene-level statistical evidence: excess of de novo and rare protein-damaging variants in cases (FDR < 0.1). BRWD1 also overlaps an OCD GWAS locus. No per-patient variant data are given in the abstract.

citation: Mouse BRWD1 is critical for spermatid postmeiotic transcription and female meiotic chromosome stability (PMID: 25547156)
phenotype: Male and female infertility; Down-regulation of ~300 mostly spermatid-specific transcripts in testis; Near-complete loss of protamine and transition protein transcripts; No global epigenetic chromatin changes in testis; Oocytes: severe chromosome condensation and structural defects; Oocytes: abnormal telomere structure; Oocytes: >2-fold overexpression of MLL5 and LINE-1 elements at the germinal vesicle stage; Failure to complete oogenesis and spermatogenesis

citation: Rescue of deficits by Brwd1 copy number restoration in the Ts65Dn mouse model of Down syndrome (PMID: 36289231)
phenotype: Brwd1 upregulated in the brain of trisomic mice; Selective restoration of Brwd1 to two copies (removal of the extra copy) in Ts65Dn mice rescued hippocampal LTP deficits; Rescued cognitive deficits; Rescued gene expression changes; Rescued aberrant BAF complex localization, chromatin accessibility and gene expression

citation: BRWD1 orchestrates epigenetic landscape of late B lymphopoiesis (PMID: 30250168)
phenotype: Brwd1-/- small pre-B cells: altered enhancer accessibility, with early development enhancers not closed and late B lymphopoiesis enhancers not opened; Dysregulation of >7000 genes, with failure to repress proliferative programs and to induce differentiation programs; Expression of B-cell TFs unaffected; Transcriptional and enhancer profiles resemble those of human patients with BRWD1 mutations (hypogammaglobulinemia); Block in late B-cell development

citation: BRWD1 directs B cell epigenetic states required for germinal center initiation, maintenance and function (PMID: 42864370)
phenotype: Cd23Cre;Brwd1fl/fl: diminished germinal center B cell responses and class switch recombination after immunization; AicdaCre;Brwd1fl/fl: increased GC B cell proliferation; AicdaCre;Brwd1fl/fl: defective affinity maturation and tolerance; Somatic hypermutation and memory/plasma cell differentiation intact; Altered transcriptional and epigenetic identities of LZ, DZp and DZd GC states

citation: Mouse BRWD1 is critical for spermatid postmeiotic transcription and female meiotic chromosome stability (PMID: 25547156)
summary: Brwd1 knockout mice show down-regulation of ~300 mostly spermatid-specific transcripts in testis, including near-complete loss of protamine and transition protein transcripts, without global chromatin changes. In oocytes, Brwd1 loss causes chromosome condensation and structural defects, abnormal telomeres, and >2-fold overexpression of MLL5 and LINE-1 elements. BRWD1 is essential for fertility in both sexes.

citation: Histone reader BRWD1 targets and restricts recombination to the Igk locus (PMID: 26301565)
summary: Downregulation of IL-7 receptor signaling in small pre-B cells induces BRWD1 expression. BRWD1 is recruited to the Igk epigenetic landscape set by pre-BCR-dependent Erk activation. It enhances RAG recruitment, gene accessibility and nucleosome positioning 5' of each Jκ recombination signal sequence, which targets recombination to Igk.

citation: BRWD1 orchestrates epigenetic landscape of late B lymphopoiesis (PMID: 30250168)
summary: In small pre-B cells BRWD1 closes early-development enhancers and opens late B-lymphopoiesis enhancers to TF binding. It regulates >7000 genes, repressing proliferative programs and inducing differentiation programs, without regulating the expression of the TFs themselves. Hypogammaglobulinemia patients with BRWD1 mutations show B-cell transcriptional and enhancer profiles similar to those of Brwd1-/- mice.

citation: BRWD1 orchestrates small pre-B cell chromatin topology by converting static to dynamic cohesin (PMID: 37985858)
summary: BRWD1 converts chromatin-bound static cohesin into dynamic cohesin that can mediate long-range looping. This switches poised to active enhancer-promoter interactions and coordinates Igk locus contraction. ATP depletion showed cohesin conversion to be the main energetic mechanism behind dynamic looping.

citation: Rescue of deficits by Brwd1 copy number restoration in the Ts65Dn mouse model of Down syndrome (PMID: 36289231)
summary: BRWD1 (HSA21-encoded) is upregulated in Down syndrome iPSC-derived neurons and trisomic mouse brain. It binds the BAF chromatin remodeling complex tightly, and increased Brwd1 causes BAF genomic mistargeting. Restoring Brwd1 to normal copy number in Ts65Dn mice rescued hippocampal LTP, cognition, BAF localization, chromatin accessibility and gene expression.

citation: BRWD1 establishes epigenetic states for germinal center initiation, maintenance, and function (PMID: 38712068)
summary: Brwd1 loss in follicular B cells inhibits GC initiation and class switch recombination. In GC B cells it causes admixing of chromatin accessibility across GC subsets, induction of inflammatory pathways, and defects in proliferation, affinity maturation and tolerance.

citation: The dual bromodomain and WD repeat-containing mouse protein BRWD1 is required for normal spermiogenesis and the oocyte-embryo transition (PMID: 18353305)
summary: The ENU-induced repro5 mutation, mapped to Brwd1, causes infertility in both sexes. Males show defective spermiogenesis with oligoasthenoteratospermia. Mutant oocytes have maturation defects, with reduced progression to MII and arrest before or at the two-pronuclei stage after IVF. Brwd1 is broadly expressed and is believed to act through the Brg1-dependent SWI/SNF pathway.

citation: ASHG 2011 - Analysis of transcriptional profiles in schizophrenia (Duan et al.)
summary: In LCL expression profiling, BRWD1 was one of eight transcripts differentially expressed by schizophrenia status that survived Bonferroni correction. It is brain-expressed and has a proposed function in neurotransmitter or intercellular communication.

citation: Excess of rare variants in genes that are key epigenetic regulators of spermatogenesis in the patients with non-obstructive azoospermia (PMID: 25739334)
summary: Targeted sequencing found an excess of rare non-silent variants in epigenetic regulators of spermatogenesis, including BRWD1, in non-obstructive azoospermia patients. The burden was 22.5% carrier frequency in patients versus 13.7% in controls.

citation: MALAT1 promotes cisplatin resistance in cervical cancer by activating the PI3K/AKT pathway (PMID: 30536307)
summary: MALAT1 overexpression up-regulated BRWD1 mRNA in HeLa and C-33A cervical cancer cells. BRWD1 knockdown increased cisplatin sensitivity by reducing proliferation and promoting apoptosis and cleaved caspase-3. This links BRWD1 to cisplatin resistance via the MALAT1/PI3K-AKT axis.

citation: Molecular characterization of centerin, a germinal centre cell serpin (PMID: 17447896)
summary: Recombinant bacterial centerin (SERPINA9/GCET1) undergoes the stressed-to-relaxed conformational change required for protease inhibition. It rapidly inhibits trypsin (ka=1.9x10^5 M-1 s-1) and weakly inhibits thrombin and plasmin. It also binds DNA and heparin, although these interactions did not change the inhibition rate. This suggests it acts in germinal centres as an inhibitor of a trypsin-like protease.

citation: Expression of the serpin centerin defines a germinal center phenotype in B-cell lymphomas (PMID: 18550480)
sample_size: 30 DLBCL cases plus follicular lymphomas and normal tissues
summary: A monoclonal antibody showed centerin protein in Burkitt lymphoma Raji cells and in germinal center B cells of tonsil, lymph node and GI lymphoid tissue. It was strongly expressed in most follicular lymphomas, and 47% (14/30) of DLBCLs were positive, correlating most closely with CD10.

citation: Oligonucleotide-based analysis of differentially expressed genes in hippocampus of transgenic mice expressing NSE-controlled APPsw (PMID: 16933151)
sample_size: 12-month-old APPsw transgenic vs control mice; 116 DEGs total
summary: Serpina9 was up-regulated in the hippocampus of 12-month-old APPsw-transgenic AD model mice. Microarray results were confirmed by RT-PCR, suggesting a link to AD neuropathology.

citation: Genome-Wide Analyses Suggest Mechanisms Involving Early B-Cell Development in Canine IgA Deficiency (PMID: 26225558)
sample_size: GWAS in four dog breeds (German shepherd, Golden retriever, Labrador retriever, Shar-Pei)
summary: In German shepherds, a genome-wide significant locus for IgA levels contained SERPINA9 (with KIRREL3) as a candidate gene. SERPINA9 expression is restricted to B cells and peaks when B cells proliferate into plasma cells.

citation: Molecular subtyping of CD5+ diffuse large B-cell lymphoma based on DNA-targeted sequencing and Lymph2Cx (PMID: 36081566)
summary: High SERPINA9 mRNA expression correlated with better overall survival in CD5+ DLBCL, and was an independent prognostic predictor together with MME.

citation: Tumor gene expression signatures associated with outcome in large B-cell lymphoma treated with CD19-directed CAR T-cell therapy (axicabtagene ciloleucel) (PMID: 40083872)
summary: SERPINA9 is one of 17 genes in a tumor expression signature (17-GES) associated with progression after axi-cel therapy in LBCL (HR 6.12 for EFS). The signature was elevated at progression.

citation: Potential biomarkers screening to predict side effects of dexamethasone in different cancers (PMID: 32048780)
sample_size: GEO lymphoma datasets; 180 DEGs in lymphoma
summary: SERPINA9 was among the dexamethasone-specific differentially expressed genes in lymphoma cell samples, indicating that its expression responds to dexamethasone treatment in lymphoma cells.

citation: Genomic analysis reveals molecular characterization of CD30(+) and CD30(-) extranodal natural killer/T-cell lymphomas (ENKTLs) (PMID: 39187207)
sample_size: 10 paired CD30+ and CD30- ENKTL samples
summary: Whole exome sequencing identified somatic SERPINA9 mutations shared between CD30+ and CD30- ENKTL samples.

citation: Identification of Prognostic Genes Relevant With the Nuclear Factors of Activated T Cells Based on Transcriptomics in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma (PMID: 42471772)
summary: SERPINA9 was identified as one of seven NFAT-related prognostic genes in OSCC (with ALB, PDK4, SERPINA5, SPINK6, CGNL1 and IL17F) and was used in a risk model predicting survival. RT-qPCR validation showed significant changes for ALB, PDK4, SERPINA5, CGNL1 and IL17F, but SERPINA9 is not listed among them.

citation: Whole-genome sequencing identifies novel genes for autism in Chinese trios (PMID: 39126614)
variant_detail: Not specified in the abstract. ZNF483 was highlighted as a high-confidence ASD risk gene based on de novo/inherited coding variants.
phenotype: Autism spectrum disorder
diagnostic_reason: Gene-level association model with de novo and inherited coding variants in ASD trios; supported by GO enrichment, expression and network analysis. Variant-level details are not given in the abstract.

citation: Genetic Variant Analyses Identify Novel Candidate Autism Risk Genes from a Highly Consanguineous Cohort of 104 Families from Oman (PMID: 39769462)
variant_detail: NM_133464.5 c.2047C>T, p.R683* (homozygous in the table; novel)
phenotype: Autism spectrum disorder
diagnostic_reason: Nonsense variant classified Pathogenic, novel, in a candidate ASD gene. It is homozygous, not heterozygous, so it does not strictly meet the heterozygous criterion.

citation: A novel familial 9q31.2q32 microdeletion: Muscle cramping, somnolence, fatigue, sensorineural hearing loss, pubertal delay, and short stature (PMID: 30847195)
variant_detail: Heterozygous 9q31.2q32 microdeletion, chr9:109195179-113974353 (hg18), encompassing ZNF483 (a multi-gene deletion)
phenotype: Fatigue; Muscle cramps; Somnolence; Short stature; Delayed puberty (small testes, low testosterone, required testosterone induction); Sensorineural hearing loss; Mild developmental delay
diagnostic_reason: Familial microdeletion with a suggested critical region; ZNF483 was discussed as a candidate for the pubertal delay phenotype.

citation: Hong et al. 2017 - TRIM28 and Interacting KRAB-ZNFs Control Self-Renewal of Human Pluripotent Stem Cells through Epigenetic Repression of Pro-differentiation Genes (PMID: 29198826)
summary: ZNF483 was identified from expression datasets as one of three KRAB-ZNFs (with ZNF114 and ZNF589) that maintain pluripotency in human PSCs. These KRAB-ZNFs act with TRIM28 to repress differentiation genes by altering H3K9me3 and DNA methylation at their promoters.

citation: Zinc finger protein 483 (ZNF483) regulates neuronal differentiation and methyl-CpG-binding protein 2 (MeCP2) intracellular localization (PMID: 34192606)
summary: CRISPR-Cas9 ZNF483-knockout P19 cells showed decreased proliferation, altered aggregate formation, reduced NeuN expression and altered MeCP2 phosphorylation. ZNF483 overexpression enhanced cytosolic MeCP2 localization. ZNF483 may promote neuronal differentiation by regulating MeCP2 subcellular localization.

citation: Zinc finger protein 483 (ZNF483) regulates neuronal differentiation and methyl-CpG-binding protein 2 (MeCP2) intracellular localization (PMID: 34192606)
summary: ZNF483 was characterized as a MeCP2-binding protein, one of nine MeCP2-binding candidates proposed from the cerebral cortex. Phylogenetic profiling showed ZNF483 is broadly conserved in metazoans, whereas MeCP2 arose in chordates.

citation: Whole-genome sequencing identifies novel genes for autism in Chinese trios (PMID: 39126614)
sample_size: 112 ASD patients and their parents (334 individuals)
summary: WGS of ASD trios highlighted ZNF483 as a high-confidence candidate autism risk gene. Support came from de novo and inherited coding variants, association modeling, and GO enrichment, expression and network analyses.

citation: Kentistou et al. 2024 - Understanding the genetic complexity of puberty timing across the allele frequency spectrum (PMID: 38951643)
summary: Exome analysis found rare loss-of-function variants in ZNF483 associated with age at menarche. These variants abolished the impact of polygenic risk on pubertal timing.

citation: Understanding the genetic complexity of puberty timing across the allele frequency spectrum (PMID: 37503126)
summary: The preprint reports the same finding: rare LoF variants in ZNF483 from exome sequencing of ~220,000 women affect pubertal timing and abolish the polygenic risk effect.

citation: ASHG 2023 - Understanding the genetic complexity of puberty timing across the allele frequency spectrum
summary: Exome sequence analysis identified rare loss-of-function variants in ZNF483 associated with age at menarche. These variants abolished the impact of polygenic risk.

citation: Gene transcripts expressed in equine white blood cells are potential biomarkers of extracorporeal shock wave therapy (PMID: 34008346)
summary: ZNF483 transcript in horse white blood cells was significantly down-regulated at various time points after extracorporeal shock wave therapy, by qPCR and microarray. It is a candidate biomarker of ESWT.

citation: Transcriptome Profiling of Prostate Cancer, Considering Risk Groups and the TMPRSS2-ERG Molecular Subtype (PMID: 37298233)
sample_size: 58 localized and 43 locally advanced PCa samples
summary: ZNF483 was among the genes with the highest predictive potential in RNA-seq profiling of high-risk prostate cancer, including the TMPRSS2-ERG subtype.

citation: Effect of Heixiaoyao Powder on Hippocampal Gene Expression Profile of Alzheimer's Disease Rats (PMID: 30641629)
summary: Znf483 mRNA increased in the hippocampus of the Aβ-induced AD rat model. It decreased after Heixiaoyao Powder or Western medicine treatment, and the authors suggest HP acts partly by regulating znf483, zfp37 and zic4.

citation: Systematic Ocular Phenotyping of Knockout Mouse Lines Identifies Genes Associated With Age-Related Corneal Dystrophies (PMID: 40323269)
phenotype: Abnormal cornea morphology in late-adult mice (49+ weeks); Identified from IMPC data as one of 14 genes linked to late-adult corneal phenotypes (Ik, KMPC center); Ik expressed in human cornea T/NK cells (66.67%) by single-cell transcriptomics

citation: Unknown authors 2021 - Inactivating Mutations of the IK Gene Weaken Ku80/Ku70-Mediated DNA Repair and Sensitize Endometrial Cancer to Chemotherapy (PMID: 34065218)
summary: Co-IP and mass spectrometry identified an IK interaction with Ku80, linking IK to Ku80/Ku70-mediated DNA repair. IK knockdown in endometrial cancer cells caused G2/M enrichment, inactivated Ku80/Ku70 DNA repair signaling, and sensitized cells to cisplatin. IK is described as a mitotic factor promoting cell cycle progression.

citation: Unknown authors 2021 - Inactivating Mutations of the IK Gene Weaken Ku80/Ku70-Mediated DNA Repair and Sensitize Endometrial Cancer to Chemotherapy (PMID: 34065218)
significance: Reported as significantly better overall survival; no specific p-value in abstract
summary: Somatic IK-inactivating mutations (mostly frameshift and stop-gain) were associated with decreased IK expression. They were also linked to higher mutation burden, better chemotherapy response, and longer 10-year survival in endometrial cancer. Co-occurring IK/Ku80 mutations were associated with significantly better overall survival.

citation: Unknown authors 1997 - Implication of a new molecule IK in CD34+ hematopoietic progenitor cell proliferation and differentiation (PMID: 9160666)
summary: IK transcripts are present in CD34+ cells from human umbilical cord blood. IK expression rose during growth factor-induced proliferation and differentiation, inversely correlating with the loss of HLA-DR.

citation: Unknown authors 1997 - Implication of a new molecule IK in CD34+ hematopoietic progenitor cell proliferation and differentiation (PMID: 9160666)
summary: An antisense oligonucleotide against the IK mRNA initiation site decreased IK transcripts and increased HLA-DR expression. It also inhibited colony formation by multilineage, early erythroid and granulomonocytic CD34+ progenitors, reducing mean colony size by 70%. This supports a role for IK in growth factor-dependent proliferation and differentiation, via modulation of HLA-DR.

citation: Unknown authors 1994 - A new cytokine (IK) down-regulating HLA class II: monoclonal antibodies, cloning and chromosome localization (PMID: 7970704)
summary: IK was purified as a 19 kDa cytokine secreted by K562 leukemic cells and other cancer cells. It inhibits IFN-gamma-induced HLA class II expression, and also cycloheximide-induced HLA-DR, in Colo 205 colon carcinoma cells. Blocking mAbs antagonized this effect.

citation: Unknown authors 1994 - A new cytokine (IK) down-regulating HLA class II: monoclonal antibodies, cloning and chromosome localization (PMID: 7970704)
summary: The IK cDNA was cloned and sequenced. It detects a 2.1 kb mRNA in various cell types, has no homology to known cytokines, and maps to chromosome 2p15-p14. Transient transfection in COS cells produced a secreted, biologically active 19 kDa protein recognized by the blocking mAb 1C5B11.

citation: De Novo Variants in PPFIA2 in Individuals With Neurodevelopmental Disorders (PMID: 41044885)
variant_detail: Heterozygous de novo variants in PPFIA2 (individual variant notations not given in the abstract); two index individuals identified by exome/genome sequencing plus seven additional individuals from large cohorts
phenotype: neurodevelopmental disorder; overlapping phenotype across individuals (details not given in abstract)
diagnostic_reason: De novo occurrence, rare variants, gnomAD gene constraint metrics, and overlapping phenotypes among 9 individuals

citation: SNP array screening of cryptic genomic imbalances in 450 Japanese subjects with intellectual disability and multiple congenital anomalies previously negative for large rearrangements (PMID: 26740234)
variant_detail: Pathogenic CNV involving PPFIA2 (exact coordinates and copy-number state not given in the abstract)
phenotype: intellectual disability; multiple congenital anomalies
diagnostic_reason: Small CNV affecting PPFIA2 identified by SNP array; PPFIA2 proposed as a novel candidate gene for ID

citation: De Novo Variants Predominate in Autism Spectrum Disorder (PMID: 41010044)
phenotype: autism spectrum disorder
diagnostic_reason: De novo missense variant on trio-WGS, absent from gnomAD, predicted deleterious (scores 0.935 D and 0.998 D, conservation 100), classified as a Principal Diagnostic Variant

citation: Liprin alfa 2 gene expression is increased by cannabis use and associated with neuropsychological function (PMID: 30879928)
significance: Intelligence correlation B=-22.9, p=0.002 (all); B=-28.5, p=0.037 (non-users)
summary: Whole-blood PPFIA2 mRNA was higher in heavy cannabis users than in non-users (logFC 0.17), confirmed by qPCR. Expression correlated negatively with estimated intelligence, including in non-users. CBD increased PPFIA2 expression in monocytes, but THC in monocytes and THC or CBD in neuroblastoma cells did not.

citation: Prognostic Significance of PPFIA2 in Localized Prostate Cancer: Integrative Analysis and Functional Validation (PMID: 41617436)
sample_size: Multiple cohorts (TCGA-PRAD, CPC, Stockholm, GSE54460) plus an in-house IHC cohort
significance: Associated with earlier BCR across cohorts (specific p-values not given in abstract)
summary: PPFIA2 knockdown in LNCaP and C4-2 prostate cancer cells reduced proliferation and migration. High PPFIA2 expression, confirmed at the protein level by IHC, predicted earlier biochemical recurrence. GSEA linked PPFIA2 to activation of proliferation pathways and suppression of protein synthesis, and high expression was associated with a lower SPOP mutation frequency.

citation: Association mapping of the high-grade myopia MYP3 locus reveals novel candidates UHRF1BP1L, PTPRR, and PPFIA2 (PMID: 23422819)
summary: An intronic PPFIA2 SNP (rs17306116) was associated with high-grade myopia at the MYP3 locus. PPFIA2 was also differentially expressed in fetal versus adult ocular tissue (confirmed by RT-qPCR). Replication in an independent cohort approached significance.

citation: Extreme downregulation of chromosome Y and Alzheimer's disease in men (PMID: 32147245)
sample_size: 371 undiseased brains; AD case-control cohorts of 556 cases and 462 controls
summary: Extreme downregulation of chromosome Y in brain was associated with rs114241159 within ACSS3/PPFIA2, a region previously linked to amyloid beta concentrations. This suggests a link between the PPFIA2 locus and a male-specific Alzheimer's pathway.

citation: SNP array screening of cryptic genomic imbalances in 450 Japanese subjects with intellectual disability and multiple congenital anomalies (PMID: 26740234)
summary: A pathogenic CNV affecting PPFIA2 was found in a subject with ID/MCA, identifying PPFIA2 as a novel candidate gene for intellectual disability.

citation: Lactate treatment improves brain biochemistry and cognitive function in transgenic Alzheimer's and wild-type mice (PMID: 41981183)
summary: In 5XFAD Alzheimer's mice, chronic lactate treatment increased PPFIA2 protein, one of several synaptic integrity proteins (with OPCML, STXBP3, SYT1, VGLUT2 and VSNL1), in a sex-dependent manner. This links PPFIA2 to synaptic integrity and cognitive resilience.

citation: Visium spatial transcriptomics reveals intratumor heterogeneity and profiles of Gleason score progression in prostate cancer (PMID: 38077153)
summary: PPFIA2 was among the differentially expressed genes (with NANS, PABPC1L, PILRB and SESN3) associated with Gleason score upgrading in spatial transcriptomics of glandular epithelial cells from prostate cancer tissue.

citation: Identification of a Candidate Gene Panel for the Early Diagnosis of Prostate Cancer (PMID: 25788493)
summary: PPFIA2 was one of eight prostate cancer biomarkers validated by qPCR in tissue and urinary sediments. It was not part of the best-performing three-gene urinary panel (HOXC6, TDRD1, DLX1).

citation: ASHG 2017 - Whole exome sequencing reveals candidate variants for elevated intraocular pressure in the Beaver Dam Eye Study
sample_size: 135 exomes (30 cases, 11 controls); 936 samples for validation genotyping
summary: A splicing variant in PPFIA2 (12:81671194) was uniquely seen in 7 of 30 unrelated high-IOP individuals and in 1 high-IOP relative, but not in controls. It is proposed as a candidate for elevated intraocular pressure.

citation: ASHG 2009 - Identifying the Genetic Underpinnings Associated With Healthspan
summary: In a pilot GWAS of healthy aging ('wellderly', age ≥80) versus young controls, the top association was rs10746192 in an intron of PPFIA2, a protein tyrosine phosphatase.

citation: Zhang et al. 2015 - Increased co-expression of genes harboring the damaging de novo mutations in Chinese schizophrenic patients during prenatal development (PMID: 26666178)
variant_detail: De novo missense variant in PPP6R3 (chr11:68370926, G/C); protein change not given in the available passage
phenotype: schizophrenia
diagnostic_reason: De novo variant identified by trio exome sequencing and predicted damaging by multiple in silico tools. PPP6R3 was not among the four genes prioritized by the authors (LRP1, MACF1, DICER1, ABCA2), so the evidence for pathogenicity is weak.

citation: PPP6R3-mediated dephosphorylation regulates mRNA translation during spermatogonial differentiation (PMID: 40721635)
phenotype: Germline-specific deletion of Ppp6r3 causes abnormal spermatogonial differentiation; Male infertility; Translation inhibition in KIT+ spermatogonia; Increased phosphorylation of EIF3C (S39) and EIF4G1 (S1217) with enhanced protein degradation; Reduced non-phosphorylated EIF3C and EIF4G1 and reduced enrichment of differentiation-associated mRNAs; Phosphosite-mutant EIF3C S39A and EIF4G1 S1217A overexpression in Ppp6r3-cKO spermatogonial progenitor cells rescued differentiation potential

citation: Role of ppp6r3 in zebrafish gonadal differentiation and gametogenesis (PMID: 40962474)
phenotype: Two CRISPR/Cas9 ppp6r3 mutant lines generated; Mutants develop only as males (sex-biased development); Mutant males cannot fertilize wild-type eggs; Spermatogenesis disrupted with block in transition from spermatocytes to mature sperm in testes; Defects in gonadal differentiation and gametogenesis

citation: Removal of developmentally regulated microexons has a minimal impact on larval zebrafish brain morphology and function (PMID: 41252186)
phenotype: ppp6r3 microexon deletion mutant had mild neural phenotypes at larval stage (brain activity/morphology/behavior); Most of the 45 microexon mutants had minimal or no phenotypes
knockout_type: other (CRISPR/Cas9 microexon deletion; partial loss of a microexon in ppp6r3)

citation: SAPS3 subunit of protein phosphatase 6 is an AMPK inhibitor and controls metabolic homeostasis upon dietary challenge in male mice (PMID: 36914647)
phenotype: Whole-body or liver-specific Saps3 (Ppp6r3) deletion protects male mice from high-fat-diet-induced metabolic detriments; AMPK activation, improved glucose homeostasis and insulin sensitivity under HFD; Reversal of HFD-induced metabolic and transcriptional alterations; No effect of SAPS3 loss under balanced (normal) diet; Genetic inhibition of AMPK blocked the protective phenotype in knockout mice
knockout_type: full knockout and liver-specific conditional knockout

citation: Recent Advances in Experimental Functional Characterization of GWAS Candidate Genes in Osteoporosis (PMID: 40806370)
phenotype: Review notes that Ppp6r3 deletion in mice decreased bone mineral density (BMD)

citation: Zhang et al. 2024 - The protein phosphatase PP6 promotes RIPK1-dependent PANoptosis (PMID: 38807188)
summary: A cell death-based CRISPR screen identified PP6 holoenzyme components as regulators of TAK1 inhibitor-induced PANoptosis. PPP6R3 acts redundantly with PPP6R1 and PPP6R2, and their combined depletion was needed to block cell death. PP6 promoted the pro-death RIPK1 S166 autophosphorylation and reduced the pro-survival S321 phosphorylation.

citation: Transcriptome-wide association study and eQTL colocalization identify potentially causal genes responsible for human bone mineral density GWAS associations (PMID: 36416764)
significance: TWAS and colocalization significant (512 genes overall)
summary: TWAS and eQTL colocalization using GTEx gave PPP6R3 the strongest support among 512 genes for the BMD GWAS, and it had not previously been implicated in BMD. Ppp6r3 deletion in mice decreased BMD, supporting it as a causal BMD gene.

citation: Role of ppp6r3 in zebrafish gonadal differentiation and gametogenesis (PMID: 40962474)
summary: CRISPR/Cas9 ppp6r3 mutant zebrafish lines developed only as males and could not fertilize wild-type eggs. In mutant testes, the transition from spermatocytes to mature sperm was blocked, disrupting spermatogenesis. Ppp6r3 is therefore needed for gonadal differentiation, sex determination and gametogenesis.

citation: Interactome analysis of the influenza A virus transcription/replication machinery identifies protein phosphatase 6 as a cellular factor required for efficient virus replication (PMID: 25187537)
summary: Affinity purification mass spectrometry of the influenza polymerase (Strep-tagged PB2) in infected human cells co-purified PPP6R3 with PPP6C and PPP6R1. PP6 interacted directly with PB1 and PB2, and PPP6C knockdown reduced viral RNA accumulation and virus growth.

citation: Meta-Analysis of Genomewide Association Studies Reveals Genetic Variants for Hip Bone Geometry (PMID: 30888730)
sample_size: up to 18,719 discovery individuals plus 7 replication cohorts
significance: GWS p≤2.6×10-8; fracture p=7.5×10-5; eQTL p=0.0007
summary: Genome-wide significant hip geometry association at 11q13 near LRP5 and PPP6R3 (rs7102273). The SNP was also associated with fracture, and a bone transcriptome eQTL linked rs7102273 to PPP6R3 expression.

citation: Bivariate genome-wide association meta-analysis of pediatric musculoskeletal traits reveals pleiotropic effects at the SREBF1/TOM1L2 locus (PMID: 28743860)
summary: The PPP6R3/LRP5 locus was among eight loci with pleiotropic effects on lean mass and BMD in a bivariate GWAS of children.

citation: ASHG 2012 - The PPP6R3/LRP5 locus influences lean mass in children of different ethnic background and highlights pleiotropic effects on muscle-bone interactions
significance: lean mass P=2.9×10-8; bivariate P=4.8×10-8; BMD P=7.6×10-5
summary: A SNP in the PPP6R3/LRP5 locus was associated with lean mass in children and nominally with BMD. The abstract describes PPP6R3 as a gene of unknown function that is ubiquitously expressed across tissues, including bone and muscle. LD at the locus makes it hard to tell which gene drives the signal.

citation: Causal genes for osteoporosis: Mendelian randomization analysis with multilayer xQTL data (PMID: 42260878)
significance: passed multiple-testing correction and HEIDI filtering
summary: SMR integrating FinnGen osteoporosis GWAS with expression, splicing, methylation and protein QTLs identified PPP6R3 as one of 15 high-confidence causal genes. It passed HEIDI filtering.

citation: NRG1 fusions in breast cancer (PMID: 33413557)
sample_size: 571 breast cancers analyzed, plus the MDA-MB-175 cell line
summary: The MDA-MB-175 fusion originally reported as TENM4-NRG1 is actually a double fusion, PPP6R3-TENM4-NRG1, producing multiple transcripts, some of which include the NRG1 cytoplasmic tail.

citation: PPP6R3-USP6 amplification: Novel oncogenic mechanism in malignant nodular fasciitis (PMID: 27113271)
summary: A PPP6R3-USP6 gene fusion was amplified in a malignant nodular fasciitis case with metastasis, and it upregulated USP6 mRNA transcription. This is consistent with PPP6R3 promoter-driven USP6 activation.

citation: Transcription factor protein interactomes reveal genetic determinants in heart disease (PMID: 35182466)
variant_detail: GLYR1 de novo missense variant (exact nucleotide/protein change not given in abstract); disrupts interaction with GATA4
phenotype: Congenital heart disease
diagnostic_reason: De novo missense variant in a CHD proband identified from ~9,000 proband-parent trio exomes. The gene was prioritized by residue, gene, and proband-level scoring within the GATA4/TBX5 interactomes. The variant disrupted GATA4 interaction and impaired function in vitro and in mice.

citation: Primary complex motor stereotypies are associated with de novo damaging DNA coding mutations that identify KDM5B as a risk gene (PMID: 37788244)
variant_detail: GLYR1 de novo damaging variant (exact change not given in the provided text); listed among 52 genes with de novo damaging variants in pCMS probands
phenotype: Primary complex motor stereotypies
diagnostic_reason: De novo predicted-damaging coding variant identified by whole-exome sequencing of pCMS parent-child trios. GLYR1 is only listed in a table of genes with such variants and is not a high-confidence risk gene.

citation: Deficiency of nucleosome-destabilizing factor GLYR1 dampens spermatogenesis in mice (PMID: 38395189)
phenotype: Subfertility in males with Glyr1 depleted in spermatogenic cells; Reduced sperm count; Reduced sperm motility; Increased rate of sperm malformation, mainly head and neck defects in cauda epididymal spermatozoa; Fewer spermatocytes across different meiotic stages; Reduced histone acetylation in spermatogenic cells

citation: Uniparental Disomy Reveals Hidden Genetic Causes of Congenital Heart Disease (PMID: 42539127)
phenotype: Patient-specific cardiac phenotypes recapitulated in zebrafish functional studies of GLYR1, PIEZO1 and MESD (specific GLYR1 zebrafish phenotypes not detailed in the abstract); Homozygous pathogenic GLYR1 variant found within a UPD region in a CHD patient

citation: Transcription factor protein interactomes reveal genetic determinants in heart disease (PMID: 35182466)
significance: Enrichment of de novo missense variants in interactomes (significance not given in the abstract)
summary: GLYR1 was identified in the GATA4/TBX5 interactomes of human cardiac progenitors and prioritized as a likely CHD gene. GLYR1 and GATA4 co-occupy and co-activate cardiac developmental genes. A CHD-associated GLYR1 missense variant disrupted its interaction with GATA4 and impaired function in vitro and in mice.

citation: Deficiency of nucleosome-destabilizing factor GLYR1 dampens spermatogenesis in mice (PMID: 38395189)
significance: Reported as significant increase in malformation rate (no values in the abstract)
summary: Glyr1 is widely expressed in mouse testicular cells. Its depletion in spermatogenic cells caused subfertility, reduced sperm count and motility, and increased head and neck malformations. It also reduced spermatocytes across meiotic stages and lowered histone acetylation.

citation: Downregulation of GLYR1 contributes to microsatellite instability colorectal cancer by targeting p21 via the p38MAPK and PI3K/AKT pathways (PMID: 32370786)
significance: Reported as significant downregulation (no values in the abstract)
summary: GLYR1 is downregulated in MSI CRC and interacts with MLH1 to regulate its nuclear import and expression. GLYR1 knockdown in SW480 and SW620 cells accelerated G1/S transition, promoted proliferation, inhibited differentiation, and reduced 5-FU sensitivity. It acts through p38MAPK inhibition and PI3K/AKT activation, which lower p21.

citation: Candidate driver genes in microsatellite-unstable colorectal cancer (PMID: 21544814)
significance: Mutation frequency significantly above control repeats
summary: GLYR1 has a frequent coding G8 microsatellite frameshift mutation (51%) in MSI CRC. Tumors with biallelic mutations showed defective GLYR1 protein by immunohistochemistry, supporting a loss-of-function, tumor suppressor-like role.

citation: GLYR1 transcriptionally regulates PER3 expression to promote the proliferation and migration of multiple myeloma (PMID: 38642856)
summary: GLYR1 binds the PER3 promoter (luciferase and ChIP assays) and transcriptionally activates PER3. Through PER3, GLYR1 suppresses the viability and migration of multiple myeloma cells and promotes apoptosis.

citation: GLYR1-mediated downregulation of lncRNA HSD11B1-AS1 promotes proliferation, migration, and invasion of breast cancer cells (PMID: 41217560)
summary: GLYR1 directly binds the HSD11B1-AS1 promoter and represses its transcription, as shown by ChIP and luciferase assays. This enhances proliferation, migration, and invasion of breast cancer cells, and rescue experiments confirmed the axis.

citation: Reader interactome of epigenetic histone marks in birds (PMID: 26703087)
summary: GLYR1 (N-PAC) is a known H3K36me3 reader in mammals. It was reproducibly not enriched at H3K36me3 in chicken and zebra finch peptide pull-down proteomics, suggesting species-specific differences in readers.

citation: Study of a patient with MDS/MPN with co-morbid neutrophilia and a novel NCOR1::GLYR1 fusion gene (PMID: 38565504)
summary: A novel NCOR1::GLYR1 fusion was identified by RNA-seq and validated by qPCR and Sanger sequencing in an MDS/MPN patient who progressed to AML. Fusion transcript levels fell after chemotherapy, so the fusion is considered pathogenic.

citation: Proteomic profiling of the prefrontal cortex reveals Dysregulated Mitochondria-Metabolism-Synapse axis in a chronic Stress-Induced mouse model of depression (PMID: 41765126)
summary: Glyr1 was among the proteins differentially expressed in the prefrontal cortex of chronic social defeat stress mice. It was validated by PRM and Western blot within a signal-transduction module (with Rigi, Pbrm1, Plppr5).

citation: Comparative RNA-seq analysis reveals potential mechanisms mediating the conversion to androgen independence in an LNCaP progression cell model (PMID: 24012641)
summary: A GLYR1-SLC9A8 fusion gene was found specifically in androgen-independent LNCaP-AI-F prostate cancer cells and predicted to be damaging and oncogenic.

citation: A cardiovascular, craniofacial, and neurodevelopmental disorder caused by loss-of-function variants in the eIF3 complex component genes EIF3A and EIF3B (PMID: 41033306)
variant_detail: Loss-of-function variants in EIF3B (individual variants not given in the abstract); 14 individuals with EIF3B variants, which may include microdeletions involving EIF3B
phenotype: congenital cardiac defects; craniofacial dysmorphisms; mild developmental delay; behavioral abnormalities
diagnostic_reason: De novo or loss-of-function variants. Gene highly constrained against LoF. EIF3B lies within the minimal 7p22.3 microdeletion region for cardiac anomalies. Zebrafish eif3ba mutants show thin heart tubes, absent craniofacial cartilage and embryonic lethality.
center_country: International matchmaking collaboration (specific centers not stated in abstract)

citation: A cardiovascular, craniofacial, and neurodevelopmental disorder caused by loss-of-function variants in the eIF3 complex component genes EIF3A and EIF3B (PMID: 41679311)
variant_detail: Not available (no abstract; likely same report as PMID 41033306)
phenotype: cardiac defects; craniofacial dysmorphisms; neurodevelopmental delay
diagnostic_reason: Not stated in the available text. Title indicates loss-of-function variants in EIF3B.

citation: Delineation of a less than 200 kb minimal deleted region for cardiac malformations on chromosome 7p22 (PMID: 21671376)
variant_detail: De novo interstitial deletion of less than 400 kb at 7p22 (CNV). It spans MAD1L1, FTSJ2, NUDT1 and SNX8 and may include upstream regulatory elements of EIF3B; EIF3B itself is not clearly deleted.
phenotype: tetralogy of Fallot; bilateral second branchial arch remnants; mild dysmorphic features
diagnostic_reason: De novo deletion confirmed by array CGH, qPCR and FISH, absent in parents. It defines a minimal deleted region for cardiac malformations. EIF3B involvement is only possible, via regulatory elements.

citation: 7p22.3 microdeletion: a case study of a patient with congenital heart defect, neurodevelopmental delay and epilepsy (PMID: 39152504)
variant_detail: 7p22.3 microdeletion (CNV) in a region including candidate cardiac genes SNX8 and EIF3B (exact coordinates not given in the abstract)
phenotype: congenital heart defect; epilepsy; moderate mental and motor developmental delay; hypotonia; apraxia/dyspraxia
diagnostic_reason: Microdeletion at 7p22.3 overlapping the minimal region for heart malformations. EIF3B and SNX8 are proposed candidate genes, but the evidence is described as controversial.

citation: A cardiovascular, craniofacial, and neurodevelopmental disorder caused by loss-of-function variants in the eIF3 complex component genes EIF3A and EIF3B (PMID: 41033306)
phenotype: developmental abnormalities; thin heart tubes; lack of craniofacial cartilage; embryonic lethality
knockout_type: full knockout (mutations in orthologous eif3s10 [EIF3A] and eif3ba [EIF3B] genes)

citation: PMID 41033306 - A cardiovascular, craniofacial, and neurodevelopmental disorder caused by loss-of-function variants in the eIF3 complex component genes EIF3A and EIF3B (PMID: 41033306)
summary: Fourteen individuals carried de novo or loss-of-function EIF3B variants, and four carried EIF3A variants. They presented with cardiac defects, craniofacial dysmorphism and mild neurodevelopmental delay. EIF3B lies in the 7p22.3 microdeletion cardiac region. Zebrafish eif3ba and eif3s10 mutants had thin heart tubes, absent craniofacial cartilage and embryonic lethality.

citation: PMID 27373335 - eIF3 Peripheral Subunits Rearrangement after mRNA Binding and Start-Codon Recognition (PMID: 27373335)
summary: A cryo-EM structure of the mammalian 48S initiation complex at 5.8 Å shows that eIF3b relocates to the 40S intersubunit face, below the eIF2-Met-tRNAi ternary complex, after mRNA attachment. eIF3b is a peripheral eIF3 subunit, and this rearrangement underlies eIF3 function in mRNA scanning and the timing of subunit joining.

citation: PMID 39247811 - FOXA1-dependent PUS1 regulates EIF3b stability in a non-enzymatic pathway mediating prostate cancer bone metastasis (PMID: 39247811)
summary: PUS1 protects EIF3b from ubiquitin-mediated degradation, independently of its enzymatic activity, in prostate cancer. EIF3b overexpression rescued the loss of metastasis caused by PUS1 knockdown, and FOXA1 drives PUS1 expression by binding its promoter.

citation: PMID 36050601 - EIF3B stabilizes PTGS2 expression by counteracting MDM2-mediated ubiquitination to promote the development and progression of malignant melanoma (PMID: 36050601)
summary: EIF3B is highly expressed in melanoma and correlates with lymphatic metastasis and pathological stage. Its depletion blocked melanoma progression in vitro and in vivo, and its overexpression increased proliferation and migration. EIF3B stabilizes PTGS2 by inhibiting MDM2-mediated ubiquitination, and PTGS2 silencing reversed the effect of EIF3B overexpression.

citation: PMID 33459066 - EIF3B promotes cancer progression in pancreatic cancer (PMID: 33459066)
summary: EIF3B is aberrantly highly expressed in pancreatic cancer and associated with poor prognosis. Knockdown in SW1990 and PANC-1 cells reduced viability and proliferation, caused cell cycle arrest and apoptosis, and suppressed xenograft growth. It also lowered CDH1 and IRS1 and raised DDIT3, PTEN and CDKN1B.

citation: PMID 40576144 - EIF3B-METTL3 complex promotes cell proliferation, invasion and EGFR/AKT signaling in cervical cancer (PMID: 40576144)
summary: EIF3B and METTL3 form a complex, shown by co-immunoprecipitation, in cervical cancer cells (HeLa, SiHa). EIF3B overexpression promoted proliferation and invasion and activated EGFR/AKT signaling. METTL3 knockdown abolished these effects, so the complex rather than EIF3B alone drives the phenotype.

citation: PMID 38247171 - YTHDF2 Is a Therapeutic Target for HCC by Suppressing Immune Evasion and Angiogenesis Through ETV5/PD-L1/VEGFA Axis (PMID: 38247171)
summary: YTHDF2 binds the m6A site in the 5'UTR of ETV5 mRNA and recruits EIF3B to promote ETV5 translation. This drives PD-L1 and VEGFA transcription, immune evasion and angiogenesis in HCC.

citation: PMID 39547463 - New TIPARP inhibitor rescues mitochondrial function and brain injury in ischemic stroke (PMID: 39547463)
summary: EIF3B is a direct target of TIPARP, and the two interact through nucleoplasmic redistribution, leading to mitochondrial dysfunction in ischemic stroke. Tiparp knockdown or inhibition with XG-04-B1 restored mitochondrial homeostasis in mice.

citation: PMID 40592131 - Shared molecular biomarkers and therapeutic targets in rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis: Focus on EIF3B, KHSRP, NCL, PDCD1LG2, and SLC25A37 (PMID: 40592131)
summary: EIF3B is a hub gene differentially expressed in RA and OA synovium (GEO datasets) and shows diagnostic potential (AUC 0.795–0.958). It was downregulated in both RA and OA mouse models versus controls, with higher expression in RA than in OA.

citation: PMID 28360085 - Silencing of translation initiation factor eIF3b promotes apoptosis in osteosarcoma cells (PMID: 28360085)
summary: eIF3b silencing decreased viability and induced apoptosis in U2OS and other osteosarcoma lines, but did not fully suppress growth of normal fibroblasts. Silencing upregulated TNFRSF21, whose overexpression itself induced cell death.

citation: Loss of CTLH component MAEA impairs DNA repair and replication and leads to developmental delay (PMID: 41420108)
variant_detail: Specific variants not given in the abstract; eight patients with MAEA variants (the companion paper lists R34C, E349G, Y394D, M396R as disease-linked variants)
phenotype: neurodevelopmental disorder (DIADEM); developmental delay; intellectual disability; defective HR-dependent DNA repair and replication fork restart/protection in patient-derived cells
diagnostic_reason: Patient-derived cell lines and mutation modeling show defective HR-dependent DNA repair, reduced RAD51 loading, and impaired replication fork restart and protection. The abstract does not state variant type or inheritance, so the missense classification is inferred and uncertain.
