phenotype: microcephaly; craniofacial abnormalities; ocular defects; heart malformations
diagnostic_reason: Functional assays show the disease-linked variants are defective in the replication stress response. The abstract does not give zygosity or inheritance, and the phenotypes are listed for the disorder as a whole rather than per variant.

citation: Maea expressed by macrophages, but not erythroblasts, maintains postnatal murine bone marrow erythroblastic islands (PMID: 30674470)
phenotype: Deletion of Maea in macrophages (Csf1r-Cre or CD169-Cre) severely reduced bone marrow macrophages, erythroblasts and in vivo erythroblastic island formation; Deletion in the erythroid lineage (Epor-Cre) caused no such phenotype, indicating a macrophage-dominant role in BM erythropoiesis; Maea deletion in spleen macrophages did not alter their numbers or functions; Postnatal Maea deletion (Mx1-Cre) impaired BM erythropoiesis; A novel monoclonal antibody inhibiting Maea function also impaired BM erythropoiesis; Background: constitutive Maea-deficient mice die perinatally with anemia and defective erythrocyte enucleation

citation: MAEA is an E3 ubiquitin ligase promoting autophagy and maintenance of haematopoietic stem cells (PMID: 33947846)
phenotype: Maea is highly expressed in HSCs; Maea deletion severely impairs HSC quiescence and lymphoid potential; Maea deletion leads to a lethal myeloproliferative syndrome; Surface expression of cytokine receptors (MPL, FLT3) is stabilised, prolonging intracellular signalling; Autophagy flux is impaired in HSCs but not in mature haematopoietic cells; Receptor kinase inhibitors or autophagy-inducing compounds rescued the functional defects of Maea-deficient HSCs

citation: maea affects head formation through ß-catenin degradation during early Xenopus laevis development (PMID: 36444483)
phenotype: Maea knockdown interfered with head formation in embryos; maea.S overexpression at the anterior dorsal region enlarged head structures; maea.S co-injection reduced expression of the Wnt target genes nodal3.1 and sia1 induced by β-catenin mRNA; Maea.S ubiquitinated β-catenin and decreased its protein levels

citation: CTLH ubiquitin ligase substrates ZMYND19 and MKLN1 negatively regulate mTORC1 at the lysosomal membrane (PMID: 41315365)
summary: A genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 screen in EBV-associated gastric carcinoma cells with alpelisib identified CTLH subunits, including catalytic MAEA, as top synergistic hits. MAEA knockout caused strong accumulation of the CTLH substrates MKLN1 and ZMYND19. These substrates localize to lysosomal outer membranes and block the mTORC1-Rheb interaction, so MAEA-dependent CTLH activity tunes mTORC1.

citation: Maea expressed by macrophages, but not erythroblasts, maintains postnatal murine bone marrow erythroblastic islands (PMID: 30674470)
summary: Conditional Maea knockout mice showed that deleting Maea in macrophages (Csf1r-Cre, CD169-Cre) severely reduced BM macrophages, erythroblasts and island formation. Deletion in the erythroid lineage (Epor-Cre) had no such effect, so Maea is needed in macrophages. Postnatal deletion (Mx1-Cre) or a function-blocking antibody also impaired BM erythropoiesis.

citation: MAEA is an E3 ubiquitin ligase promoting autophagy and maintenance of haematopoietic stem cells (PMID: 33947846)
summary: Maea is highly expressed in HSCs and acts as a membrane-associated E3 ligase subunit. Its deletion in mice impairs HSC quiescence and causes a lethal myeloproliferative syndrome. Loss of Maea stabilizes surface cytokine receptors (MPL, FLT3), prolongs their signalling, and impairs autophagy flux in HSCs. Receptor kinase inhibitors or autophagy inducers rescue the defects.

citation: The E3 ubiquitin ligase MAEA promotes macrophage phagocytosis and inhibits gastrointestinal cancer progression by mediating PARP1 ubiquitination and degradation (PMID: 39990651)
summary: Mass spectrometry and immunoprecipitation showed that MAEA interacts with PARP1 and mediates its K48-linked ubiquitination and degradation. Low MAEA expression correlates with worse survival in gastrointestinal cancer patients. MAEA suppresses tumor proliferation and chemoresistance in vitro and in xenografts, inhibits M2 macrophage polarization, and enhances phagocytosis. Combining MAEA with veliparib improved oxaliplatin efficacy.

citation: E3 ligase MAEA-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of PHD3 promotes glioblastoma progression (PMID: 36882523)
summary: TMT proteomics found MAEA upregulated in recurrent glioma, and high expression correlated with poor prognosis. MAEA targets PHD3 at K159 for K48-linked polyubiquitination and degradation, which stabilizes HIF-1α and raises CD133. This promotes stemness, invasion and TMZ resistance, and MAEA knockdown inhibits xenograft growth.

citation: Pathogenic variants in MAEA disrupt DNA replication fork stability and are associated with developmental abnormalities in humans (PMID: 40880485)
summary: An E3 ligase screen for RAD51 regulators identified MAEA, a core CTLH subunit, as a regulator of homologous recombination. MAEA loss impairs RAD51 recruitment at stalled forks and causes nascent strand degradation. MAEA associates with and ubiquitylates Ku80, enabling its removal and RAD51 loading. Patient variants (R34C, E349G, Y394D, M396R), linked to microcephaly, craniofacial, ocular and heart defects, are defective in the replication stress response.

citation: maea affects head formation through ß-catenin degradation during early Xenopus laevis development (PMID: 36444483)
summary: In Xenopus embryos, maea transcripts are ubiquitously detected early. Maea.S overexpression enlarges head structures and reduces β-catenin-induced Wnt target genes (nodal3.1, sia1). Maea knockdown interferes with head formation. Maea.S ubiquitinates and degrades β-catenin, including the 4KR mutant, so it acts on other lysine residues.

citation: RANBP9 and RANBP10 cooperate in regulating non-small cell lung cancer proliferation (PMID: 40883813)
summary: This paper concerns the CTLH E3 ligase complex, of which MAEA is a member (MAEA is not named in the abstract). RANBP9 or RANBP10 can each independently support CTLH complex formation in NSCLC cells. They reshape the proteome and ubiquitylome and regulate proliferation.

citation: Identification of MAEA protein as a potential target for chemoresistance in osteosarcoma using bioinformatics and proteomic analysis (PMID: 40989695)
summary: Proteomics and MEGENA network analysis identified MAEA as a hub protein in osteosarcoma patients with low chemotherapy-induced necrosis. Immunohistochemistry confirmed higher MAEA expression in OS samples than in healthy controls, suggesting a role in chemoresistance.

citation: ASHG 2011 - Comprehensive evaluation of type 2 diabetes susceptibility in the Japanese population by genome-wide imputation analysis using the 1000 Genomes Project data
sample_size: 4,470 cases/3,071 controls discovery; 1,175 cases/839 controls replication
summary: SNPs in the CTBP1-MAEA region (rs730831, rs4974585, rs4974586) were associated with type 2 diabetes in Japanese cohorts. Conditional analysis identified rs730831 in CTBP1 as the lead SNP, making CTBP1 rather than MAEA the favored candidate gene. The risk allele correlated with higher CTBP1 expression.

citation: De novo non-synonymous TBL1XR1 mutation alters Wnt signaling activity (PMID: 28588275)
variant_detail: chr17:27028608 G>A, p.Asp1716Asn (de novo)
phenotype: sporadic schizophrenia
diagnostic_reason: de novo non-synonymous variant found by trio whole exome sequencing; PolyPhen-2 probably damaging, SIFT damaging, PROVEAN neutral. Not further functionally studied; the paper focused on TBL1XR1.

citation: Genetic alterations in SUPT6H are associated with neurodevelopmental disorders (PMID: 41864309)
phenotype: Homozygous and heterozygous Supt6 null mice show embryonic lethality; Homozygous Supt6 cKOPV mice show motor defects; Homozygous Supt6 cKOPV mice show behavioral seizures; Heterozygous Supt6 cKOPV mice show behavioral phenotypes relevant to neuropsychiatric disorders with normal motor activity; Significant reduction of parvalbumin-expressing neurons in both heterozygous and homozygous cKOPV mice
knockout_type: full knockout (homozygous and heterozygous null) and conditional knockout (parvalbumin-interneuron-specific, cKOPV; homozygous and heterozygous)
significance: Reported as significant reduction in parvalbumin-expressing neurons vs wild-type; no specific p-values given in abstract

citation: SPT6 maintains epidermal homeostasis by inhibiting an NF-κB-positive feedback loop to prevent excessive inflammation (PMID: 41922599)
phenotype: Spontaneous psoriasis-like skin inflammation; Epidermal hyperplasia; Immune cell infiltration; Parakeratosis; Hyperkeratosis; Significantly delayed wound healing with impaired Wnt signaling; Keratinocyte subpopulations with inflammatory signatures, elevated NF-κB signaling and suppressed Wnt signaling (scRNA-seq)
knockout_type: conditional knockout (K14-CreERT; Supt6 fl/fl, basal keratinocyte-specific, inducible)
significance: Delayed wound healing described as significant; no specific p-values in the provided text

citation: Targeted protein degradation reveals a direct role of SPT6 in RNAPII elongation and termination (PMID: 34233157)
summary: Acute targeted degradation of SPT6 (SUPT6H) in human cells showed it is required for RNAPII processivity and productive transcription of protein-coding genes. Acute loss also caused readthrough transcription at thousands of genes, so SPT6 is needed for RNAPII termination. Long-term depletion induced cryptic intragenic transcription, consistent with its role as an epigenetic safeguard.

citation: Genetic alterations in SUPT6H are associated with neurodevelopmental disorders (PMID: 41864309)
sample_size: 18 human SNVs; mouse models (Supt6 null and PV-cKO)
summary: Molecular modeling of 18 published SUPT6H SNVs from developmental disorder patients predicts loss of function. Supt6 null mice (homozygous or heterozygous) show embryonic lethality. Parvalbumin-interneuron conditional KO mice have motor defects, seizures and neuropsychiatric-like behaviors, with fewer parvalbumin neurons.

citation: Identification and analysis of the human and murine putative chromatin structure regulator SUPT6H and Supt6h (PMID: 8786132)
summary: Human SUPT6H and mouse Supt6h were cloned and are homologs of yeast SPT6 and C. elegans emb-5, with over 98% protein identity between human and mouse. The 1603-aa human protein has an acidic N-terminus, a degenerate SH2 domain and a leucine zipper. Northern blotting showed a constitutively expressed 7.0-kb transcript. The gene maps to 17q11.2.

citation: Identification of novel SHPS-1-associated proteins and their roles in regulation of insulin-like growth factor-dependent responses in vascular smooth muscle cells (PMID: 19299420)
summary: SUPT6H is one of four SH2-domain proteins (with SHP-2, CTK, STAT1) that bind directly to the cytoplasmic domain of SHPS-1. It acts as a scaffold linking further binding partners to SHPS-1 in the IGF-I-regulated signaling complex in vascular smooth muscle cells.

citation: MiR-423-5p Inhibition Exerts Protective Effects on Angiotensin II-Induced Cardiomyocyte Hypertrophy (PMID: 36517015)
summary: SUPT6H is a direct target of miR-423-5p, shown by luciferase reporter assay. SUPT6H knockdown worsened Ang II-induced hypertrophy and oxidative stress in human cardiomyocytes. Silencing miR-423-5p reversed this effect.

citation: CDK12 Is Necessary to Promote Epidermal Differentiation Through Transcription Elongation (PMID: 35325240)
summary: CDK12 promotes Ser2 phosphorylation of the RNAPII CTD and stabilizes SPT6 binding to target genes, including differentiation transcription factor genes (GRHL3, KLF4, OVOL1). This places SPT6 in the CDK12-dependent transcription elongation pathway for epidermal differentiation.

citation: S100A10 and its binding partners in depression and antidepressant actions (PMID: 36046712)
summary: Supt6h is a direct binding partner of S100A10 (p11) in the brain. This interaction links p11 to nuclear events such as chromatin remodeling, histone modification and gene transcription relevant to depressive-like behavior and antidepressant responses in mice.

citation: Transcriptomic and immunophenotypic characterization of two cases of adamantinoma-like Ewing sarcoma of the thyroid gland (PMID: 37195579)
summary: SUPT6H, a regulator of EWSR1::FLI1 splicing, was overexpressed along with HNRNPH1 and SF3B1 in adamantinoma-like Ewing sarcoma by RNA-seq. These regulators are needed to produce a functional fusion oncoprotein.

citation: Multi-organ toxicity induced by fine particulate matter PM(2.5) in zebrafish (Danio rerio) model (PMID: 28391149)
summary: supt6h is among the cardiac function genes (with spaw and cmlc1) that were markedly down-regulated by PM2.5 exposure in zebrafish. This coincided with pericardial edema and reduced heart rate.

citation: A Novel Platinum-Resistance-related Gene Signature in Ovarian Cancer: Identification and Patient-derived Organoids Verification (PMID: 39901543)
summary: SUPT6H is one of nine genes in a platinum-resistance prognostic signature for ovarian cancer. The signature was validated in patient-derived organoids, where high-risk patients were more cisplatin-resistant.

citation: Aurora kinase B-phosphorylated HP1α functions in chromosomal instability (PMID: 31130069)
phenotype: HP1α knockout MEFs show mitotic chromosomal instability; Anaphase/telophase chromatin bridges; Micronuclei formation; The same defects occur when the non-phosphorylatable S92A mutant is reconstituted; Defects are rescued by wild-type HP1α or the phosphomimetic S92D variant
knockout_type: full knockout (HP1α-null MEFs, with reconstitution of S92A, S92D or wild-type HP1α)

citation: Somervaille et al. 2009 - Hierarchical maintenance of MLL myeloid leukemia stem cells employs a transcriptional program shared with embryonic rather than adult stem cells (PMID: 19200802)
phenotype: Cbx5, together with Myb and Hmgb3, is a critical component of the ESC-like leukemia stem cell maintenance program; Coexpression of Myb, Hmgb3 and Cbx5 is sufficient for Hoxa/Meis-independent immortalization of myeloid progenitors; Cbx5 is essential for maintaining self-renewing leukemia stem cells

citation: Hoffmann/Ma et al. - HP1α is a chromatin crosslinker that controls nuclear and mitotic chromosome mechanics (PMID: 34106828)
summary: Rapid auxin-inducible degradation of HP1α (CBX5) in human cells did not change transcription, local chromatin compaction or histone methylation, but it reduced chromatin and nuclear stiffness. HP1α acts as a chromatin crosslinker through dimerization (the dimerization-deficient I165E mutant fails to do this), and it supports mitotic chromosome stiffness, alignment and segregation.

citation: CBX5/G9a/H3K9me-mediated gene repression is essential to fibroblast activation during lung fibrosis (PMID: 31095524)
summary: CBX5 (HP1α) acts with the histone methyltransferase G9a and H3K9me marks to epigenetically repress PPARGC1A (PGC1α) in lung fibroblasts. TGFβ and matrix stiffness engage this pathway. Inhibiting it raises PGC1α and reduces collagen accumulation after bleomycin injury.

citation: Targeting the Epigenetic Regulator CBX5 Promotes Fibroblast Metabolic Reprogramming and Inhibits Lung Fibrosis (PMID: 39642371)
summary: CBX5 expression is enriched in pathogenic fibroblasts and fibroblastic foci of IPF lungs (scRNA-seq and IHC). Mesenchymal CBX5 loss attenuated bleomycin-induced fibrosis and downregulated Cthrc1, Col1a1 and Spp1, while upregulating Ppara and Pparg. CBX5 silencing in IPF fibroblasts reduced TGF-stimulated glycolysis and enhanced AMPK signaling and mitochondrial metabolism.

citation: Cell division cycle 7 kinase is a negative regulator of cell-mediated collagen degradation (PMID: 29792348)
summary: A Drosophila phagocyte screen identified CDC7 as a suppressor of collagen uptake. CBX5 is a putative CDC7 target, and genetic silencing of CBX5 increased expression of the collagen receptor Endo180 and increased collagen uptake.

citation: Network biology of tumor stem-like cells identified a regulatory role of CBX5 in lung cancer (PMID: 22900142)
summary: Network analysis of tumor stem-like cells versus parental tumor cells and hESCs identified CBX5 as a regulator of lung cancer stem-like properties and a predictor of prognosis. sh-CBX5 knockdown in vitro and in vivo validated the finding, along with a Taiwanese lung cancer cohort.

citation: Transcriptional control of CBX5 by the RNA binding proteins RBMX and RBMXL1 maintains chromatin state in myeloid leukemia (PMID: 34458856)
summary: RBMX/RBMXL1 control nascent transcription of the CBX5 (HP1α) locus in myeloid leukemia cells. Their loss changed chromatin accessibility and caused chromosomal breaks, and forced CBX5 expression rescued the growth and apoptosis defects.

citation: Regulatory dissection of the CBX5 and hnRNPA1 bi-directional promoter in human breast cancer cells (PMID: 26791953)
summary: CBX5 shares a bi-directional promoter with hnRNPA1 and is down-regulated in metastatic breast cancer cells. Novel CBX5 transcripts were found in intron 1, including autonomous-promoter HP1α-coding isoforms and the non-coding STET isoform. STET is inversely correlated with HP1α-coding mRNA in breast cancer cell lines and patient tissues.

citation: Blood transcriptomics of drug-naïve sporadic Parkinson's disease patients (PMID: 26510930)
sample_size: 40 PD and 20 controls (discovery); 12 in validation set
summary: CBX5 was differentially expressed in the blood of drug-naïve sporadic PD patients and was validated by RT-qPCR in an independent cohort. This is part of a chromatin remodeling and methylation signature.

citation: Porphyromonas gingivalis Outer Membrane Vesicles Promote Apoptosis via msRNA-Regulated DNA Methylation in Periodontitis (PMID: 36629433)
summary: A bacterial msRNA, sRNA45033, in P. gingivalis OMVs targets CBX5 in human periodontal ligament cells, confirmed by dual-luciferase assay and overexpression/knockdown. CUT&Tag showed CBX5 regulates apoptosis through methylation of p53 DNA.

citation: BRD4 facilitates DNA damage response and represses CBX5/Heterochromatin protein 1 (HP1) (PMID: 28881656)
summary: BRD4 inhibition (siRNA or JQ1) increased CBX5 (HP1α) levels in ovarian cancer cells. Nuclear CBX5 and γ-H2AX were mutually exclusive in BRD4- and CHK1-inhibited cells, suggesting BRD4 promotes the DNA damage response by repressing CBX5.

citation: Haploinsufficiency of brain-specific kinase BRSK1 causes epilepsy and neurodevelopmental disorders (PMID: 41035394)
variant_detail: Frameshift/nonsense variants (including indels) in BRSK1; specific notations not given in abstract. Complete loss of detectable BRSK1 protein.
phenotype: epilepsy; neurodevelopmental disorders
diagnostic_reason: Six novel variants in seven probands from trio exome sequencing; five de novo, one inherited, one recurrent; LoF variants led to loss of BRSK1 protein, the missense reduced protein levels; Brsk1 knockout mice (heterozygous and homozygous) show seizure susceptibility, hyperexcitability and neurobehavioral impairments, supporting haploinsufficiency
center_country: Not stated in abstract (cohort of 394 epilepsy probands; likely China)

citation: Haploinsufficiency of brain-specific kinase BRSK1 causes epilepsy and neurodevelopmental disorders (PMID: 41035394)
variant_detail: One missense variant (specific notation not given in abstract) that reduced BRSK1 protein levels
phenotype: epilepsy; neurodevelopmental disorders
diagnostic_reason: Six novel variants in seven probands from trio exome sequencing; five de novo, one inherited, one recurrent; LoF variants led to loss of BRSK1 protein, the missense reduced protein levels; Brsk1 knockout mice (heterozygous and homozygous) show seizure susceptibility, hyperexcitability and neurobehavioral impairments, supporting haploinsufficiency
center_country: Not stated in abstract (cohort of 394 epilepsy probands; likely China)

citation: ASHG 2022 - An emirati cohort of autism spectrum disorders
variant_detail: Novel de novo variant in BRSK1 (notation and type not specified)
phenotype: autism spectrum disorder
diagnostic_reason: Novel de novo variant identified by trio exome sequencing in an Emirati ASD cohort; BRSK1 proposed as a candidate ASD gene (not classified as likely pathogenic)

citation: Haploinsufficiency of brain-specific kinase BRSK1 causes epilepsy and neurodevelopmental disorders (PMID: 41035394)
phenotype: increased seizure susceptibility in heterozygous and homozygous mice; neuronal hyperexcitability; neurobehavioral impairments; recapitulates the clinical features of human BRSK1 haploinsufficiency (epilepsy and neurodevelopmental disorders); proteomic and phosphoproteomic dysregulation of pathways critical for axonal development and synaptic function
knockout_type: full knockout (Brsk1 exon 4-7 deletion, Brsk1Δ4-7; both heterozygous and homozygous animals studied)

citation: Haploinsufficiency of brain-specific kinase BRSK1 causes epilepsy and neurodevelopmental disorders (PMID: 41035394)
sample_size: 394 epilepsy probands; 7 probands with BRSK1 variants; Brsk1Δ4-7 mouse line
summary: Trio exome sequencing found six novel BRSK1 variants (mostly de novo, frameshift/nonsense/missense) in seven epilepsy probands. Truncating variants abolished BRSK1 protein and a missense variant reduced it. Brsk1 Δ4-7 knockout mice (heterozygous and homozygous) showed seizure susceptibility, neuronal hyperexcitability and behavioral deficits, and proteomics/phosphoproteomics showed dysregulated axonal development and synaptic pathways.

citation: Monoallelic variants in BRSK1 are associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder with or without epilepsy (PMID: 42805187)
sample_size: 10 individuals; 3 missense variants modeled in Drosophila
summary: Ten individuals with heterozygous BRSK1 variants had developmental delay, autism, ADHD, anxiety and seizures. The Drosophila ortholog sff is expressed in neurons. sff null flies show locomotor defects, bang/heat sensitivity, short lifespan, NMJ overgrowth and elevated Futsch (MAP1B). Human BRSK1 cDNA rescued these phenotypes, whereas the Ile202Val, Arg237Cys and Thr406Ile alleles gave only partial rescue, consistent with partial loss of function.

citation: Decreased expression and prognostic role of cytoplasmic BRSK1 in human breast carcinoma: correlation with Jab1 stability and PI3K/Akt pathway (PMID: 25036402)
sample_size: 95 breast carcinoma samples; MDA-MB-231 and other breast cancer cell lines
summary: Cytoplasmic BRSK1 was inversely correlated with Jab1 and with histologic grade in breast carcinoma, and low expression predicted poor survival. Release from serum starvation lowered BRSK1 and p27 and raised Jab1 and p-Akt. PI3K inhibition with LY294002 increased BRSK1. BRSK1 is proposed as a tumor suppressor acting through the PI3K/Akt–Jab1–p27 axis.

citation: Integrative High-Throughput RNAi Screening Identifies BRSK1, STK32C and STK40 as Novel Activators of YAP/TAZ (PMID: 40869130)
summary: Two kinome RNAi screens in TNBC lines (YAP/TAZ localization and TEAD-luciferase reporter) identified BRSK1 as a regulator of YAP/TAZ activity. This places BRSK1 as an AMPK-family member in Hippo pathway regulation, alongside NUAKs, MARKs and SIKs.

citation: Brain specific kinase-1 BRSK1/SAD-B associates with lipid rafts: modulation of kinase activity by lipid environment (PMID: 22020259)
summary: Brain BRSK1, but not BRSK2, is palmitoylated, and a pool of it localizes to membrane lipid rafts. Raft-associated BRSK1 has higher Thr189 T-loop phosphorylation. Raft-like lipid vesicles increased recombinant BRSK1 activity about 3-fold, including the constitutively active T189E mutant, revealing lipid-environment regulation independent of T-loop phosphorylation.

citation: BRSK1 confers cisplatin resistance in cervical cancer cells via regulation of mitochondrial respiration (PMID: 37140697)
summary: BRSK1 was upregulated in cisplatin-treated cervical tumors and cell lines. Its depletion sensitized normal and resistant cells to cisplatin. This effect depends on kinase activity and on a mitochondrial pool of BRSK1 that regulates mitochondrial respiration. High BRSK1 expression correlated with poor prognosis in cisplatin-treated patients.

citation: Neuronal Growth Factor regulates Brain Specific Kinase 1 expression by inhibiting promoter methylation and promoting Sp1 recruitment (PMID: 30196145)
summary: BRSKs are preferentially expressed in brain after E12. NGF increased Brsk1 mRNA in PC12 cells through MAPK-dependent Sp1 activation. Sp1 binding at a CpG-island site in the minimal promoter (-342 to +125) was blocked by DNA methylation. 5'Aza-dC synergized with NGF, and DNMT3B overexpression (itself an NGF/MAPK target) abolished the promoter's NGF response.

citation: LKB1 is a master kinase that activates 13 kinases of the AMPK subfamily, including MARK/PAR-1 (PMID: 14976552)
summary: LKB1 (with STRAD and MO25) phosphorylates the T-loop of BRSK1 and BRSK2 and other AMPK-related kinases, increasing activity more than 50-fold. This places BRSK1 downstream of LKB1 in the AMPK-related kinase cascade. AMPK activators phenformin and AICAR did not stimulate this pathway.

citation: Regulation of brain-specific kinases 1 and 2 (BRSK1/2) by Ca(2+)/calmodulin (PMID: 41905287)
summary: A screen of 462 kinases identified calmodulin interaction with BRSK2, and BRSK1 also binds CaM in a Ca2+-dependent manner via its kinase domain. Ca2+/CaM blocks LKB1-mediated Thr189 phosphorylation and activation of BRSK1 (IC50 ~7 µM) without affecting LKB1 activity or PP2Cα dephosphorylation of already-phosphorylated BRSK1.

citation: The balance of mitochondrial fission and fusion in cortical axons depends on the kinases SadA and SadB (PMID: 34936879)
summary: SadA/B (BRSK2/BRSK1) regulate axonal mitochondrial dynamics in cortical neurons through tau phosphorylation, stimulated by Ankyrin B. Loss of SadA/B causes hyper-fused mitochondria, integrated stress response activation, excess actin stabilization and reduced Drp1 recruitment to mitochondria.

citation: Germ Cell-Specific Retinoic Acid Receptor α Functions in Germ Cell Organization, Meiotic Integrity, and Spermatogonia (PMID: 30099545)
phenotype: germ cell-specific Rara deletion; reduced epididymal sperm counts; disorganized germ cell layers in seminiferous tubules, worsening with age; abnormal tubules lacking lumen, with vacuoles and massive germ cell sloughing, similar to Rara-null tubules; impaired synaptonemal complex integrity and meiotic progression; decreased initiation of spermatogenesis from spermatogonial stem cells after busulfan treatment (reduced spermatogonial proliferation)

citation: Retinoic acid induces Sertoli cell paracrine signals for spermatogonia differentiation but cell autonomously drives spermatocyte meiosis (PMID: 23012458)
phenotype: somatic genetic ablations of RA synthesis and signaling in Sertoli cells, including Rara; RARA in Sertoli cells mediates RA effects on differentiation of A aligned into A1 spermatogonia, possibly via Mafb expression; RA-dependent control of Stra8 expression and meiotic initiation in spermatocytes; RA of Sertoli cell origin is essential for spermiation

citation: Retinoic acid receptor antagonists for male contraception: current status (PMID: 32671394)
phenotype: review noting that global Rara knockout validates RARA as a male contraceptive target; RARA activity is indispensable for spermatogenesis; pan-RAR and RARA-selective antagonists (BMS-189453, BMS-189532, BMS-189614) cause reversible spermatogenic disruption in mice

citation: The bile acid-activated retinoic acid response in dendritic cells is involved in food allergen sensitization (PMID: 34365653)
phenotype: DC-specific Rara knockout (DC KO Rara); RA signaling in DCs is required for food allergen-specific IgE and IgG1 production; bile acid-activated RA signaling promotes DC interferon I signature, OX40L and PDL2 upregulation, and Th2 differentiation

citation: Bacterial Quorum Sensing Molecules Promote Allergic Airway Inflammation by Activating the Retinoic Acid Response (PMID: 32622265)
phenotype: DC-specific Rara knockout diminished the AHL-stimulated type 2 immune response (IgE and IgG1 production); reduced AHL-driven allergic airway inflammation and Th2 differentiation

citation: Zhang et al. 2015 - MicroRNA-27a Contributes to Rhabdomyosarcoma Cell Proliferation by Suppressing RARA and RXRA (PMID: 25915942)
summary: miR-27a is up-regulated in translocation-positive alveolar RMS cell lines and targets RARA and RXRA. Overexpressing miR-27a increased proliferation and reduced the fraction of cells in G1. This links RARA suppression to cell cycle control.

citation: Clearance of PML/RARA-bound promoters suffice to initiate APL differentiation (PMID: 25258343)
summary: RXRA is a coreceptor of the PML/RARA fusion and promotes its efficient DNA binding. Ablating retinoid X receptors loosens PML/RARA DNA binding and induces terminal differentiation of APL cells ex vivo and in vivo. RXRA sumoylation contributes to PML/RARA-dependent transformation.

citation: FTO Plays an Oncogenic Role in Acute Myeloid Leukemia as a N(6)-Methyladenosine RNA Demethylase (PMID: 28017614)
summary: FTO is an m6A demethylase that regulates RARA and ASB2 mRNA by reducing m6A levels in the transcripts. Through this, FTO inhibits ATRA-induced differentiation of AML cells. FTO is highly expressed in t(15;17)/PML-RARA AMLs.

citation: Functional multiomics reveals genetic and pharmacologic regulation of surface CD38 in multiple myeloma (PMID: 40453054)
summary: Genome-wide CRISPRi screens in myeloma cells confirmed RARA as a known regulator of surface CD38. All-trans retinoic acid specifically upregulated CD38 in the integrated transcriptome and surface proteome data.

citation: Targeting ALDH1A1 to enhance the efficacy of KRAS-targeted therapy through ferroptosis (PMID: 39317105)
summary: ALDH1A1 boosts retinoic acid synthesis and improves RARA function. This contributes to resistance to KRAS inhibitors by counteracting ferroptosis, together with activation of the CREB1/GPX4 pathway.

citation: Dysregulation of the ALDH1A3/PML-RARα axis promotes the progression of acute promyelocytic leukemia (PMID: 41580016)
summary: ALDH1A3 cooperates with MAZ to transcriptionally repress PML-RARα expression, shown by ChIP, luciferase reporter assays and EMSA. PML-RARα in turn increases methylation of the ALDH1A3 promoter and suppresses its expression in APL patients. This reciprocal repression correlates with clinical remission.

citation: Expression and function of PML-RARA in the hematopoietic progenitor cells of Ctsg-PML-RARA mice (PMID: 23056333)
summary: In Ctsg-PML-RARA mice, PML-RARA is expressed in KLS hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells as well as in CMPs, GMPs and promyelocytes. It alters the transcriptional signature of these cells and affects multilineage repopulation, but does not induce promyelocyte self-renewal.

citation: Function of PML-RARA in Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia (PMID: 39017850)
summary: The PML-RARA fusion deregulates transcriptional control of RAR targets involved in self-renewal and myeloid differentiation and disrupts PML nuclear bodies. Its target genes are not uniformly repressed; some are upregulated or unchanged. RA and arsenic target the fusion's transcriptional deregulation and its protein stability.

citation: Novel treatment of acute promyelocytic leukemia: As2O3, retinoic acid and retinoid pharmacology (PMID: 24433507)
summary: PML/RARa acts as a strong transcriptional repressor of the RAR complex at RAREs by recruiting N-CoR, SMRT and HDACs. High-dose RA relieves this repression and promotes degradation of the fusion. Wild-type RARa is upregulated and PML nuclear bodies relocalize.

citation: Indeno[1,2,3-cd]pyrene and picene mediate actions via estrogen receptor α signaling pathway in in vitro cell systems, altering gene expression (PMID: 32251684)
summary: In MCF-7 cells, the PAHs indeno[1,2,3-cd]pyrene and picene downregulated RARA among 14 ESR1-regulated genes, as shown by RNA sequencing.

citation: Garcia-Beltran et al. 2016 - HLA-F and MHC-I open conformers (OCs) bind KIR3DS1 (PMID: 27649529)
summary: Surface plasmon resonance, pull-down and heterodimerization assays showed that HLA-F and other MHC-I open conformers physically bind KIR3DS1 but not KIR3DL1. HLA-F immobilized on surfaces increased granule exocytosis in activated KIR3DS1+ cells, indicating a functional response.

citation: HLA-F and MHC class I open conformers are ligands for NK cell Ig-like receptors (PMID: 24018270)
summary: Peptide-free HLA-F open conformer physically and functionally interacts with KIR3DL2 and KIR2DS4. Classical MHC-I open conformers also act as KIR ligands, suggesting an immunoregulatory role in inflammation.

citation: HLA-F and MHC-I open conformers cooperate in a MHC-I antigen cross-presentation pathway (PMID: 23851683)
summary: HLA-F and MHC-I open conformers on activated lymphocytes and monocytes mediate cross-presentation of exogenous antigen. This pathway is TAP- and tapasin-independent, sensitive to lysosomal enzyme inhibitors, and depends on allotype-specific epitope recognition.

citation: Interactions Between KIR3DS1 and HLA-F Activate Natural Killer Cells to Control HCV Replication in Cell Culture (PMID: 30031767)
summary: HLA-F is up-regulated on HCV-infected cells in culture, in humanized-liver mice and in primary liver tissue. KIR3DS1-HLA-F interaction contributes to NK cell-mediated control of HCV replication.

citation: HLA-F transcriptional and protein differential expression according to its genetic polymorphisms (PMID: 37166140)
sample_size: 1000 Genomes samples plus healthy donor PBMC
summary: SNPs rs1362126, rs2523405 and rs2523393 near HLA-F or in HLA-F-AS1 were associated with HLA-F expression, with the largest effect sizes and a double-dose effect. This was shown in 1000 Genomes RNAseq and by Q-PCR and intracellular cytometry in PBMC. Allele frequencies differ across geographic populations.

citation: Endometrial HLA-F expression is influenced by genotypes and correlates differently with immune cell infiltration in IVF and recurrent implantation failure patients (PMID: 35689445)
sample_size: 85 RIF women, 36 IVF controls; 5 primary ESC cultures
summary: HLA-F protein is expressed in mid-secretory endometrium and endometrial stromal cells. Levels vary with HLA-F SNP genotypes and diplotypes, and correlate with CD163+ M2 macrophage and CD56+ uNK cell infiltration and with plasma progesterone.

citation: Correlation of alteration of HLA-F expression and clinical characterization in 593 brain glioma samples (PMID: 30755240)
significance: Kaplan-Meier survival association (p-value not given in abstract)
summary: High HLA-F expression correlated with poorer overall survival in glioma and GBM. It was enriched in GBM, IDH1 wild-type and mesenchymal subtype tumors, and correlated with other HLA class I molecules.

citation: HLA-F expression is a prognostic factor in patients with non-small-cell lung cancer (PMID: 21561677)
summary: HLA-F was detected by IHC in 24.1% of NSCLC lesions but not in adjacent normal lung. Positive expression was an independent poor prognostic factor (HR 5.12).

citation: Human leukocyte antigen (HLA)-E and HLA-F expression in gastric cancer (PMID: 25862890)
summary: HLA-F was expressed on the cell membrane of gastric cancer cells. Expression correlated with depth of invasion, nodal, lymphatic and venous invasion, and with poorer five-year survival, especially in combination with HLA-E.

citation: ASHG 2018 - Illuminating the dark genome: Evaluation of technologies to assess medically relevant dark spots
summary: A polymorphic 2.6 kbp deletion upstream of HLA-F was identified. RNA-Seq showed it correlates with HLA-F expression level and exon usage.

citation: ASHG 2023 - A RING1 contribution to neurogenesis and schizophrenia (C. Ryan)
variant_detail: RING1 G284A (p.Gly284Ala; modeled as homozygous G284A/G284A in isogenic hESC lines)
phenotype: neurodevelopmental disorder; microcephaly; intellectual disability; early onset schizophrenia
diagnostic_reason: Missense variants in RING1/RNF2 blunt H2AUb1 catalysis. The RING1 G284A variant reduced global H2AUb1, increased expression of DNA damage repair genes, impaired double strand break repair and prolonged S phase in hESC-derived NPCs and cerebral organoids. The abstract does not describe individual patients.

citation: Ring1 regulates dorsoventral patterning of the mouse telencephalon (PMID: 33177537)
phenotype: Deletion of Ring1b or both Ring1a and Ring1b in neuroepithelial cells caused ectopic expression of dorsal genes, including BMP and Wnt ligand genes, in the ventral telencephalon; Shh expression was attenuated in the ventral telencephalon; Ventral telencephalon development was impaired (loss of ventralization); Ring1B binding and H3K27me3 were present at BMP and Wnt ligand genes specifically in the ventral region

citation: Rnf2 (Ring1b) deficiency causes gastrulation arrest and cell cycle inhibition (PMID: 12589020)
phenotype: Rnf2-null embryos arrested at gastrulation, with defects in both embryonic and extraembryonic tissues; Rnf2 hemizygosity did not affect vertebral identity, but aggravated the cerebellar phenotype in a Bmi1 null background; Early arrest was partially bypassed by inactivation of the Cdkn2a (Ink4a/ARF) locus; Ring1 (Ring1a) mutants have relatively mild phenotypes, with strong skeletal transformation in hemizygous mice
knockout_type: full knockout (Rnf2 null; Ring1 null/hemizygous mice discussed for comparison)

citation: Essential role of MESP1-RING1A complex in cardiac differentiation (PMID: 36413948)
phenotype: Ring1A knockout mice showed cardiac abnormalities similar to those in patients with MESP1 mutations; RING1A depletion impaired human cardiomyocyte differentiation (in vitro)

citation: RING1 dictates GSDMD-mediated inflammatory response and host susceptibility to pathogen infection (PMID: 40369166)
phenotype: Loss of Ring1 increased S. typhimurium infectious load and mortality; Ring1 deletion initially reduced M. tuberculosis infectious load, but later caused increased lung inflammation and impaired immune defense; Ring1 knockout exacerbated LPS-induced acute sepsis; Increased GSDMD levels and pyroptosis

citation: Role of remodeling and spacing factor 1 in histone H2A ubiquitination-mediated gene silencing (PMID: 28855339)
phenotype: RSF1 and Ring1 acted cooperatively to regulate mesodermal cell specification and gastrulation during early embryonic development

citation: De novo mutation in RING1 with epigenetic effects on neurodevelopment (PMID: 29386386)
summary: A de novo RING1 p.R95Q variant in the catalytic RING domain was found in a girl with syndromic neurodevelopmental disability. The mutant retains ubiquitin chain formation but cannot ubiquitylate nucleosomal H2A, and patient cells show reduced H2A monoubiquitylation. The equivalent mutation in C. elegans spat-3, or a spat-3 knockout, reduced H2A ubiquitylation and caused neuronal migration and axon guidance defects, including in heterozygotes.

citation: ASHG 2023 - A RING1 contribution to neurogenesis and schizophrenia (C. Ryan)
summary: Isogenic hESC lines carrying pathogenic RING1 variants were differentiated into NPCs and 3D cerebral organoids. The RING1 G284A/G284A variant lowered global H2AUb1, increased expression of DNA damage repair genes, impaired double-strand break repair, and stalled the cell cycle through a prolonged S phase. RING1/RNF2 missense variants that blunt H2AUb1 catalysis are linked to microcephaly, intellectual disability and early-onset schizophrenia.

citation: Polycomb protein RING1A limits hematopoietic differentiation in myelodysplastic syndromes (PMID: 29383137)
summary: RING1A is expressed in CD34+ bone marrow progenitors and is overexpressed in high-risk MDS. Higher expression associated with more dysplastic lineages and blasts. RING1A knockdown promoted spontaneous and retinoic acid-induced differentiation in an MDS-derived AML line and augmented erythroid differentiation in primary CD34+ cells. A RING1 inhibitor reduced colony formation by CD34+ cells from MDS patients and healthy controls.

citation: Ring1-mediated ubiquitination of H2A restrains poised RNA polymerase II at bivalent genes in mouse ES cells (PMID: 18037880)
summary: Conditional deletion of Ring1A and Ring1B in mouse ES cells caused sequential loss of H2A ubiquitination, release of poised Ser5-phosphorylated RNAP II, and de-repression of bivalent developmental genes. Ring1-mediated H2A ubiquitination therefore enforces the poised polymerase state.

citation: The Polycomb group protein Ring1 regulates dorsoventral patterning of the mouse telencephalon (PMID: 33177537)
summary: Deletion of Ring1b, or of both Ring1a and Ring1b, in neuroepithelial cells caused ectopic expression of dorsal genes (BMP and Wnt ligands) and reduced Shh in the ventral telencephalon. Ring1B binds BMP and Wnt ligand genes in the ventral region, where H3K27me3 is also present. Ring1 thus supports ventral telencephalon development by suppressing BMP and Wnt signaling.

citation: Role of histone H2A ubiquitination in Polycomb silencing (PMID: 15386022)
summary: Ring1 is a component of the hPRC1L complex together with Ring2, Bmi1 and HPH2. The complex monoubiquitinates nucleosomal H2A at K119. In Drosophila, dRing colocalizes with ubiquitinated H2A at Ubx, and its RNAi removal causes loss of H2A ubiquitination and Ubx derepression.

citation: Targeting UBE2T Potentiates Gemcitabine Efficacy in Pancreatic Cancer by Regulating Pyrimidine Metabolism and Replication Stress (PMID: 36842710)
summary: UBE2T catalyzes RING1-mediated ubiquitination of p53 in pancreatic cancer. This relieves p53 transcriptional repression of RRM1 and RRM2, increasing pyrimidine biosynthesis, easing replication stress, and conferring gemcitabine resistance.

citation: Down-regulation of lncRNA XIST inhibits cell proliferation via regulating miR-744/RING1 axis in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 31292221)
summary: XIST acts as a competing endogenous RNA for miR-744, which regulates RING1. The XIST/miR-744/RING1 axis activates Wnt/β-catenin signaling and promotes NSCLC proliferation, migration and invasion in vitro and in vivo.

citation: Chromobox 3 assembles an epigenetic complex contributing to cystathionine γ-lyase-mediated protection against aortic aneurysm/dissection (PMID: 42236713)
summary: RING1 was identified as part of a CBX3-centered epigenetic complex with SUV39H1, KDM2A and HDAC1. The complex coordinates H3K9/H3K4 methylation and acetylation to regulate ECM remodeling, apoptosis and inflammation genes in vascular smooth muscle cells.

citation: ASHG 2013 - DNA methylation analysis of iPS cells using whole-genome bisulphite sequencing (D. Lee et al.)
summary: During reprogramming of mouse fibroblasts to iPSCs, CpG methylation gain occurs rapidly and massively around PRC (RING1, Suz12, EZH2) binding sites.

citation: A functional role for Septin-2 in the maintenance of the axon initial segment and in human cognitive development (PMID: 41408595)
variant_detail: Specific variant notations not given in the abstract. Mutations reported in five unrelated individuals and one mother-daughter duo, predicted to preclude Septin-2 homodimerization (dominant negative).
phenotype: cognitive impairment (in the majority of individuals); impaired higher cognitive function / neurodevelopmental phenotype
diagnostic_reason: Predicted dominant-negative effect blocking septin octamer assembly by preventing Septin-2 homodimerization. Mutant constructs in neurons caused loss of AIS Ankyrin G, aberrant MAP2 in the distal axon, axonal shortening and hypoexcitability, and the Ankyrin G interaction was largely ablated. The variant type is inferred from the dominant-negative and homodimerization mechanism, not stated in the abstract.

citation: Hypoxia exposure impairs male fertility via inhibiting Septin2-mediated spermatogonial proliferation (PMID: 40487848)
phenotype: Sept2 knockdown in normoxic mice phenocopied hypoxia-induced spermatogenesis defects; Impaired spermatogonial proliferation; G1-S phase arrest in spermatogonial cells upon Sept2 depletion; Reduced AKT phosphorylation via PP2A/B56γ stabilization; Hypoxia downregulated Sept2 in spermatogonia and impaired fertility, sperm quality, and testicular histology
sample_size: n = 3-5 mice per intervention group; hypoxic mouse model n = 5

citation: SEPTIN7 Deficiency Disrupts Endothelial Integrity and Causes Myxomatous Valve Disease in Juvenile Mice (PMID: 42657464)
phenotype: Endocardial lineage-specific Septin2 conditional knockout mice developed normally without detectable abnormalities; No detectable cardiac or valve abnormalities in Septin2 mutants (in contrast to Septin7 mutants, which had juvenile lethality and myxomatous valve disease)

citation: Toriyama et al. 2017 - Folate-dependent methylation of septins governs ciliogenesis during neural tube closure (PMID: 28432198)
phenotype: Disruption of folate-mediated methylation pathway compromised neural tube closure and ciliogenesis; Embryos with neural tube defects failed to adequately methylate septin2; Septin2 methylation affected GTP binding and septin2-6-7 complex formation

citation: Toriyama et al. 2017 - Folate-dependent methylation of septins governs ciliogenesis during neural tube closure (PMID: 28432198)
summary: Folate-dependent one-carbon methylation pathway regulates septin2 methylation. Embryos with neural tube defects failed to adequately methylate septin2. Methylation affects its GTP binding and formation of the septin2-6-7 complex, which is critical for ciliogenesis and neural tube closure.

citation: 2019 - Septin2 mediates podosome maturation and endothelial cell invasion associated with angiogenesis (PMID: 31865373)
summary: Septin2, Septin6 and Septin7 are required for maturation of endothelial podosomes into matrix-degrading organelles. Septin2 is recruited after Tks5 and F-actin and localizes around the podosome perimeter, where it forms a diffusion barrier. Its phosphoinositide-binding residues are required for podosome function and for angiogenic endothelial invasion.

citation: 2024 - S-Nitrosylation of Septin2 Exacerbates Aortic Aneurysm and Dissection by Coupling the TIAM1-RAC1 Axis in Macrophages (PMID: 38357802)
summary: Septin2 is S-nitrosylated at Cys111 in aortic tissue from dissection patients and in Ang II-infused Apoe-/- mice. SNO-Septin2 has reduced interaction with TIAM1, which activates RAC1 and NF-κB signaling, driving macrophage inflammation and extracellular matrix degradation. RAC1 inhibitors (R-Ketorolac, NSC23766) were protective.

citation: 2023 - SEPTIN2 suppresses an IFN-γ-independent, proinflammatory macrophage activation pathway (PMID: 37978190)
summary: SEPT2 was identified by high-content screening as a negative regulator of IFN-γ-independent macrophage autoactivation. ER stress induces SEPT2, which balances acetylation and ubiquitination of HSPA5 at K327, alleviating ER stress and limiting M1-like polarization and cytokine release.

citation: 2023 - Lysyl hydroxylase LH1 promotes confined migration and metastasis of cancer cells by stabilizing Septin2 to enhance actin network (PMID: 36721170)
summary: LH1 binds and stabilizes SEPT2 in a hydroxylase-domain-dependent manner, enhancing actin polymerization and confined migration and metastasis in HCC and PDAC. Tumors with high LH1 and SEPT2 had the poorest prognosis.

citation: 2018 - Coupling function of cyclin-dependent kinase 2 and Septin2 in the promotion of hepatocellular carcinoma (PMID: 30444001)
sample_size: 8 paired fresh HCC tissues; 100 HCC patients
summary: CDK2 and SEPT2 show similar cell-cycle dynamics with peak protein levels in G2/M. CDK2 interacts with and stabilizes SEPT2. Their expression is correlated in HCC tissue, and high co-expression is associated with relapse, poor differentiation and microvascular invasion.

citation: 2004 - Functional interdependence between septin and actin cytoskeleton (PMID: 15541171)
summary: Septin2 filaments associate with actin bundles but are excluded from dynamic leading edges and ruffles. Septin2 assemblies are highly dynamic by FRAP independent of actin. RNAi and truncation experiments show Septin2 stabilizes or maintains actin stress fibres.

citation: 2025 - Hypoxia exposure impairs male fertility via inhibiting Septin2-mediated spermatogonial proliferation (PMID: 40487848)
sample_size: 24 high-altitude residents, 6 pathological hypoxia patients, 19 controls; mouse n=3-5/group
summary: Hypoxia downregulates Sept2 transcription in spermatogonia by disrupting POLR2A binding to the Sept2 promoter. Sept2 loss stabilizes PP2A B56γ, causing AKT dephosphorylation and G1-S arrest. Sept2 knockdown in mice phenocopied the hypoxic spermatogenesis defects, and overexpression rescued proliferation in vitro.

citation: 2010 - Septin2 is modified by SUMOylation and required for chromosome congression in mouse oocytes (PMID: 20372094)
summary: Septin2 is SUMO-1 modified in mouse oocytes and localizes to the spindle and midbody. Inhibitor or siRNA disruption of septins causes chromosome misalignment and failure of the metaphase I/anaphase I transition via spindle checkpoint activation, but does not affect cytokinesis.

citation: 2014 - FHL2-driven molecular network mediated Septin2 knockdown inducing apoptosis in mesangial cell (PMID: 25103794)
summary: FHL2 is a new Septin2 interaction partner. Septin2 knockdown induces rat mesangial cell apoptosis via FHL2-mediated p-ERK1 and p-AKT signaling. FHL2 overexpression alleviates the apoptosis.

citation: Molecular characterisation of a 15 Mb constitutional de novo interstitial deletion of chromosome 3p in a boy with developmental delay and congenital anomalies (PMID: 12836054)
variant_detail: de novo ~15 Mb interstitial deletion del(3)(p13p11) (D3S3551 to centromere), paternal origin, encompassing PROK2, GPR27, RYBP, PPP4R2, ROBO1, GBE1 and others
phenotype: developmental delay; psychomotor retardation; craniofacial dysmorphism; cleft lip
diagnostic_reason: De novo large interstitial deletion confirmed by G-banding, FISH with BAC clones and polymorphic marker analysis. GPR27 is only one of several deleted genes and is not itself implicated as causal.

citation: Copy Number Variants in 30 Saudi Pediatric Patients with Neurodevelopmental Disorders: From Unknown Significance to Diagnosis (PMID: 39539796)
variant_detail: 3p13p12.3 (70411134_75249376) x1 heterozygous deletion, 4838 kb, spanning 19 genes including FOXP1, GPR27, PROK2, SHQ1
phenotype: intellectual developmental disorder; language impairment; possible autistic features; psychomotor impairment; developmental regression; epilepsy
diagnostic_reason: CNV reclassified as pathogenic using the ClinGen CNV Pathogenicity Calculator (ACMG criteria). The pathogenicity is attributed mainly to FOXP1 deletion, with PROK2 and SHQ1 also noted as morbid genes. GPR27 is a passenger gene in the deletion.
center_country: King Saud Medical City, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

citation: The distinct and overlapping phenotypic spectra of FOXP1 and FOXP2 in cognitive disorders (PMID: 22736078)
variant_detail: 785 kb heterozygous deletion at 3p14.1 involving FOXP1, EIF4E3, PROK2 and GPR27 (patient from Pariani et al. 2009)
phenotype: gross motor delay; contractures; blepharophimosis; hypertonia; speech delay (vowel sounds but no words at 23 months)
diagnostic_reason: Deletion including FOXP1 was reported as an early hint of FOXP1 involvement in neurodevelopmental disorders. GPR27 is only a co-deleted gene, and the phenotype is attributed mainly to FOXP1.

citation: Genetic deletion of gpr27 alters acylcarnitine metabolism, insulin sensitivity, and glucose homeostasis in zebrafish (PMID: 31914600)
phenotype: Potentiated elevation of glucose levels after pharmacological or nutritional perturbation; Elevated medium-chain acylcarnitines (C6-hexanoyl-, C8-octanoyl-, C9-nonanoyl-, C10-decanoylcarnitine); Abrogated insulin-dependent Akt phosphorylation; Reduced glucose utilization (insulin resistance); Increased expression of carnitine shuttle enzymes, including the CPT1C homolog

citation: Deletion of Gpr27 in vivo reduces insulin mRNA but does not result in diabetes (PMID: 32221326)
phenotype: No gross abnormalities; Insulin and Pdx1 mRNA reduced by about 30% in islets; No reduction in islet insulin content or beta cell mass; Slightly worsened glucose tolerance with lower plasma insulin; Similar insulin tolerance to controls; Reduced expression of the neighboring gene Eif4e3, likely from deletion of antisense transcription start sites

citation: Surface Electrical Impedance Myography Detects Skeletal Muscle Atrophy in Aged Wildtype Zebrafish and Aged gpr27 Knockout Zebrafish (PMID: 37509577)
phenotype: Exacerbated skeletal muscle atrophy in aged gpr27 knockout animals, shown by both sEIM and histology; Reduced myofiber cross-sectional area
significance: Significance values are reported for young vs aged wildtype sEIM comparisons (e.g., p < 0.000001); no values are given in the abstract for the gpr27 knockout effect

citation: Zebrafish gpr27 knockout - Genetic deletion of gpr27 alters acylcarnitine metabolism, insulin sensitivity, and glucose homeostasis in zebrafish (PMID: 31914600)
summary: Whole-body gpr27 knockout zebrafish showed potentiated glucose elevation after pharmacological or nutritional challenge. They also had elevated medium-chain acylcarnitines (C6-C10), abrogated insulin-dependent Akt phosphorylation and glucose utilization, and increased expression of carnitine shuttle enzymes including the CPT1C homolog. This implicates Gpr27 in lipid metabolism, insulin signaling and glucose homeostasis.

citation: Deletion of Gpr27 in vivo reduces insulin mRNA but does not result in diabetes (PMID: 32221326)
summary: Whole-body Gpr27 knockout mice were born at Mendelian ratios with no gross abnormalities. Islet insulin and Pdx1 mRNA fell by about 30%, but islet insulin content and beta cell mass were unchanged. Glucose tolerance was slightly worse with lower plasma insulin and normal insulin tolerance. Gpr27 deletion also reduced expression of the neighboring gene Eif4e3, likely by removing antisense transcription start sites.

citation: An siRNA screen in pancreatic beta cells reveals a role for Gpr27 in insulin production (PMID: 22253604)
summary: In an siRNA screen of mouse GPCRs in MIN6 beta cells, Gpr27 was a top positive regulator of insulin promoter activity. Knockdown reduced insulin promoter activity and glucose-stimulated insulin secretion, and the effect depended on Pdx1. Gpr27 overexpression in 293T cells increased inositol phosphates and knockdown in MIN6 reduced them, suggesting Gq/11 coupling.

citation: Activation of the Orphan GPCR GPR27 by Surrogate Ligands Promotes β-Arrestin 2 Recruitment (PMID: 28314853)
summary: A screen identified N-phenyl-2,4-dichlorobenzamide-scaffold surrogate agonists selective for GPR27 over GPR85 and GPR173. They drive β-arrestin 2 recruitment, confirmed in several orthogonal assays. GPR27 showed no ligand-independent activity and no G protein activation, indicating an atypical, arrestin-biased signaling profile.

citation: Development of Ligands for the Super Conserved Orphan GPCR GPR27 with Improved Efficacy and Potency (PMID: 38060818)
summary: Benzamide derivatives (e.g., PT-91/7p, pEC50 6.15; 7ab, pEC50 6.56) were developed as GPR27-specific β-arrestin 2 recruiting agonists with no G protein activation. Compound 7p is metabolically stable with brain exposure in mice. GPR27 is linked to insulin production and secretion, lipid metabolism, neuronal plasticity and L-lactate homeostasis.

citation: Whole-genome sequencing reveals an association between small genomic deletions and an increased risk of developing Parkinson's disease (PMID: 36869069)
sample_size: 310 PD and 100 controls (primary); 100 PD and 100 controls (independent)
summary: Clustered small genomic deletions in the GPR27 region, which has high enhancer signals, were most closely associated with Parkinson's disease in Korean cohorts. GPR27 is brain-specifically expressed, and GPR27 copy number loss was associated with upregulated SNCA and downregulated dopamine neurotransmitter pathways.

citation: Discovery of three novel G-protein-coupled receptor genes (PMID: 9479505)
summary: GPR27 was cloned as an intronless ORF encoding a 379-aa GPCR. Its transcripts were detected in several areas of human and rat CNS.

citation: Integrative Brain Transcriptome Analysis Reveals Region-Specific and Broad Molecular Changes in Shank3-Overexpressing Mice (PMID: 30233305)
summary: Gpr27 mRNA decreased in the cortex and striatum of Shank3-overexpressing mice. In cultured neurons, Gpr27 mRNA levels were modulated by neuronal activity.

citation: GPR27 Regulates Hepatocellular Carcinoma Progression via MAPK/ERK Pathway (PMID: 35330739)
summary: GPR27 knockdown in HCC cells inhibited proliferation, colony formation and viability and induced S-phase arrest. Overexpression had the opposite effects. GPR27 acts via the MAPK/ERK pathway, as shown by RNA-seq and a mouse xenograft model.

citation: GPR27 expression correlates with prognosis and tumor progression in gliomas (PMID: 38638156)
summary: In TCGA data, GPR27 expression was negatively correlated with glioma WHO grade and higher in IDH-mutant and 1p/19q co-deleted tumors. Lower expression correlated with poorer survival, and GPR27 inhibited glioma cell growth in cellular experiments.

citation: Wang et al. 2021 - High Expression of Annexin A9 Promotes Cell Proliferation and Migration in Gastric Cancer via the TGF-β Signaling Pathway (PMID: 34587407)
summary: ANXA9 is upregulated in gastric cancer tissues and cells and predicts unfavorable prognosis. Overexpression in HGC-27 cells increased migration, colony formation and S/G2 phase entry, while knockdown in MGC-803 cells suppressed growth and migration. ANXA9 altered EMT markers and SMAD2/3 and p-SMAD2/3 distribution, implicating the TGF-β/SMAD pathway.

citation: Annexin A9 promotes cell proliferation by regulating the Wnt signaling pathway in colorectal cancer (PMID: 37349657)
summary: ANXA9 is elevated in CRC tissue and cells, and high expression is associated with shorter survival. Knockdown inhibited proliferation, invasion and migration and caused cell cycle arrest. Genes co-expressed with ANXA9 were enriched in Wnt signaling, ANXA9 deletion suppressed proliferation through Wnt, and Wnt activation reversed this effect.

citation: Annexin A9 promotes invasion and metastasis of colorectal cancer and predicts poor prognosis (PMID: 29393380)
summary: ANXA9 protein is higher in CRC tissue than in adjacent mucosa and is an independent risk factor for survival. It is associated with invasion depth and lymph node metastasis. siRNA knockdown in HCT116 cells reduced viability, migration and invasion, downregulated ADAM17 and MMP9, and upregulated TIMP-1 and E-cadherin.

citation: ANXA9 facilitates S100A4 and promotes breast cancer progression through modulating STAT3 pathway (PMID: 38609357)
summary: ANXA9 is highly expressed in metastatic breast cancer. It mediates S100A4 and regulates the AKT/mTOR/STAT3 and p53/Bcl-2 apoptosis pathways. ANXA9 also transfers S100A4 into the tumor microenvironment and promotes secretion of IL-6, IL-8, CCL2 and CCL5, acting through self-phosphorylation at Ser2 and Thr69. Knockdown suppressed xenograft growth and lung metastasis in vivo.

citation: Exosome-derived ANXA9 functions as an oncogene in breast cancer (PMID: 37294149)
summary: ANXA9 is expressed about 1.5-2-fold higher in breast cancer tissue than in normal tissue and is highest in luminal subtypes. It is secreted in tumor-derived exosomes. Silencing reduced colony formation (~30%), migration (~65%) and invasion (~68%), and halved xenograft tumor size.

citation: miR-186-ANXA9 signaling inhibits tumorigenesis in breast cancer (PMID: 37841425)
summary: ANXA9 is a direct target of miR-186-5p, confirmed by luciferase reporter assay, qRT-PCR and western blot, and the two are inversely correlated in breast tumors. ANXA9 knockdown phenocopied miR-186-5p overexpression, and ANXA9 re-expression rescued the apoptosis. The miR-186-5p effect involved decreased Bcl-2 and increased p53.

citation: Hsa-miR-105-1 Regulates Cisplatin-Resistance in Ovarian Carcinoma Cells by Targeting ANXA9 (PMID: 33680718)
summary: ANXA9 is a verified target of miR-105-1 by dual luciferase assay. ANXA9 is upregulated in cisplatin-resistant ovarian cancer cells, where miR-105-1 is downregulated. miR-105-1 mimics lowered ANXA9, raised P53, P21 and Bax, lowered E2F1 and Bcl-2, and restored cisplatin sensitivity.

citation: Knockdown of sulfotransferase 2B1 suppresses cell migration, invasion and promotes apoptosis in ovarian carcinoma cells via targeting annexin A9 (PMID: 38777329)
summary: SULT2B1 binds ANXA9 by co-immunoprecipitation and regulates its expression in SKOV3 ovarian cancer cells. ANXA9 deficiency mimicked SULT2B1 silencing, reducing migration and invasion and increasing apoptosis. ANXA9 overexpression reversed the effects of SULT2B1 knockdown.

citation: ERα and ERβ Homodimers in the Same Cellular Context Regulate Distinct Transcriptomes and Functions (PMID: 35872983)
summary: In MCF7 cells expressing ERβ only, ChIP-based work showed ERβ binds cis-regulatory chromatin of ANXA9, which is proposed as a direct, ERβ-specific migration-related target.

citation: Frequent Alteration of Annexin A9 and A10 in HPV-Negative Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinomas (PMID: 30744186)
summary: ANXA9 is downregulated in 42% of HPV-negative HNSCC tumors compared with normal epithelium. Expression is associated with oropharyngeal location and histological differentiation grade.

citation: Integrating single-cell RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics reveals MDK-NCL dependent immunosuppressive environment in endometrial carcinoma (PMID: 37081869)
sample_size: 33,162 cells from 5 scRNA-seq datasets, 1 ST dataset, 569 TCGA-UCEC RNA-seq samples
summary: Cell-cell communication analysis of scRNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics placed NCL as the receptor in the MK (midkine) pathway. MDK-NCL signaling from malignant epithelial cells to endothelial cells was confirmed between spatial neighbors. NCL expression was inversely correlated with ImmuneScore in TCGA and GEO data.

citation: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics integration reveals FAM49B promotes tumor-associated macrophages polarization in colorectal cancer via the MK pathway (PMID: 41246334)
sample_size: 33 scRNA-seq samples from 16 CRC patients, 2 paired ST samples
summary: In colorectal cancer, MDK-NCL signaling from High_FAM49B epithelial cells to macrophages drives TAM polarization. NCL upregulation accompanied the CXCL3+ to SPP1+ TAM transition in pseudotime analysis, and NCL+ TAMs co-localized with MDK+ epithelial cells spatially. FAM49B knockdown reduced MDK expression.

citation: Integrative single-cell and spatial transcriptomics analysis reveals MDK-NCL pathway's role in shaping the immunosuppressive environment of lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 40396179)
sample_size: TCGA-LUAD plus in-house paired tumor/normal cohort
significance: Significant upregulation in tumor vs normal (reported as significant)
summary: NCL and MDK mRNA and protein were significantly upregulated in LUAD tumors compared with normal tissue, validated by qPCR and western blot in an in-house cohort. MDK-NCL signaling was enriched at the tumor-immune interface. High MDK-NCL expression correlated with reduced immune infiltration, higher TMB and MSI, higher PD-1 and CTLA-4, and poorer survival.

citation: Repurposing AS1411 for constructing ANM-PROTACs (PMID: 38657608)
summary: NCL is a membrane-nucleus shuttling protein recognized by the AS1411 aptamer, and it forms a complex with the E3 ligase MDM2. AS1411 anchoring of the NCL-MDM2 complex was used to recruit MDM2 and degrade STAT3, c-Myc, p53-R175H and AR-V7 in tumor cells and in vivo.

citation: Phase separation of circCHD6-encoded 216aa protein promotes colorectal cancer metastasis (PMID: 41120080)
summary: circCHD6-216aa binds nucleolin and stabilizes NCL's phase-separated nuclear condensates. This promotes NCL-dependent transcription of CD44 and drives CRC metastasis.

citation: NF-κB1 p50 stabilizes HIF-1α protein through suppression of ATG7-dependent autophagy (PMID: 36575197)
summary: In p50-/- cells under arsenic exposure, NCL protein translation increased. NCL binds Sp1 mRNA and stabilizes it, which raises ATG7 transcription and autophagy. miR-494 targets the NCL 3'-UTR to inhibit its translation.

citation: Nucleolin loss of function leads to aberrant Fibroblast Growth Factor signaling and craniofacial anomalies (PMID: 35762670)
summary: ncl-/- zebrafish show craniofacial anomalies with reduced rRNA synthesis and p53-dependent apoptosis. NCL also stabilizes fgf8a mRNA, so loss shortens its half-life and disrupts Fgf signaling, Sox9a-mediated chondrogenesis and Runx2-mediated osteogenesis. Exogenous FGF8 rescued the phenotype.

citation: Aptamer-based approaches to detect nucleolin in prostate cancer (PMID: 33676639)
summary: NCL protein was markedly higher in PBMC lysates of prostate cancer patients (mean 626.1 pg/mL) than in healthy controls (mean 198.5 pg/mL), with greater levels in advanced stages. The modified AS1411-N5 G-quadruplex aptamer bound NCL with KD of about 138 nM.

citation: Targeting epigenetic pathway with gold nanoparticles for acute myeloid leukemia therapy (PMID: 29554483)
summary: NCL was identified as part of an NCL/miR-221/NFκB/DNMT1 axis that promotes aggressive AML. Targeting it with AS1411 and anti-miR-221 nanoparticles reduced DNMT1 and global DNA methylation, restored p15INK4B and p27Kip1, blocked proliferation and clonogenicity, and extended survival in an AML animal model.

citation: ASHG 2011 - Genome-wide association analyses in up to 181,171 individuals reveal 14 new loci associated with heart rate
summary: A heart rate-associated variant was associated with NCL transcript levels in blood (eQTL), which makes NCL one of 11 nearby transcripts implicated at the heart rate loci.

citation: Pathogenic XPO1 variants cause a dominant neurodevelopmental disorder (PMID: 40819229)
variant_detail: Putative loss-of-function de novo XPO1 variants (nonsense/frameshift/splice; specific notations not given in abstract); about 11 individuals
phenotype: neurodevelopmental disorder; overlapping phenotype across the cohort (details not given in abstract)
diagnostic_reason: De novo variants in individuals with an overlapping phenotype gathered through matchmaking; Drosophila knockdown showed developmental defects and impaired habituation learning; XPO1 is deleted in 2p15p16.1 microdeletion syndrome

citation: Pathogenic XPO1 variants cause a dominant neurodevelopmental disorder (PMID: 40819229)
variant_detail: De novo XPO1 missense variants (10 variants; specific notations not given in abstract)
phenotype: neurodevelopmental disorder; overlapping phenotype across the cohort (details not given in abstract)
diagnostic_reason: De novo variants in individuals with an overlapping phenotype gathered through matchmaking; Drosophila knockdown showed developmental defects and impaired habituation learning; XPO1 is deleted in 2p15p16.1 microdeletion syndrome

citation: Pathogenic XPO1 variants cause a dominant neurodevelopmental disorder (PMID: 40819229)
variant_detail: De novo XPO1 in-frame deletion (1 variant; notation not given in abstract)
phenotype: neurodevelopmental disorder
diagnostic_reason: De novo variants in individuals with an overlapping phenotype gathered through matchmaking; Drosophila knockdown showed developmental defects and impaired habituation learning; XPO1 is deleted in 2p15p16.1 microdeletion syndrome

citation: ASHG 2015 - Molecular and clinical delineation of the 2p15-16.1 microdeletion syndrome
variant_detail: 105 kb 2p15p16.1 microdeletion including only XPO1 and the distal end of USP34 (prenatal case and one postnatal case)
phenotype: dysmorphic facial features; brain structural abnormalities; cognitive impairment
diagnostic_reason: Small overlapping deletion containing only XPO1 and distal USP34 in patients with a phenotype overlapping 2p15p16.1 deletion syndrome

citation: ASHG 2016 - Driver genes for 2p15p16.1 microdeletion syndrome identified using clinical, genomic and functional analysis
variant_detail: 2p15p16.1 microdeletions of varying size including XPO1 (with USP34, BCL11A, REL in various combinations)
phenotype: intellectual disability; microcephaly; hypotonia; delayed growth; craniofacial features; digital anomalies
diagnostic_reason: Deletion of XPO1 gave reduced protein expression in patient LCLs and nuclear accumulation of the cargo rpS5; xpo1a knockdown in zebrafish caused microcephaly and developmental abnormalities
center_country: Canada (University of British Columbia) and collaborators in USA/UK

citation: Exome analysis links kidney malformations to developmental disorders and reveals causal genes (PMID: 40774958)
variant_detail: Rare damaging XPO1 variants (not specified in abstract) in CAKUT cases
phenotype: congenital anomalies of the kidneys and urinary tract (CAKUT)
diagnostic_reason: XPO1 identified as one of 40 candidate CAKUT genes through enrichment of rare damaging variants in constrained genes

citation: Nuclear export inhibitors avert progression in preclinical models of inflammatory demyelination (PMID: 25706475)
phenotype: Xpo1 knockdown in cultured neurons was neuroprotective, mirroring the effect of pharmacological CRM1 inhibition; Pharmacological CRM1 inhibitors attenuated disease progression in murine demyelination models, including when started after onset of paralysis; CRM1 inhibitors decreased immune cell proliferation, with nuclear accumulation of cell cycle inhibitors; CRM1 inhibitors preserved cytoskeletal integrity in demyelinated axons; CRM1 inhibitors were neuroprotective in the kainic acid model of axonal damage; In neurons, CRM1 inhibitors prevented nuclear export of molecules associated with axonal damage and retained neuroprotective transcription factors
organism: mouse (cultured neurons; in vivo work used pharmacological CRM1 inhibitors, not genetic knockout)

citation: Pathogenic XPO1 variants cause a dominant neurodevelopmental disorder (PMID: 40819229)
sample_size: 22 individuals with de novo XPO1 variants
summary: Ubiquitous and neuron-specific XPO1 knockdown in Drosophila impaired development. GABAergic neuron-specific knockdown impaired habituation learning. De novo XPO1 variants (half putative LoF, half missense or in-frame deletion) in 22 individuals define a dominant monogenic neurodevelopmental disorder.

citation: ASHG 2011 - Functional characterization of the 2p15-16 microdeletion
summary: XPO1 RNAi knockdown in C. elegans causes early embryonic lethality. An XPO1::GFP transgene is expressed ubiquitously throughout development and in adults. XPO1 lies in the minimal deleted region of the 2p15-16 microdeletion.

citation: ASHG 2011 - Functional characterization of the 2p15-16 microdeletion
summary: XPO1 is expressed in adult mouse brain, gut and lung. In human fetal brain it shows mild positivity in immature ependyma and Cajal-Retzius cells. Whole-genome expression showed no copy-number-related reduction of XPO1 in patient samples.

citation: ASHG 2016 - Driver genes for 2p15p16.1 microdeletion syndrome identified using clinical, genomic and functional analysis
summary: XPO1 is dosage sensitive, with reduced protein in patient lymphoblast lines. XPO1 deletion co-segregated with nuclear accumulation of the export cargo rpS5. Zebrafish xpo1a knockdown caused microcephaly, dysmorphic body, growth defects and brain abnormalities, implicating XPO1 as a driver gene.

citation: Exportin-1 functions as an adaptor for transcription factor-mediated docking of chromatin at the nuclear pore complex (PMID: 40068679)
summary: In yeast, Crm1/Xpo1 binds Gcn4 and Nup2 directly and co-occupies enhancers with Nups. Crm1 inhibition blocks Nup2-genome interaction. The Crm1-Gcn4 interaction needs neither Ran-GTP nor the NES-binding site, and Crm1/Ran-GTP stimulate Gcn4 DNA binding.

citation: Nuclear export of R-loop by the DDX1 and XPO1 complex promotes senescence-associated secretory phenotype and inflammaging (PMID: 42303864)
summary: An XPO1-DDX1 complex is essential for nuclear export of R-loops into cytoplasmic chromatin fragments in senescent cells, activating cGAS-STING and the SASP. XPO1 inhibition with KPT-330 blocked R-loop export, attenuated the SASP and inflammation, and extended healthspan.

citation: XPO1-dependency of DEK::NUP214 leukemia (PMID: 40148556)
summary: XPO1 deletion in DEK::NUP214 FKH-1 cells showed strong dependency. XPO1 co-localizes with DEK::NUP214 at chromatin, and eltanexor disrupted this, down-regulating cell-cycle and self-renewal targets. Eltanexor delayed leukemia in a PDX model (median 377 vs 244 days).

citation: Impaired nucleocytoplasmic transport in SOD1-mediated ALS (PMID: 41691309)
summary: Mutant SOD1 disrupts nuclear import and export and causes cytosolic accumulation of XPO1 and RanGAP1. AAV-mediated reduction of mutant SOD1 restored nuclear XPO1 localization in transgenic mice. Similar changes appeared in patient fibroblasts and postmortem spinal cord.

citation: Function of Nup98 subtypes and their fusion proteins, Nup98-TopIIβ and Nup98-SETBP1 in nuclear-cytoplasmic transport (PMID: 28392395)
summary: Nup98-TopIIβ and Nup98-SETBP1 partially co-localize with XPO1 and full-length Nup98, and negatively regulate XPO1-mediated protein export.

citation: Mutant NPM1 Maintains the Leukemic State through HOX Expression (PMID: 30205049)
summary: XPO1 mediates cytoplasmic export of mutant NPM1c. XPO1 inhibition relocalizes NPM1c to the nucleus, down-regulates HOX genes, promotes differentiation of AML cells and prolongs survival of Npm1-mutated leukemic mice.

citation: Exportin 1 (XPO1) Expression and Effectiveness of XPO1 Inhibitor Against Canine Lymphoma Cell Lines (PMID: 40872651)
summary: XPO1 mRNA and protein are highly expressed in 17-71, CLBL-1, CLC, CLGL-90 and UL-1 canine lymphoma lines, and moderately in GL-1, Ema and Nody-1. KPT-335 inhibited growth in all lines (IC50 89.8-418 nM), with no correlation between XPO1 level and drug efficacy.

citation: 2025 - Loss of ING3 in the Prostate Leads to Activation of DNA Damage Repair Markers (PMID: 40149370)
phenotype: Prostate-specific Ing3 knockout (PB-Cre4) showed mosaic gene deletion, with recombination efficiency of ~15-30% across the anterior, dorsolateral and ventral lobes; Increased γH2AX and 53BP1 DNA-damage markers by immunohistochemistry; No gross anatomical abnormalities; No prostate intraepithelial neoplasia (PIN) lesions or malignant transformation; Low ING3 expression in prostate, consistent with an Ing3-LacZ reporter allele; Confirmed the embryonic lethal phenotype of homozygous Ing3 null mice, rescued by ectopic ING3 expression

citation: 2021 - Knockdown screening of chromatin binding and regulatory proteins in zebrafish identified Suz12b as a regulator of tfpia and an antithrombotic drug target (PMID: 34315984)
phenotype: ing3 knockdown (in a 3-gene piggyback screen) increased tfpia mRNA levels; Simultaneous knockdown of brd7, ing2, ing3, ing4 and suz12b increased tfpia mRNA; Knockdown of these genes, individually and together, prolonged the time to occlude the caudal vessel after laser injury (antithrombotic phenotype)

citation: 2025 - Knockout of the ING5 epigenetic regulator confirms roles in stem cell maintenance and tumor suppression in vivo (PMID: 39787145) [ING3 knockout described as background, citing ref 27]
phenotype: Ing3-null mice did not survive past E10.5; Embryos showed severe growth retardation; Failure of neural tube closure

citation: Loss of Ing3 Expression Results in Growth Retardation and Embryonic Death (PMID: 31905726)
summary: A mouse line with an UbC-mCherry cassette inserted into the Ing3 locus lacks ING3 protein. Homozygous mutants die in utero, with growth retardation at E10.5, neural tube closure defects, no closed primary brain vesicles, and a lack of ectodermal differentiation. ING3 is a core subunit of the minimal NuA4 HAT complex (EAF6, EPC1, ING3, TIP60), and these data show it is essential for embryonic and brain development.

citation: ING3 protein expression profiling in normal human tissues suggest its role in cellular growth and self-renewal (PMID: 25819753)
summary: A new monoclonal antibody that recognizes human and mouse ING3 showed highest expression in small intestine, bone marrow and epidermis, which are rapidly renewing tissues. ING3 was also higher in proliferating than in quiescent epithelial cells, which suggests a role in growth and self-renewal.

citation: Immunohistochemical profile of ING3 protein in normal and cancerous tissues (PMID: 28454301)
summary: ING3 was mainly cytoplasmic in normal mouse and human tissues, with nuclear staining in some epithelia. Staining was strong in stomach, skin and cervix and weak in brain, liver, testis and prostate. ING3-positive cases made up 35.5% of 1,194 tumours, most often ovarian (59.2%), endometrial (47.9%), breast and cervical, and least often renal, hepatocellular and esophageal carcinoma.

citation: Human ex vivo prostate tissue model system identifies ING3 as an oncoprotein (PMID: 29381681)
summary: ING3 overexpression stimulated proliferation in ex vivo prostate tissue and transformed normal human dermal fibroblasts. ING3 was elevated in prostate cancer, where it correlated with poorer survival. Knockdown impaired proliferation of breast, ovarian and prostate cancer cells. ING3 associates with chromatin modifiers and H3K4me3 at transcription start sites to control a cell-cycle gene network, which points to an oncogenic role.

citation: ING3 promotes UV-induced apoptosis via Fas/caspase-8 pathway in melanoma cells (PMID: 16520380)
summary: UV irradiation rapidly induced ING3 mRNA and protein. ING3 overexpression enhanced UV-induced apoptosis independently of p53, increased cleavage of Bid and caspases-8, -9 and -3, and upregulated Fas. Apoptosis was blocked by caspase-8 or Fas inhibition, and ING3 knockdown reduced UV-induced apoptosis.

citation: ING3 is essential for asymmetric cell division during mouse oocyte maturation (PMID: 24066152)
summary: ING3 localizes to the germinal vesicle in oocytes and to the cytoplasm after GVBD. siRNA knockdown caused symmetric division, with no actin cap or cortical granule-free domain and failed spindle migration. mTOR and its downstream genes Cdc42, Rac1 and RhoA were downregulated, so ING3 may act through the mTOR pathway.

citation: ASHG 2018 - Genome-scale capture C promoter interaction analysis implicates novel effector genes at GWAS loci for bone mineral density
summary: Promoter capture-C and ATAC-seq in human osteoblasts linked BMD GWAS variants at the WNT16-CPED1 locus to the ING3 promoter. siRNA knockdown of ING3 in primary MSC-derived osteoblasts strongly impaired osteoblast differentiation, with reduced ALP and no mineral deposition. ING3 is thus implicated as an effector gene for bone mineral density.

citation: A Novel Splice Variant of the Inhibitor of Growth 3 Lacks the Plant Homeodomain and Regulates Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition in Prostate Cancer Cells (PMID: 34439818)
summary: A splice variant lacking exon 11 and the PHD (ING3Δex11) was found in LNCaP cells and patient specimens.
