Unlike full-length ING3, it induces EMT markers and alters 3D spheroid morphology, so the PHD appears to inhibit EMT. ING3 knockdown also induced EMT markers and caused senescence with cell cycle arrest. ING3 is described as an AR co-activator with oncogenic properties in prostate cancer.

citation: Downregulation of nuclear ING3 expression and translocalization to cytoplasm promotes tumorigenesis and progression in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) (PMID: 31886514)
significance: significant correlations reported (p-values not given in abstract)
summary: Nuclear ING3 was lower in HNSCC than in dysplasia or normal epithelium, while cytoplasmic ING3 was higher and associated with lymph node metastasis and 14-3-3η expression. Nuclear ING3 correlated positively with p300, p21 and acetylated p53, which suggests that ING3 cooperates with p300 to acetylate p53.

citation: Downregulation of ING3 mRNA expression predicts poor prognosis in head and neck cancer (PMID: 18081876)
significance: significant in multivariate analysis (p-value not given in abstract)
summary: About half of head and neck tumours showed ING3 mRNA downregulation relative to matched normal tissue. Low ING3 was an independent predictor of poor overall survival, with 5-year survival of about 35% versus about 60% for normal to high ING3.

citation: De Novo Deletion in the 12q24.23q24.31 Chromosomal Region Causing a Neurodevelopmental Syndrome in a Female Saudi Patient: A Case Report (PMID: 40018479)
variant_detail: De novo heterozygous ~6.6 Mb deletion at 12q24.23q24.31 spanning 122 genes, including MSI1. This is a contiguous-gene deletion, and MSI1 is not singled out as causal.
phenotype: refractory epilepsy; spasticity in all limbs; global developmental delay; intellectual disability; widely separated eyes (hypertelorism); small nasal tip; congenital heart defects (tricuspid atresia, single ventricle); clubbing of fingers and toes; overlapping toes
diagnostic_reason: De novo 6.6 Mb deletion in 12q24.23q24.31, a region previously associated with neurodevelopmental abnormalities. The deletion was attributed to the whole region, not to MSI1 specifically.

citation: Msi1 and Msi2 conditional KO study - The Musashi proteins MSI1 and MSI2 are required for photoreceptor morphogenesis and vision in mice (PMID: 33168629)
phenotype: Pan-retinal and rod-specific double Msi1/Msi2 deletion abolished the light response; Severely disrupted photoreceptor outer segment morphology; Ciliary defects; Retinal neuronal degeneration with complete photoreceptor loss within 6 months; Loss of photoreceptor-specific exon usage in transcripts needed for outer segment morphogenesis, ciliogenesis and synaptic transmission

citation: Kawahara et al. 2010 - Neural RNA-binding protein Musashi1 controls midline crossing of precerebellar neurons through posttranscriptional regulation of Robo3/Rig-1 expression (PMID: 20696379)
phenotype: Robo3 protein dramatically reduced in precerebellar neurons, with Robo3 mRNA unchanged; Severely impaired axonal midline crossing of precerebellar neurons; Impaired neuronal migration of precerebellar neurons; Phenocopies Robo3-deficient mice

citation: Musashi-1-type 2 deiodinase pathway regulates astrocyte proliferation (PMID: 38879014)
phenotype: Increased D2 (Dio2) expression in the cortex of mice lacking MSI1 protein; MSI1 knockdown in primary mouse cortical astrocytes increased D2 expression and slowed cell proliferation by 56%

citation: Characterization of the RNA-binding protein Musashi1 in zebrafish (PMID: 22429745)
phenotype: Morpholino knockdown of zmsi1 in one-cell stage embryos frequently caused aberrant formation of the central nervous system

citation: Musashi-1, an RNA-binding protein, is indispensable for survival of photoreceptors (PMID: 18662689)
phenotype: Photoreceptor degeneration; Lack of the visual cycle protein RPE65 in the microvilli of RPE cells

citation: Musashi-dependent mRNA translational activation is mediated through association with the Scd6/Like-sm family member, LSM14B (PMID: 40211036)
phenotype: Antisense knockdown of MSI1/2 in Xenopus oocytes abolished oocyte maturation (no GVBD); LSM14B knockdown likewise blocked oocyte maturation; LSM14B mediates Musashi1-dependent translational activation required for maturation

citation: Vaidyanathan et al. ASHG 2012 - Simplified sample preparation and streamlined library preparation method for deep sequencing Ribosome Protected mRNA Fragments
summary: Msi1 is a conserved RNA-binding protein highly expressed in cancers including glioblastoma. shRNA knockdown of Msi1 in U251 glioblastoma cells, followed by ribosome profiling, was used to identify direct mRNA targets and the translational control Msi1 exerts.

citation: MSI1, a negative regulator of the RAS-cAMP pathway in Saccharomyces cerevisiae (PMID: 2554329)
summary: Yeast MSI1 was isolated as a high-copy suppressor of ira1 heat-shock sensitivity and encodes a WD-repeat protein homologous to G-protein beta subunits. Overexpression suppressed ira1 and RAS2Val19 phenotypes (heat-shock sensitivity, sporulation defect) and lowered elevated cAMP, but did not suppress bcy1, indicating MSI1 is a negative regulator of RAS-cAMP signaling.

citation: CAC3(MSI1) suppression of RAS2(G19V) is independent of chromatin assembly factor I and mediated by NPR1 (PMID: 11238915)
summary: Yeast Cac3p/Msi1p, an RbAp48 homolog and CAF-I component, suppresses RAS/cAMP signaling independently of CAC1/CAC2 and chromatin assembly. It localizes to nucleus and cytoplasm, associates with the kinase Npr1p, and suppresses RAS by sequestering Npr1p, possibly through increased ubiquitination of an Npr1p substrate.

citation: MSI1 and HDA6 function interdependently to control flowering time via chromatin modifications (PMID: 34807487)
summary: Arabidopsis MSI1, a PRC2 subunit, interacts with histone deacetylase HDA6 in vitro and in vivo. They bind FLC, MAF4 and MAF5 chromatin interdependently, repressing these genes through H3K9 deacetylation and H3K27me3 to control flowering time.

citation: Arabidopsis MSI1 is required for negative regulation of the response to drought stress (PMID: 19825648)
summary: Transcriptional profiling of MSI1-depleted (msi1-cs) Arabidopsis showed up-regulation of ABA-responsive drought/salt-stress genes. MSI1 binds chromatin of the drought-inducible target RD20, suggesting a role in negatively regulating drought response.

citation: PcG Proteins MSI1 and BMI1 Function Upstream of miR156 to Regulate Aerial Tuber Formation in Potato (PMID: 31427464)
summary: In potato, StMSI1 (PRC2) overexpression raised miR156 and caused aerial tubers and reduced below-ground tuber yield. StMSI1-OE repressed StBMI1-1/3 through H3K27me3 and activated miR156 through H3K4me3, and altered auxin, brassinosteroid and cytokinin gene expression. StMSI1 levels increased in stolons under short days.

citation: The Msi1-mTOR pathway drives the pathogenesis of mammary and extramammary Paget's disease (PMID: 32457396)
summary: MSI1 is ectopically overexpressed in basal epithelial cells of human Paget's disease skin. Msi1 overexpression in mouse epidermal basal layer phenocopies the disease through mTOR-driven keratinocyte-to-Paget-like cell conversion, which rapamycin rescued.

citation: Cycling Stem Cells Are Radioresistant and Regenerate the Intestine (PMID: 32726617)
summary: Lineage tracing with an Msi1 reporter marks cells just above Lgr5-high cells in intestinal crypts that are DNA damage resistant. Most are heterogeneous cycling ISCs with low Lgr5 expression that regenerate the epithelium after radiation and preferentially produce Paneth cells.

citation: Alternative splicing of ALDOA confers tamoxifen resistance in breast cancer (PMID: 39164523)
sample_size: 9 pairs of primary and relapse breast tumors
summary: MSI1 directly interacts with ALDOA mRNA and mediates inclusion of exon 7.2 in its 5'UTR, increasing translation, ALDOA protein, mTOR activity and tamoxifen resistance. High MSI1 expression is associated with poor prognosis in patients on endocrine therapy.

citation: Musashi-1 and miR-147 Precursor Interaction Mediates Synergistic Oncogenicity Induced by Co-Infection of Two Avian Retroviruses (PMID: 36291177)
summary: ALV-J and REV structural proteins synergistically induce MSI1, which binds pri-miR-147 through its RNA-binding site and blocks miR-147 maturation. This relieves inhibition of NF-κB/KIAA1199/EGFR signaling, suppressing senescence and activating EMT.

citation: ASHG 2017 - ARID4A de novo variants identified by exome sequencing among individuals with neurodevelopmental disorders (Monaghan et al.)
variant_detail: One frameshift variant (specific notation not provided); de novo
phenotype: developmental delay; behavior abnormalities; variable features across cohort: autism, developmental regression, tone abnormalities, intellectual disability, brain anomalies, facial dysmorphism
diagnostic_reason: De novo on trio-based exome sequencing (one possible paternal mosaic); missense variants had damaging in-silico predictions and affected evolutionarily conserved residues

citation: ASHG 2017 - ARID4A de novo variants identified by exome sequencing among individuals with neurodevelopmental disorders (Monaghan et al.)
variant_detail: Five missense variants (specific notation not provided); four confirmed de novo, one possibly paternally mosaic (not confirmed de novo)
phenotype: developmental delay (6/6); behavior abnormalities (6/6); developmental regression (3/6); autism (4/6); tone abnormalities (4/6); intellectual disability; brain anomalies on MRI (thin corpus callosum, absent septum pellucidum, holoprosencephaly in one; pontocerebellar atrophy in another); facial dysmorphism (2 patients)
diagnostic_reason: De novo on trio-based exome sequencing (one possible paternal mosaic); missense variants had damaging in-silico predictions and affected evolutionarily conserved residues

citation: Zhang et al. 2022 - A novel heterozygous missense variant of the ARID4A gene identified in Han Chinese families with schizophrenia-diagnosed siblings that interferes with DNA-binding activity (PMID: 35365808)
variant_detail: c.1231C>G, p.His411Asp
phenotype: schizophrenia (affected siblings in Han Chinese families)
diagnostic_reason: Identified by WES in families with schizophrenia-diagnosed siblings; functional studies showed a less compact ARID domain conformation, weaker dsDNA binding, and disrupted G1 cell cycle arrest with increased proliferation

citation: Deciphering the genetic basis of developmental language disorder in children without intellectual disability, autism or apraxia of speech (PMID: 39948625)
variant_detail: NM_002892.4 c.1539dup, p.(Glu514ArgfsTer3)
phenotype: severe developmental language disorder (without ID, ASD or CAS)
diagnostic_reason: Frameshift variant in a gene intolerant to LoF variation, with no established Mendelian disorder yet; listed as a candidate variant and not classified as pathogenic

citation: The genetic landscape of autism spectrum disorder in an ancestrally diverse cohort (PMID: 39632905)
variant_detail: chr14:58353693 A>C, p.E564A (de novo)
phenotype: autism spectrum disorder
diagnostic_reason: De novo nonsynonymous variant in a candidate ASD gene (family MC_172_3)

citation: Wu et al. 2013 - ARID4A and ARID4B regulate male fertility, a functional link to the AR and RB pathways (PMID: 23487765)
phenotype: progressive loss of male fertility; hypogonadism; seminal vesicle agenesis/hypodysplasia; spermatogenic arrest at meiotic spermatocyte and postmeiotic haploid spermatid stages; increased permeability of the blood-testis barrier (seminiferous tubules); Sertoli cell dysfunction recapitulating Sertoli-specific AR and RB knockout phenotypes; altered expression of AR- and RB-responsive genes
knockout_type: full knockout (Arid4a-/- combined with Arid4b heterozygous knockout; Arid4a-/-Arid4b+/-)

citation: Wu et al. 2008 - Identification of chromatin remodeling genes Arid4a and Arid4b as leukemia suppressor genes (PMID: 18728284)
phenotype: ineffective hematopoiesis in all lineages in young mice; monocytosis, severe anemia and thrombocytopenia after 5 months of age; bone marrow failure with myelofibrosis; splenomegaly and hepatomegaly; CMML-like myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative disorder; progression to acute myeloid leukemia (5 of 42 Arid4a-/- mice; 10 of 12 Arid4a-/-Arid4b+/- mice); decreased Hoxb3, Hoxb5, Hoxb6 and Hoxb8 expression in bone marrow; reduced FoxP3 expression in Arid4a-/-Arid4b+/- bone marrow; increased histone trimethylation of H3K4, H3K9 and H4K20
significance: Histone trimethylation fold increases: H3K4 32-fold (95% CI 27-32), H3K9 45-fold (95% CI 41-49), H4K20 2.2-fold (95% CI 1.7-2.7); statistical tests two-sided

citation: Hu et al. 2017 - miR-376c promotes carcinogenesis and serves as a plasma marker for gastric carcinoma (PMID: 28486502)
summary: ARID4A is a direct target of miR-376c in gastric carcinoma cells. ARID4A knockdown increased proliferation, migration and anchorage-independent growth, and ARID4A was strongly downregulated in tumor tissue, opposite to miR-376c. This supports a tumor-suppressor role.

citation: Downregulation of ARID4A and ARID4B promote tumor progression and directly regulated by microRNA-30d in patient with prostate cancer (PMID: 29797600)
significance: r=-0.313, P=0.001 (miR-30d vs ARID4A); P=0.005 (Gleason); P=0.012 (PSA failure); P=0.033 (recurrence-free survival)
summary: ARID4A is a miR-30d target and its mRNA is negatively correlated with miR-30d in prostate cancer tissue. It is downregulated in tumors with high Gleason score, PSA failure and short recurrence-free survival. ARID4A knockout promoted PCa cell proliferation, migration and invasion in vitro.

citation: Structural basis for tunable affinity and specificity of LxCxE-dependent protein interactions with the retinoblastoma protein family (PMID: 35716663)
summary: Crystal structures and binding data show that an ARID4A LxCxE peptide binds the p107 pocket domain, alongside HDAC1 and EID1 peptides. This confirms ARID4A as a direct Rb-family-binding transcriptional co-repressor with defined affinity and specificity.

citation: Wu et al. 2006 - Deficiency of Rbbp1/Arid4a and Rbbp1l1/Arid4b alters epigenetic modifications and suppresses an imprinting defect in the PWS/AS domain (PMID: 17043311)
summary: Arid4a was recovered in a gene-trap screen for regulators of Snrpn-EGFP imprinting. It interacts with Arid4b and the Snrpn promoter. In mice, Arid4a-/- with Arid4b+/- reduced H4K20me3, H3K9me3 and DNA methylation at the PWS-IC and suppressed an AS imprinting defect, placing ARID4A in epigenetic complexes regulating PWS/AS imprinting.

citation: AlphaFold-guided structural analyses of nucleosome binding proteins (PMID: 40794873)
summary: An AlphaFold-based screen of more than 7600 human nuclear proteins identified ARID4A and ARID4B as novel nucleosome-binding proteins.

citation: A novel heterozygous missense variant of the ARID4A gene identified in Han Chinese families with schizophrenia-diagnosed siblings that interferes with DNA-binding activity (PMID: 35365808)
sample_size: Han Chinese families with schizophrenia-diagnosed siblings
summary: Whole-exome sequencing found ARID4A p.His411Asp in schizophrenia families. The crystal structure of the PWWP-ARID tandem shows a structural supramodule. The mutant ARID domain is less compact and binds dsDNA more weakly, reduces G0-G1 arrest and increases HEK293T proliferation.

citation: ASHG 2017 - ARID4A de novo variants identified by exome sequencing among individuals with neurodevelopmental disorders
summary: Trio exome sequencing of 11,649 NDD probands found de novo ARID4A variants (one frameshift, five missense) in 6 individuals. All had developmental delay and behavioral abnormalities, and many had autism, tone abnormalities, regression or brain anomalies. A prior 14q23 deletion including ARID4A suggests haploinsufficiency.

citation: ASHG 2014 - Position effects modify gene expression in a ring chromosome 14?
summary: ARID4A was significantly downregulated in blood from a patient with ring chromosome 14 compared with 7 controls, possibly through position effects or nuclear repositioning of the ring chromosome. GeneMania indicated ARID4A is co-expressed with the other studied genes.

citation: Structural basis for the DNA-binding activity of human ARID4B Tudor domain (PMID: 33675746)
summary: The ARID4A N-terminal domain is an interdigitated double Tudor domain with DNA-binding activity. It has higher DNA affinity than the ARID4B Tudor domain, largely because of Leu50 (Glu50 in ARID4B), despite more than 80% sequence identity.

citation: ARID4A and ARID4B regulate male fertility, a functional link to the AR and RB pathways (PMID: 23487765)
summary: Arid4a-/-Arid4b+/- mice show progressive loss of male fertility, hypogonadism, spermatogenic arrest and an impaired blood-testis barrier. Arid4a is expressed mainly in Sertoli cells. ARID4A and ARID4B act as transcriptional coactivators in the AR and RB pathways, regulating AR- and RB-responsive genes.

citation: De novo variants in genes regulating stress granule assembly associate with neurodevelopmental disorders (PMID: 35977029)
variant_detail: De novo variants in G3BP1 (specific variants not given in the abstract), reported as a nominally significant excess among 40,853 individuals with NDDs
phenotype: neurodevelopmental disorder
diagnostic_reason: Nominally significant excess of de novo variants in G3BP1 in a large NDD cohort. G3BP1 is an essential gene in the core stress granule interaction network. NDD-related de novo variants were shown to disrupt the core SG network interaction and SG formation, though this was tested for the newly implicated and known NDD genes in general.

citation: G3BP1 Succinylation at K413 is Critical for Cardiac Function by Modulating PI3K-AKT-mTOR Signal Axis (PMID: 42107065)
variant_detail: De novo G3BP1 p.E411G (described as disrupting succinylation at K413)
phenotype: dilated cardiomyopathy; heart failure
diagnostic_reason: De novo variant in a DCM patient. The variant disrupts succinylation at K413, and the mechanism of excess PI3K-AKT-mTOR activation was supported by functional data in mouse models and in vitro.

citation: Prentzell et al. 2021 - G3BPs tether the TSC complex to lysosomes and suppress mTORC1 signaling (PMID: 33497611)
phenotype: g3bp1 inhibition disturbed neuronal development and function; white matter heterotopia; neuronal hyperactivity; phenotypes consistent with mTORC1 hyperactivity

citation: Liu et al. 2018 - G3BP1 promotes DNA binding and activation of cGAS (PMID: 30510222)
phenotype: G3BP1 deficiency (cells) led to inefficient cGAS DNA binding and reduced cGAS-dependent IFN production; G3BP1 inhibitor EGCG blocked DNA-induced IFN production in vivo; EGCG blunted autoinflammatory responses in an Aicardi-Goutières syndrome mouse model (pharmacological inhibition, not a genetic knockout in the animal)

citation: 2025 - Dysregulation of GTPase-activating protein-binding protein1 in the pathogenesis of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (PMID: 40813380)
phenotype: Hepatocyte-specific G3BP1 knockout male mice had more severe MASLD and MASH; dysregulated autophagy with impaired autophagosome-lysosome fusion (via STX17 and VAMP8 interactions); increased de novo lipogenesis; impaired nuclear translocation of TFE3

citation: Zhang et al. 2023 - Stress granule homeostasis is modulated by TRIM21-mediated ubiquitination of G3BP1 and autophagy-dependent elimination of stress granules (PMID: 36692217)
summary: TRIM21 catalyzes K63-linked ubiquitination of G3BP1, which inhibits G3BP1 LLPS in vitro, and TRIM21 knockdown promotes SG formation. The autophagy receptors SQSTM1/p62 and CALCOCO2/NDP52 directly interact with G3BP1 during arsenite stress and mediate SG elimination.

citation: G3BP1 promotes DNA binding and activation of cGAS (PMID: 30510222)
summary: G3BP1 physically interacts with cGAS and promotes formation of large cGAS-DNA complexes, enhancing DNA binding and IFN production. G3BP1 deficiency impairs cGAS activation. The G3BP1 inhibitor EGCG disrupts G3BP1-cGAS complexes and blunts autoinflammation in an Aicardi-Goutières syndrome mouse model and in patient cells.

citation: Structure-Mediated RNA Decay by UPF1 and G3BP1 (PMID: 32017897)
summary: G3BP1, together with UPF1, is required for a genome-wide decay pathway targeting mRNAs with highly structured 3' UTRs. Depleting G3BP1 increased steady-state levels of structured mRNAs and circular RNAs.

citation: Identification of small molecule inhibitors of G3BP-driven stress granule formation (PMID: 38284934)
summary: Small molecules G3Ia and G3Ib bind a pocket in G3BP1/2 that is also targeted by viral inhibitors. They disrupt RNA-G3BP1-caprin 1 co-condensation in vitro, inhibit SG formation in cells, and dissolve pre-existing SGs across cell types and stressors.

citation: TRIM25 predominately associates with anti-viral stress granules (PMID: 38750080)
summary: TRIM25 co-condenses with the SG core protein G3BP1 in a dsRNA-dependent manner. This enhances TRIM25 ubiquitination activity toward antiviral proteins and activates RIG-I signaling, restraining RNA virus infection.

citation: DCAF7 Acts as A Scaffold to Recruit USP10 for G3BP1 Deubiquitylation and Facilitates Chemoresistance and Metastasis in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma (PMID: 38973296)
summary: DCAF7 scaffolds USP10 and G3BP1, removing K48-linked ubiquitin from G3BP1 Lys76. This stabilizes G3BP1 and promotes SG-like structures in NPC cells. G3BP1 knockdown reversed the SG-like structures and the oncogenic effects of DCAF7.

citation: G3BPs tether the TSC complex to lysosomes and suppress mTORC1 signaling (PMID: 33497611)
summary: G3BP1 and G3BP2 localize to the cytoplasmic surface of lysosomes and anchor the TSC complex there, suppressing mTORC1 activation by amino acids and insulin. G3BP1 deficiency causes mTORC1 hyperactivity phenotypes, and low G3BP1 enhances breast cancer cell motility and correlates with poor patient outcomes. g3bp1 inhibition in zebrafish disturbs neuronal development and function.

citation: Stress granules are shock absorbers that prevent excessive innate immune responses to dsRNA (PMID: 37028415)
summary: Without the SG nucleators G3BP1/2 and UBAP2L, dsRNA triggers excessive RLR-mediated inflammation and immune-mediated apoptosis. This also applies to ADAR1-deficiency-derived host dsRNA, and SGs additionally suppress viral replication independently of RLR signaling.

citation: hnRNPA2B1 represses the disassembly of arsenite-induced stress granules and is essential for male fertility (PMID: 38363675)
summary: hnRNPA2B1 interacts with G3BP1, G3BP2, USP10 and Caprin-1. USP10 deubiquitinates G3BP1, and hnRNPA2B1 depletion weakens the G3BP1-USP10/Caprin-1 interaction and raises G3BP1 ubiquitination under arsenite, accelerating SG disassembly.

citation: G3BP1 modulates SPOP to promote prostate tumorigenesis (PMID: 35252555)
summary: G3BP1 interacts with SPOP, the substrate adaptor of the CUL3-SPOP ubiquitin ligase, and acts as an upstream inhibitor of CUL3-SPOP ligase activity. This promotes prostate cancer.

citation: Ueno et al. 2011 - KIF16B/Rab14 molecular motor complex is critical for early embryonic development by transporting FGF receptor (PMID: 21238925)
phenotype: Rab14-GDP dominant-negative overexpression reproduced the Kif16b/FGFR2 deficiency phenotype; Impaired FGFR transport (Golgi-to-endosome/plasma membrane); Impaired FGF signaling; Defective basement membrane assembly by the primitive endoderm lineage; Impaired epiblast development; In the parallel Kif16b-/- knockout, embryos failed to develop epiblast and primitive endoderm lineages and died at peri-implantation, similar to FGFR2 knockout embryos
knockout_type: other: dominant-negative Rab14 (Rab14-GDP) overexpression in mouse embryos. The Kif16b full knockout, a Rab14 effector/motor, was studied in parallel, and Rab14 itself was not knocked out.

citation: Rab14 promotes Parkin-mediated mitophagy (PMID: 40737294)
summary: Rab14 knockdown produced elongated mitochondria and increased mitochondrial proteins, whereas overexpression increased mitophagy in mito-Keima assays. Rab14-induced mitophagy depends on Parkin, TBK1 and PI3K activity, placing it in the Parkin-dependent mitophagy pathway. TGN-derived Rab14 vesicles form contact sites with mitochondria that require PI(4)KIIIβ.

citation: The endocytic pathway taken by cationic substances requires Rab14 but not Rab5 and Rab7 (PMID: 34731620)
summary: Cell-penetrating peptides, polyamines and homeodomains use an endocytic route to nonacidic Lamp1-positive late endosomes. This route is independent of Rab5 and Rab7 but requires Rab14.

citation: RAB14 GTPase is essential for actin-based asymmetric division during mouse oocyte maturation (PMID: 34323331)
summary: In mouse oocytes, RAB14 localizes to the cortex and spindle periphery. siRNA depletion caused spindle migration defects, large polar bodies (failed asymmetric division) and aberrant Golgi distribution, acting through the ROCK-cofilin pathway. Myc-Rab14 mRNA rescued these defects.

citation: Biogenesis of Rab14-positive endosome buds at Golgi-endosome contacts by the RhoBTB3-SHIP164-Vps26B complex (PMID: 38565878)
summary: Vps26B is a novel Rab14 effector, and Rab14 activity regulates SHIP164 association with early endosomes. SHIP164 depletion leads to enlarged Rab14+ endosomes lacking buds, so the RhoBTB3-SHIP164-Vps26B complex drives Rab14+ endosome budding at Golgi-endosome contacts.

citation: Rab14/MACF2 complex regulates endosomal targeting during cytokinesis (PMID: 33566684)
summary: Rab14 depletion or knockout causes cytokinesis failure or prolonged division, impairs Rab11-endosome recruitment to intracellular bridge microtubules and blocks actin clearance at the abscission site. Rab14 binds the MACF2/CAMSAP3 complex, which affects endosome targeting.

citation: Microscopic and biochemical monitoring of endosomal trafficking and extracellular vesicle secretion in an endogenous in vivo model (PMID: 36103151)
summary: In a Drosophila fat body RNAi model, Rab14 together with the kinesin Klp98A was found to function in extracellular vesicle biogenesis and secretion. Rab11 and Rab35 were the main regulators of EV secretion.

citation: Isolation, sequence identification and tissue expression distribution of three novel porcine genes--RAB14, S35A3 and ITM2A (PMID: 17380425)
summary: Porcine RAB14 encodes a 215-aa protein with 99% identity to human and mouse and 100% to rat. It is highly expressed in fat, lung, spleen and kidney, moderately in large intestine, weakly in small intestine, and barely in muscle and liver.

citation: A genome-wide CRISPR screen defines host determinants of early Brucella infection in human macrophage-like cells (PMID: 42402044)
summary: A genome-wide CRISPR screen in human macrophage-like cells found that RAB14 supports B. abortus and B. ovis infection at a post-entry step. RAB14 was dispensable for Mycobacterium abscessus infection, indicating a pathogen-specific dependency.

citation: Rab14 restricts pathogens by promoting V-ATPase lysosomal delivery to drive lysosomal acidification (PMID: 41771894)
summary: Rab14 is a broad-spectrum restriction factor against bacteria and viruses. Infection raises GTP-bound Rab14, which binds CAMK2D and blocks its phosphorylation of V0a1. This promotes V0a1-COPII binding and ER-to-lysosome V-ATPase trafficking, leading to lysosomal acidification and pathogen clearance (Rab14-CAMK2D-V-ATPase axis).

citation: Targeting CPT1A-mediated fatty acid oxidation sensitizes nasopharyngeal carcinoma to radiation therapy (PMID: 29721083)
summary: Mass spectrometry identified Rab14 as a CPT1A-binding protein, confirmed by immunoprecipitation, immunofluorescence and proximity ligation assay. The interaction promotes fatty acid trafficking from lipid droplets to mitochondria, and Rab14 knockdown attenuated this trafficking and radiation resistance in NPC cells.

citation: ATF2 phosphorylation is a core transcriptional driver of neuron apoptosis (PMID: 40654834)
summary: A genome-wide CRISPRi screen in human neurons identified ATF2 alongside DLK (MAP3K12) and JUN as required for neuronal death. ATF2 phosphorylation by MAP3 kinases drives the pro-apoptotic transcriptional response and JUN upregulation, whereas JUN phosphorylation is dispensable. ATF2 knockdown prevents neuron death in culture and is neuroprotective in in vivo injury models.

citation: RNA-binding protein RCAN1.1L modulates ATF2 mRNA stability to promote mitochondrial fission in acute ischemic stroke (PMID: 42129133)
summary: RCAN1.1L binds nucleotides 2915-2935 of the ATF2 3'UTR and stabilizes ATF2 mRNA. This increases mitochondrial ATF2 (mtATF2), which binds and upregulates FIS1 to drive mitochondrial fission and intrinsic apoptosis in ischemic neurons. An RNA aptamer that disrupts the RCAN1.1L-ATF2 mRNA interaction is neuroprotective.

citation: ATF2/BAP1 Axis Mediates Neuronal Apoptosis After Subarachnoid Hemorrhage via P53 Pathway (PMID: 38965653)
summary: ATF2 binds the BAP1 promoter and regulates BAP1 expression. BAP1 then stabilizes P53 by reducing its proteasomal degradation, promoting neuronal apoptosis after SAH in mice and hemin-treated neurons. This places ATF2 upstream in an ATF2/BAP1/P53 apoptotic pathway.

citation: Regulatory role of the p38 MAPK/ATF2 signaling pathway in visual function and visual cortical plasticity in mice with monocular deprivation (PMID: 37393009)
summary: In the mouse visual cortex after monocular deprivation, p38 MAPK inhibition (SB) lowered phospho-p38 and increased ATF2 and PSD-95 expression. This improved visual function and synaptic plasticity, indicating ATF2 acts downstream of p38 MAPK in cortical plasticity.

citation: Combination of tetrandrine and 3-n-butylphthalide protects against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury via ATF2/TLR4 pathway (PMID: 34591732)
summary: ATF2 overexpression promoted neuronal degeneration in OGD models, and ATF2 transcriptionally activates TLR4. Tetrandrine plus NBP suppressed ATF2 and TLR4 signaling, reducing neuronal apoptosis and inflammation.

citation: ASHG 2014 - Disruption of FMR1, RAI1, MBD5, and TCF4 results in abnormal expression of circadian rhythm genes and sleep disturbances
summary: In SH-SY5Y cells, siRNA knockdown of MBD5, RAI1 and TCF4 altered expression of circadian-related genes including ATF2 and ATF4, alongside CLOCK, PER1 and CRY2. This links ATF2 to circadian pathways disrupted in neurodevelopmental syndromes with sleep disturbance.

citation: ASHG 2013 - MBD5 deletion disrupts circadian gene expression and is associated with sleep disturbance in the 2q23.1 deletion syndrome
summary: Microarray pathway analysis of MBD5 knockdown in SH-SY5Y cells showed dysregulation of circadian rhythm genes including ATF2, ATF4, CLOCK and PER3. This supports ATF2 as a circadian-pathway gene affected by MBD5 loss.

citation: Increased ATF2 expression predicts poor prognosis and inhibits sorafenib-induced ferroptosis in gastric cancer (PMID: 36473315)
summary: ATF2 is upregulated in gastric cancer tissue and predicts poor prognosis. ChIP-Seq and RNA-Seq identified HSPH1 as an ATF2 target, and HSPH1 stabilizes SLC7A11 to suppress sorafenib-induced ferroptosis. ATF2 knockdown enhanced sorafenib sensitivity in xenografts.

citation: ATF2 contributes to cisplatin resistance in non-small cell lung cancer and celastrol induces cisplatin resensitization through inhibition of JNK/ATF2 pathway (PMID: 25359574)
sample_size: matched NSCLC and normal tissues from resected patients
summary: ATF2 mRNA and protein are strongly elevated in NSCLC tumors versus matched normal tissue, and cisplatin-resistant cell lines express high ATF2. Celastrol inhibition of JNK/ATF2/cJUN restored cisplatin response, and ATF2 activation correlated with worse outcome in cisplatin-treated patients.

citation: KIF18B promotes tumor progression in osteosarcoma by activating β-catenin (PMID: 32587775)
summary: KIF18B controls nuclear aggregation of ATF2 in osteosarcoma cells, thereby regulating β-catenin transcription. KIF18B also interacts with APC to regulate β-catenin post-transcriptionally.

citation: First Detection of 1p36 Deletion by Whole-Exome Sequencing in a Tunisian Patient (PMID: 41556146)
variant_detail: Heterozygous interstitial 1p36 deletion, 11.64 Mb, 155 coding genes including MMP23B, GABRD, SKI, PRDM16, KCNAB2, RERE, UBE4B and CASZ1 (detected by WES, confirmed by FISH)
phenotype: intrauterine growth restriction; neonatal epilepsy; craniofacial dysmorphism; congenital heart defect; agenesis of the corpus callosum; severe polymalformative syndrome
diagnostic_reason: Large multigene deletion classified pathogenic per ACMG and confirmed by FISH. CASZ1 is one of many deleted genes, so the phenotype cannot be attributed to CASZ1 alone.

citation: ASHG 2019 - 1p36 deletions: One cytogenetic band, multiple genetic syndromes and disease genes (D.A. Scott et al.)
variant_detail: Terminal and interstitial 1p36 deletions in >200 individuals; deletion/phenotype mapping suggests CASZ1 haploinsufficiency contributes to congenital heart defects (alongside SPEN, UBR4, ELOA, WASF2)
phenotype: congenital heart defects; intellectual disability; seizures; sensorineural hearing loss; cleft lip/palate; cardiomyopathy; renal anomalies
diagnostic_reason: Deletion/phenotype maps and pLI score (>0.8) combined with mouse model data implicate CASZ1 haploinsufficiency in congenital heart defects. No CASZ1-specific patient count is given.

citation: Identification of novel driver risk genes in CNV loci associated with neurodevelopmental disorders (PMID: 38850022)
variant_detail: 1p36.33-p36.32 deletion region encompassing CASZ1 together with SKI, RERE, PRDM16 and others (novel NDD-risk CNV locus)
phenotype: neurodevelopmental disorder / autism spectrum disorder
diagnostic_reason: Meta-analysis of CNVs in NDD cohorts (SFARI); CASZ1 is flagged as a dosage-sensitive candidate gene within the deletion locus.

citation: Noncoding de novo mutations in SCN2A are associated with autism spectrum disorders (PMID: 40894881)
variant_detail: ≥3 noncoding de novo mutations (CADD ≥15) in CASZ1 in ASD probands; individual variants not specified in the abstract
phenotype: autism spectrum disorder
diagnostic_reason: Enrichment of noncoding DNMs in probands versus unaffected siblings. This is only suggestive, and CASZ1 is not the paper's main finding.

citation: Essential role of the zinc finger transcription factor Casz1 for mammalian cardiac morphogenesis and development (PMID: 25190801)
phenotype: Hypoplasia of myocardium; Ventricular septal defect; Disorganized cardiac morphology / cardiac noncompaction; Decreased cardiomyocyte proliferation; Abnormal expression of muscle contraction genes (Tnni2, Tnnt1, Ckm, Acta1) and ion channel genes (Abcc9, Cacna1d)

citation: A single-cell time-series atlas of endothelial cell embryonic development (PMID: 41702400)
phenotype: Endothelial-specific Casz1 knockout caused impaired vascular growth; Disturbed pulmonary endothelial organotypic differentiation; Deficient epithelial-endothelial crosstalk in lung

citation: Casz1 is required for both inner hair cell fate stabilization and outer hair cell survival (PMID: 39883789)
phenotype: Transdifferentiation of inner hair cells into outer hair cells; OHC production unaffected but long-term OHC survival compromised; Gata3 down-regulated in Casz1-deleted IHCs; Hearing impairment, partially rescued by Gata3 overexpression

citation: A Casz1-NuRD complex regulates temporal identity transitions in neural progenitors (PMID: 33594190)
phenotype: Casz1 required to control the transition between neurogenesis and gliogenesis in the retina; Casz1 loss reduces rod fate and promotes gliogenesis; Interacts with the NuRD complex

citation: CASZ1 promotes vascular assembly and morphogenesis through the direct regulation of an EGFL7/RhoA-mediated pathway (PMID: 23639441)
phenotype: Failure to develop a branched and lumenized vascular system; Impaired blood vessel assembly and morphogenesis; Reduced Egfl7 and RhoA expression

citation: Congenital heart disease protein 5 associates with CASZ1 to maintain myocardial tissue integrity (PMID: 24993940)
phenotype: CASZ1 depletion produced cardiac phenotypes similar to, but milder than, CHD5 depletion; Compromised myocardial integrity; Improper basement membrane deposition; Failure of cardiac cell movements and cardiac tube morphogenesis

citation: Casz1-NuRD complex - A Casz1-NuRD complex regulates temporal identity transitions in neural progenitors (PMID: 33594190)
summary: BioID proteomics in retinal cells showed Casz1 interacts with the NuRD (nucleosome remodeling and deacetylase) complex. Both NuRD and polycomb are required for Casz1 to promote rod fate and suppress gliogenesis, and Casz1 controls the neurogenesis-to-gliogenesis transition.

citation: Casz1 controls higher-order nuclear organization in rod photoreceptors (PMID: 30072429)
summary: Conditional Casz1 deletion in mouse rods disrupts chromatin inversion, gene expression and long-term survival. Casz1 interacts with the polycomb repressor complex in a splice variant-specific manner, and both are needed to silence lamin A/C. Casz1 is also sufficient to expand and centralize heterochromatin in fibroblasts.

citation: Essential role of the zinc finger transcription factor Casz1 for mammalian cardiac morphogenesis and development (PMID: 25190801)
summary: Casz1 knockout mice show myocardial hypoplasia from reduced cardiomyocyte proliferation, ventricular septal defect and noncompaction, phenocopying 1p36 deletion CHD. Transcriptome analysis showed dysregulation of muscle contraction genes (TNNI2, TNNT1, CKM, ACTA1) and ion channel genes (ABCC9, CACNA1D).

citation: CASZ1 loss-of-function mutation contributes to familial dilated cardiomyopathy (PMID: 28099117)
summary: A heterozygous nonsense CASZ1 mutation (p.K351X) was found in a DCM family and co-segregated with disease in an autosomal dominant pattern with complete penetrance. It was absent in 400 control chromosomes, and the mutant protein had no transcriptional activity in luciferase reporter assays.

citation: CASZ1 upregulates PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling and promotes T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (PMID: 38058200)
summary: TAL1 directly and positively regulates CASZ1, and T-ALL samples overexpress the CASZ1b isoform. CASZ1b expression correlates with PI3K-AKT-mTOR activation, which is required for CASZ1b-mediated transformation of Ba/F3 cells. CASZ1b cooperates with activated NOTCH1 to drive T-ALL in zebrafish and protects T-ALL cells from chemotherapy and serum deprivation.

citation: CASZ1 induces skeletal muscle and rhabdomyosarcoma differentiation through a feed-forward loop with MYOD and MYOG (PMID: 32060262)
summary: CASZ1 upregulates MYOD signature genes and induces differentiation in myoblasts and embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma. RAS-MEK signaling suppresses CASZ1. ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq and RNA-seq show CASZ1 directly activates muscle genes and represses non-muscle genes by altering chromatin accessibility and super-enhancers. A CASZ1 coding variant was found in primary RMS tumors.

citation: Loss of CASZ1 tumor suppressor linked to oncogenic subversion of neuroblastoma core regulatory circuitry (PMID: 36243768)
summary: CASZ1 is highly expressed in developing chromaffin cells but silenced in neuroblastoma, where the core regulatory circuit component HAND2 directly represses it. Restoring CASZ1 upregulates noradrenergic neuronal genes and represses core regulatory circuit components by remodeling enhancers, inducing differentiation.

citation: CASZ1 promotes migration, invasion, and metastasis of lung cancer cells by controlling expression of ITGAV (PMID: 36777515)
summary: CASZ1b overexpression promotes lung cancer cell migration, invasion and EMT, and CASZ1 knockdown reduces these and metastasis in vivo. CASZ1 binds the ITGAV promoter and transcriptionally regulates ITGAV, affecting integrin-mediated pathways.

citation: A single-cell time-series atlas of endothelial cell embryonic development (PMID: 41702400)
summary: Single-cell mouse embryonic atlas identifies Casz1 as a pulmonary EC-enriched transcription factor. Endothelial-specific Casz1 knockout impaired vascular growth, disturbed pulmonary endothelial organotypic differentiation and weakened epithelial-EC crosstalk.

citation: Differential regulation of CASZ1 protein expression during cardiac and skeletal muscle development (PMID: 24633745)
summary: In Xenopus, CASZ1 protein is detected throughout the developing myocardium but restricted to terminally differentiated cardiomyocytes, and is down-regulated in cells re-entering the cell cycle. It is also present in differentiated skeletal muscle and lymph-heart musculature, suggesting post-transcriptional control.

citation: ASHG 2017 - Debunking the cerebral palsy (CP)-birth asphyxia myth: Frequent genomic etiologies for CP identified by exome sequencing (Moreno-De-Luca et al.)
variant_detail: Rare loss-of-function variant in MAP3K12 (specific nucleotide/protein change not provided in abstract)
phenotype: Cerebral palsy
diagnostic_reason: Rare LoF variant absent from population databases (ExAC, EVS, 1000G); MAP3K12 predicted to be extremely LoF intolerant; proposed as a novel CP candidate gene

citation: Prioritizing de novo potential non-canonical splicing variants in neurodevelopmental disorders (PMID: 38113761)
variant_detail: MAP3K12 c.436G>A (chr12:53880317 C>T), missense; non-canonical splicing variant causing exon 4 91bp deletion in minigene assay
phenotype: Neurodevelopmental disorder (unspecified developmental delay/NDD)
diagnostic_reason: De novo variant in a patient with NDD; minigene assay showed abnormal splicing (exon 4 91bp deletion); MAP3K12 implicated in axon growth

citation: Xenopus Dlk study - Dual leucine zipper kinase is necessary for retinal ganglion cell axonal regeneration in Xenopus laevis (PMID: 37152673)
phenotype: map3k12/Dlk is necessary for RGC axonal regeneration after optic nerve crush, in a dose-dependent manner; Loss of Dlk does not affect RGC innervation of the brain during development; Loss of Dlk does not affect visually driven behavior; Loss of Dlk blocks axonal regeneration and functional vision restoration after optic nerve crush; Loss of Dlk does not alter acute mitochondrial movement in RGC axons after crush; Loss of Dlk blocks Jun phosphorylation and nuclear translocation in RGCs days after crush; Jun is dispensable for reinnervation
knockout_type: other (CRISPR/Cas9 F0 mosaic knockout/knockdown of map3k12 injected at the one-cell stage)

citation: Dual leucine zipper kinase is required for mechanical allodynia and microgliosis after nerve injury (PMID: 29968565)
phenotype: Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of DLK reduces mechanical hypersensitivity (allodynia) in a neuropathic pain model; DLK inhibition prevents spinal cord microgliosis after nerve injury; DLK controls a transcriptional program in somatosensory neurons, including Csf1 and other pain-related genes

citation: DLK signaling in axotomized neurons triggers complement activation and loss of upstream synapses (PMID: 38363678)
phenotype: DLK signaling in injured motoneurons triggers induction of phagocytic microglia and synapse loss; DLK regulates C1q expression, first in the axotomized motoneuron and later in microglia; Microglia phagocytose presynaptic components of upstream synapses; Loss of cholinergic C boutons from axotomized motoneurons depends on DLK and on microglia

citation: Promoting regeneration while blocking cell death preserves motor neuron function in a model of ALS (PMID: 36342754)
phenotype: DLK deletion plus ATF3 expression gives synergistic protection in the SOD1G93A ALS model; Fewer motor neurons undergo cell death; Reduced axon degeneration; Preserved motor function and neuromuscular connectivity; Improved motor neuron electrophysiology, histology and behavior
knockout_type: conditional knockout (DLK deletion combined with constitutive ATF3 expression in SOD1G93A mice)

citation: Translatome analysis reveals cellular network in DLK-dependent hippocampal glutamatergic neuron degeneration (PMID: 40067879)
phenotype: DLK-dependent translatome identified in hippocampal glutamatergic neurons; Dorsal CA1 and dentate gyrus neurons are vulnerable to elevated DLK expression, while CA3 neurons are less vulnerable; Increased DLK signaling is associated with microtubule disruption, potentially via STMN4; Altered neurite outgrowth, axon specification and synapse formation in cultured hippocampal neurons with different DLK levels

citation: Dual Leucine Zipper Kinase Is Constitutively Active in the Adult Mouse Brain and Has Both Stress-Induced and Homeostatic Functions (PMID: 32659913)
phenotype: DLK constitutively drives nuclear p-c-Jun in cerebellar granule neurons; In rTg4510 forebrain, p-c-Jun accumulation is DLK-dependent and correlates with synaptic loss and gliosis; DLK inhibition reduces a core set of JNK-pathway transcripts; In the cerebellum, DLK regulates IGF1 signaling through IGFBP5 induction
knockout_type: other (pharmacological DLK inhibition; rTg4510 tauopathy model)

citation: Sun et al. 2026 - ATF2 phosphorylation is a core transcriptional driver of neuron apoptosis (PMID: 42161275)
summary: A genome-wide CRISPR inhibition screen in human neurons identified DLK/MAP3K12, JUN and ATF2 as a pro-death cascade. MAP3 kinase phosphorylation of ATF2 drives upregulation of JUN and neuronal apoptosis. Interfering with ATF2 prevents neuronal apoptosis in vitro and in vivo.

citation: Kim et al. 2022 - FK506-binding protein-like and FK506-binding protein 8 regulate dual leucine zipper kinase degradation and neuronal responses to axon injury (PMID: 35101451)
summary: A yeast two-hybrid screen identified FKBPL as a DLK-binding protein. FKBPL binds the DLK kinase domain, inhibits its kinase activity and induces ubiquitin-dependent degradation. FKBP8 also promotes DLK degradation via autophagy and proteasome, with K271 as the ubiquitination/SUMO3 site. FKBP8 overexpression delays axon degeneration and neuronal death after axotomy in vivo.

citation: Shin et al. 2022 - A Critical Role for DLK and LZK in Axonal Repair in the Mammalian Spinal Cord (PMID: 35361703)
summary: In mice, inducible neuronal deletion of both DLK (MAP3K12) and LZK (MAP3K13), but not either alone, abolished PTEN deletion-induced regeneration and sprouting of corticospinal tract axons. The two kinases are redundant and act in both injured and uninjured neurons, independently of PTEN/mTOR signaling.

citation: Bhattacharyya et al. 2024 - DLK signaling in axotomized neurons triggers complement activation and loss of upstream synapses (PMID: 38363678)
summary: In conditional knockout mice, DLK/MAP3K12 activation in axotomized motoneurons triggers C1q expression, first in the neuron and later in microglia, along with phagocytic microglia and loss of upstream synapses. DLK is therefore a neuronal driver of injury-induced inflammation.

citation: Pozniak/Wang et al. 2018 - Dual leucine zipper kinase is required for mechanical allodynia and microgliosis after nerve injury (PMID: 29968565)
summary: Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of DLK (Map3k12) reduces mechanical hypersensitivity and spinal microgliosis after nerve injury in mice. DLK controls a transcriptional program in somatosensory neurons that includes pain-related genes such as Csf1.

citation: Patel et al. 2015 - Discovery of dual leucine zipper kinase (DLK, MAP3K12) inhibitors with activity in neurodegeneration models (PMID: 25341110)
summary: The selective, brain-penetrant DLK inhibitor GNE-3511 protected neurons from degeneration in vitro. It was also active in two animal models of neurodegeneration, supporting DLK kinase activity as a driver of neuronal degeneration.

citation: Wang et al. 2021 - MiR-191-5p alleviates microglial cell injury by targeting Map3k12 to inhibit the MAPK signaling pathway in Alzheimer's disease (PMID: 34818971)
summary: miR-191-5p directly targets the Map3k12 3'UTR (shown by luciferase assay) and downregulates its expression. In Aβ1-42-treated microglia and APP/PS1 mice, this inhibits MAPK signaling and reduces microglial injury and apoptosis. Map3k12 therefore promotes MAPK signaling and injury in AD models.

citation: Li et al. 2015 - MicroRNA-130a Targets MAP3K12 to Modulate Diabetic Endothelial Progenitor Cell Function (PMID: 25999017)
summary: MAP3K12 is a target of miR-130a in endothelial progenitor cells. Reduced miR-130a in diabetic EPCs and high glucose lead to sustained JNK activation, apoptosis and dysfunction through MAP3K12.

citation: Tang et al. 2024 - Comprehensive analysis of MAPK genes in the prognosis, immune characteristics, and drug treatment of renal clear cell carcinoma (PMID: 39038636)
summary: MAP3K12 was the most significant gene in a six-gene MAPK prognostic signature in ccRCC and had independent prognostic value. Knockout and overexpression experiments in vitro and in vivo showed it promotes RCC proliferation, migration, invasion and tumour progression.

citation: Wang et al. 2021 - Celastrol attenuates ischemia/reperfusion-mediated memory dysfunction by downregulating AK005401/MAP3K12 (PMID: 33387968)
summary: Ischemia/reperfusion in mice and OGD/R in HT-22 hippocampal cells upregulated lncRNA AK005401 and MAP3K12, with increased p-JNK/p-c-Jun and reduced PI3K/Akt activity, leading to mitochondrial dysfunction and apoptosis. Celastrol downregulated AK005401/MAP3K12 and improved memory.

citation: Interstitial microdeletion of 17q11.2 is associated with hypotonia, fatigue, intellectual disability, and a subtle facial phenotype in three unrelated patients (PMID: 29130599)
variant_detail: De novo heterozygous interstitial microdeletions of 17q11.2 (0.97–1.18 Mb; smallest region of overlap 863 kb). The region contains 7 genes, including ZNF207, CDK5R1, PSMD11, RHOT1 and SUZ12. These are multi-gene deletions, not ZNF207-specific variants.
phenotype: developmental delay; intellectual disability (mild to severe); hypotonia (significant in two patients, investigated for a possible neuromuscular disorder); excessive fatigue with daytime somnolence (two female patients); broad and wide forehead; long palpebral fissures; bulbous nasal tip; thick lips
diagnostic_reason: The deletions were de novo and overlapped between three unrelated patients with similar phenotypes. ZNF207 is one of five genes in the smallest region of overlap predicted to be haploinsufficient (CDK5R1, PSMD11, RHOT1, SUZ12, ZNF207). CDK5R1 and RHOT1 were proposed as the main candidates, so ZNF207 is not specifically implicated.
center_country: Three unrelated patients from three different countries (specific centers not stated in the abstract)

citation: Lee et al. 2014 - A microtubule-associated zinc finger protein, BuGZ, regulates mitotic chromosome alignment by ensuring Bub3 stability and kinetochore targeting (PMID: 24462186)
summary: ZNF207 (BuGZ) associates with spindle microtubules and directly binds and stabilizes Bub3 through its GLEBS motif. Through its microtubule-binding domain it enhances Bub3 loading onto kinetochores in prometaphase, which is needed for chromosome alignment and metaphase-to-anaphase progression.

citation: ASHG/other 2025 - RNA-coupled CRISPR Screens Reveal ZNF207 as a Regulator of LMNA Aberrant Splicing in Progeria (PMID: 40568141)
summary: A pooled CRISPR splicing-reporter screen (CRASP-Seq) identified ZNF207 as a regulator of progerin splicing. ZNF207 depletion enhanced canonical LMNA splicing and lowered progerin in patient-derived cells. Its zinc finger domain interacts with U1 snRNP factors, which supports a role as a U1 snRNP auxiliary factor.

citation: 2018 - A distinct isoform of ZNF207 controls self-renewal and pluripotency of human embryonic stem cells (PMID: 30349051)
summary: ZNF207 was identified by proteomics as an OCT4 enhancer-associated protein. In hESCs a specific isoform partners with master pluripotency TFs to maintain self-renewal and pluripotency. Isoform switching directs ectoderm commitment through direct regulation of neuronal TFs such as OTX2.

citation: 2025 - ZNF207-driven PRDX1 lactylation and NRF2 activation in regorafenib resistance and ferroptosis evasion (PMID: 40680452)
summary: A CRISPR/Cas9 screen in regorafenib-treated HCC cells identified ZNF207 as a driver of resistance. ZNF207 promotes PRDX1 lactylation at K67, which enhances NRF2 nuclear translocation and activation and suppresses ferroptosis. ZNF207 knockdown restores ferroptosis and regorafenib sensitivity.

citation: 2025 - Transcription factor ZNF207 drives aerobic glycolysis and facilitates malignancy progression in hepatocellular carcinoma (PMID: 40684964)
summary: ZNF207 acts as a transcription factor that regulates ENO1 and GAPDH transcription (shown by dual-luciferase and ChIP-qPCR), promoting aerobic glycolysis in HCC. Silencing ZNF207 reduced xenograft growth and lung metastasis in nude mice. The compound pinosylvin targets ZNF207 and lowers GAPDH and ENO1.

citation: 2022 - System analysis based on the cancer-immunity cycle identifies ZNF207 as a novel immunotherapy target for hepatocellular carcinoma (PMID: 35246476)
summary: Hypoxia upregulates ZNF207 in HCC. ZNF207 acts through the MAPK-CX3CL1 axis in CD8+ T-cell chemotaxis and transcriptionally regulates IDO1, raising kynurenine and exhausting CD8+ T cells. Low ZNF207 expression predicts greater sensitivity to anti-PD1 therapy.

citation: 2019 - Expression of ZNF207 in hepatocellular carcinoma and its significance (PMID: 31113916)
sample_size: 10 paired fresh tissues (qPCR); 135 paraffin-embedded HCC cases (IHC)
significance: P<0.01 (mRNA, survival); P<0.05 (clinicopathology, independent risk factor)
summary: ZNF207 mRNA and protein are elevated in HCC relative to adjacent non-tumor liver. High expression correlates with cirrhosis, nodule number, capsule, vascular invasion and TNM stage, and is an independent risk factor for poor OS and DFS.

citation: 2025 - Downregulation of hnRNPA1 inhibits hepatocellular carcinoma cell progression by modulating alternative splicing of ZNF207 exon 9 (PMID: 39834948)
summary: hnRNPA1 binds ZNF207 RNA (RIP assay) and regulates skipping of ZNF207 exon 9. This links ZNF207 splicing to PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling and to HCC cell proliferation, migration and apoptosis in Hep G2 cells.

citation: 2015 - Oncogenic HER2 fusions in gastric cancer (PMID: 25889497)
summary: A ZNF207-HER2 fusion was found in 3 of 21 HER2-amplified gastric cancers (14%, together with MDK-HER2 and NOS2-HER2 fusions). ZNF207-HER2 is oncogenic and activates HER2 kinase. It does not bind trastuzumab, so xenografts expressing it were resistant to trastuzumab.

citation: 2023 - Conserved transcription factors promote cell fate stability and restrict reprogramming potential in differentiated cells (PMID: 36973293)
summary: A genome-wide TF screen identified ZNF207 as one of four TFs (ATF7IP, JUNB, SP7, ZNF207) that oppose cell fate reprogramming. They keep chromatin at reprogramming TF motifs closed and downregulate genes required for reprogramming. Knocking them down together with MGT overexpression improved heart function after myocardial infarction.

citation: Constitutional haploinsufficiency of tumor suppressor genes in mentally retarded patients with microdeletions in 17p13.1 (PMID: 19617690)
variant_detail: De novo 17p13.1 microdeletions sharing an overlapping ~180 kb segment encompassing 18 genes including KCTD11, DLG4, GPS2 (and GABARAP); 2 of 4 patients' deletions also included TP53. Detected by array-CGH.
phenotype: mental impairment/intellectual disability; developmental delay; congenital abnormalities
diagnostic_reason: De novo microdeletions with an overlapping minimal region in 17p13.1; GPS2 is one of several candidate genes (with KCTD11, DLG4, GABARAP) for neuronal development and mental impairment. GPS2 is not individually established as causal.
center_country: Brazil (3 patients from a cohort of 300 mentally retarded individuals)

citation: Yamamoto et al. 2010 - A functional analysis of GABARAP on 17p13.1 by knockdown zebrafish (PMID: 20111057)
variant_detail: 2.3-Mb microdeletion of 17p13.2p13.1 (includes GPS2, DLG4, GABARAP, KCTD11) detected by array-CGH
phenotype: moderate mental retardation; intractable epilepsy; dysmorphic features
diagnostic_reason: Deletion overlaps the previously proposed shortest region of overlap for 17p13.1 microdeletions; GPS2 is among the neuronal-development candidate genes, but the functional work focused on GABARAP and DLG4.

citation: ASHG 2010 - A functional analysis of GABARAP on 17p13.1 by knockdown zebrafish (T. Yamamoto et al.)
variant_detail: 2.3-Mb microdeletion of 17p13.2p13.1 (includes GPS2, DLG4, GABARAP, KCTD11) detected by array-CGH
phenotype: moderate mental retardation; intractable epilepsy; dysmorphic features
diagnostic_reason: Deletion overlaps the shortest region of overlap for 17p13.1 microdeletions; GPS2 is a candidate gene among several in the region.

citation: 2025 - GPS2 regulates embryonic angiogenesis by enhancing endothelial cell survival through stabilizing HOIP (PMID: 41507360)
phenotype: Endothelial cell-specific Gps2 deletion (Gps2ECKO) causes embryonic lethality at E16.5 due to defective vascularization; Aberrant TNFR1-mediated endothelial cell death; HOIP degradation and LUBAC instability in ECs; Attenuated TNF-induced NF-κB activation and increased formation of cell-death-inducing complex-II; TNFR1 deletion restored normal vascularization and rescued embryonic lethality

citation: 2018 - GPS2 Deficiency Triggers Maladaptive White Adipose Tissue Expansion in Obesity via HIF1A Activation (PMID: 30208320)
phenotype: Adipocyte-specific GPS2 knockout (GPS2 AKO) causes adipocyte hypertrophy, inflammation and mitochondrial dysfunction during surplus energy; Phenotype driven by HIF1A activation, with inadequate WAT remodeling; Reversible by pharmacological or genetic HIF1A inhibition

citation: 2017 - Inhibition of Ubc13-mediated Ubiquitination by GPS2 Regulates Multiple Stages of B Cell Development (PMID: 28039360)
phenotype: B cell-targeted GPS2 deletion causes developmental defects at multiple stages of B cell differentiation; Increased TLR/BCR and AKT/FOXO1 signaling through loss of Ubc13 inhibition

citation: 2020 - Adipocyte Reprogramming by the Transcriptional Coregulator GPS2 Impacts Beta Cell Insulin Secretion (PMID: 32937117)
phenotype: Adipocyte-specific GPS2 knockout causes inappropriate insulin secretion and glucose intolerance; Adipose-secreted factors cause increased pancreatic islet inflammation and impaired beta cell function

citation: 2016 - Loss of the co-repressor GPS2 sensitizes macrophage activation upon metabolic stress induced by obesity and type 2 diabetes (PMID: 27270589)
phenotype: Macrophage-specific Gps2 KO causes enhancer activation, pro-inflammatory gene expression and hypersensitivity to metabolic-stress signals; Adipose tissue inflammation and insulin resistance; Transplantation of GPS2-overexpressing bone marrow into ob/ob and diet-induced obese mice reduced inflammation and improved insulin sensitivity

citation: 2019 - Hepatocyte-specific loss of GPS2 in mice reduces non-alcoholic steatohepatitis via activation of PPARα (PMID: 30975991)
phenotype: Hepatocyte-specific Gps2 knockout alleviates diet-induced steatosis and fibrosis; Activation of lipid catabolic genes via PPARα as a direct GPS2 target

citation: 2022 - Genome-wide CRISPR knockout screening identified G protein pathway suppressor 2 as a novel tumor suppressor for uveal melanoma metastasis (PMID: 35941228)
phenotype: GPS2 knockdown in uveal melanoma cells xenografted in mice promoted proliferation and metastasis in vivo; Upregulation of MAPK and PI3K-Akt signaling and downregulation of Slit/Robo signaling

citation: 2021 - Loss of G-Protein Pathway Suppressor 2 Promotes Tumor Growth Through Activation of AKT Signaling (PMID: 33490071)
phenotype: GPS2-deleted MDA-MB-231 human breast cancer cells in an orthotopic xenograft mouse model conferred greater tumor burden; Increased proliferation, migration and invasion in vitro; Sustained AKT activation

citation: Ceccarelli/Fan et al. - GPS2 Deficiency Triggers Maladaptive White Adipose Tissue Expansion in Obesity via HIF1A Activation (PMID: 30208320)
summary: Adipocyte-specific GPS2 knockout mice show adipocyte hypertrophy, inflammation and mitochondrial dysfunction during surplus energy, driven by HIF1A activation and reversible by HIF1A inhibition. In human adipose tissue, GPS2 expression correlates negatively with HIF1A, adipocyte hypertrophy and insulin resistance.

citation: GPS2 promotes erythroid differentiation in K562 erythroleukemia cells primarily via NCOR1 (PMID: 38814500)
summary: GPS2 overexpression promoted hemin- and Ara-C-induced hemoglobin synthesis in K562 cells and increased globin and ALAS2 expression, while GPS2 knockdown inhibited differentiation. The effect depends mainly on NCOR1, since NCOR1 knockdown or deletion of the NCOR1-binding domain of GPS2 diminished it.

citation: Inhibition of K63 ubiquitination by G-Protein pathway suppressor 2 (GPS2) regulates mitochondria-associated translation (PMID: 39094987)
summary: GPS2 inhibits Ubc13-mediated K63 ubiquitination of RNA-binding and translation proteins on the outer mitochondrial membrane (PABPC1, RPS1, RACK1, eIF3M) in MEFs and human breast cancer cells. Loss of GPS2 or stress-induced nuclear translocation promotes import-coupled translation of nuclear-encoded mitochondrial proteins and an antioxidant program.

citation: Nonproteolytic ubiquitination regulates chromatin occupancy by the NCoR/SMRT/HDAC3 corepressor complex in MCF-7 breast cancer cells (PMID: 40305047)
summary: In MCF-7 cells, nuclear GPS2 licenses HDAC3 recruitment to chromatin by restricting TRAF6-mediated ubiquitination within the NCoR/SMRT complex. TRAF6 translocates to the nucleus after IL-1β, binds NCoR/SMRT directly and ubiquitinates TAB2, which contributes to corepressor clearance.

citation: GPS2 confers l-asparaginase resistance in acute lymphoblastic leukemia cells through ATF4/ASNS axis (PMID: 40693356)
summary: GPS2 binds ATF4 and stabilizes it by impairing the ATF4-BTRC (E3 ligase) interaction, which reduces ubiquitin-proteasome degradation and sustains ASNS expression. GPS2 knockdown sensitizes ALL cells to l-asparaginase in vitro and in xenografts.

citation: Exchange Factor TBL1 and Arginine Methyltransferase PRMT6 Cooperate in Protecting GPS2 from Proteasomal Degradation (PMID: 26070566)
summary: GPS2 is polyubiquitinated and degraded via the E3 ligase Siah2. Interaction with TBL1 protects GPS2 from degradation, and PRMT6-mediated arginine methylation of GPS2 regulates the TBL1 interaction and inhibits proteasomal degradation. GPS2 was first identified as part of the NCoR-SMRT corepressor complex.

citation: Liquid-liquid phase separation of GPS2-LATS1 promotes colorectal cancer progression by reprogramming lipid metabolism (PMID: 40715488)
summary: GPS2 is overexpressed in CRC, and its depletion inhibits tumor growth in vitro and in vivo. GPS2 undergoes LLPS and binds the LATS1 kinase domain through its coiled-coil domain, suppressing Hippo signaling and releasing YAP. This promotes SREBP1 nuclear translocation and PPARα transcription, reprogramming lipid metabolism.

citation: Interaction of NEP with GPS2 Facilitates Influenza A Virus Replication by Weakening the Inhibition of GPS2 to RNA Synthesis and Ribonucleoprotein Assembly (PMID: 33658351)
summary: Yeast two-hybrid, GST-pulldown and co-IP showed GPS2 binds influenza NEP. GPS2 knockdown or knockout enhanced IAV titers and overexpression impaired replication, because GPS2 reduces PB1-PB2 interaction and vRNP assembly. NEP mediates nuclear export and degradation of GPS2.

citation: GPS2 regulates embryonic angiogenesis by enhancing endothelial cell survival through stabilizing HOIP (PMID: 41507360)
summary: Endothelial-specific Gps2 knockout mice die embryonically at E16.5 from defective vascularization and TNFR1-mediated endothelial cell death, rescued by TNFR1 deletion. GPS2 binds the HOIP NZF domain and blocks K48-linked ubiquitination at K579, K737 and K988, stabilizing LUBAC and supporting TNF-induced NF-κB activation.

citation: Hepatocyte-specific loss of GPS2 in mice reduces non-alcoholic steatohepatitis via activation of PPARα (PMID: 30975991)
summary: GPS2, a subunit of the NCOR-HDAC3 complex, promotes NAFLD-to-NASH progression. Hepatocyte-specific Gps2 knockout protects against diet-induced steatosis and fibrosis and activates lipid catabolic genes, with PPARα identified as a direct target. In human liver, GPS2 expression correlates positively with a NASH/fibrosis signature.

citation: Sumo2 knockout study - SUMO2 is essential while SUMO3 is dispensable for mouse embryonic development (PMID: 24891386)
phenotype: Sumo2-/- embryos show severe developmental delay and die at ~E10.5; Sumo2+/- and Sumo2+/-;Sumo3+/- mice have no overt phenotype; Sumo3-/- mice are viable; Sumo2+/-;Sumo3-/- mice are nearly absent at birth (only 2 found in 35 litters) and the rare survivors are considerably smaller than littermates; SUMO2 is the predominantly expressed SUMO isoform
sample_size: 35 litters from Sumo2+/-;Sumo3+/- x Sumo3-/- crosses (only 2 Sumo2+/-;Sumo3-/- mice born)

citation: Small ubiquitin-like modifier 2 (SUMO2) is critical for memory processes in mice (PMID: 32910521)
phenotype: Conditional deletion of Sumo2 in forebrain neurons caused marked cognitive impairments, including episodic and fear memory deficits; Impaired dynamic SUMOylation associated with synaptic plasticity; Deficit in maintenance of hippocampal long-term potentiation; No constitutive changes in gene expression or neuronal morphology

citation: The requirement of SUMO2/3 for SENP2 mediated extraembryonic and embryonic development (PMID: 31625212)
phenotype: Inactivation of Sumo2 (or Sumo3) alleviated the placental deficiencies of Senp2 knockouts (trophoblast layer defects); Reduction of Sumo2 rescued heart structure formation (atrioventricular cushion and myocardium) in Senp2 knockouts; Hyper-SUMOylation from SENP2 deficiency compensated by reducing SUMO levels

citation: SUMO2 deletion changes chromatin accessibility and enhances cytotoxic T cell activation and tumor infiltration (PMID: 42853933)
phenotype: T cell-specific Sumo2 KO enhanced CD8+ T cell activation; Increased chromatin accessibility at AP-1 (BATF, JunB) enhancer regions; Greater tumor infiltration of Sumo2 KO OT1 and CAR T cells; Greater tumor growth inhibition than wild-type T cells; Increased TRAIL expression and activated antitumor immune microenvironment

citation: Ubiquitin-like proteins NEDD8 and SUMO2 control epithelial homeostasis, regeneration, and inflammation (PMID: 42348677)
phenotype: Epithelial conditional Sumo2 knockout showed SUMO2 is required for epithelial differentiation; Opposite function to NEDD8, which is needed for progenitor maintenance, regeneration and inflammation control

citation: Ferroptosis-induced SUMO2 lactylation counteracts ferroptosis by enhancing ACSL4 degradation in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 41057295)
summary: Ferroptosis induces SUMO2 lactylation at K11 (SUMO2-K11la), catalyzed by the lactyltransferase AARS1 and reversed by the delactylase HDAC1. SUMO2-K11la disrupts the SUMO2–ACSL4 interaction, which promotes ACSL4 degradation and ferroptosis resistance in LUAD cells. A cell-penetrating peptide blocking SUMO2-K11la sensitized xenografts to cisplatin and enhanced chemoimmunotherapy.

citation: SUMOylation-Driven mRNA Circularization Enhances Translation and Promotes Lymphatic Metastasis of Bladder Cancer (PMID: 37991737)
summary: DHCR24 mediates and recognizes SUMO2 modification of hnRNPA2B1 at K108. This promotes hnRNPA2B1–eIF4G1 interaction, TBK1 mRNA circularization and eIF4F assembly, which drives Akt/VEGFC signaling, lymphangiogenesis and lymph node metastasis. DHCR24 silencing impaired metastasis in a PDX model.

citation: Induced proximity to PML protects TDP-43 from aggregation via SUMO-ubiquitin networks (PMID: 40246979)
summary: SUMO2 attachment to TDP-43 compartmentalizes it in PML nuclear bodies and limits its aggregation under proteotoxic stress. Recruiting TDP-43 to PML triggers a SUMOylation-ubiquitylation cascade that works with p97 to protect against insolubility.

citation: Aberrant Nuclear Export of circNCOR1 Underlies SMAD7-Mediated Lymph Node Metastasis of Bladder Cancer (PMID: 35395674)
summary: SUMO2 binding to the RNA export factor DDX39B (SUMOylation) drives nuclear export of circNCOR1. Reduced SUMO2–DDX39B binding increases circNCOR1 nuclear retention, which suppresses TGFβ-SMAD signaling and bladder cancer lymph node metastasis.

citation: Guanosine modulates SUMO2/3-ylation in neurons and astrocytes via adenosine receptors (PMID: 32892251)
summary: In primary cortical neurons and astrocytes, guanosine at concentrations above 10 μM increased global SUMO2/3-ylation at 1 h. The effect was extracellular and blocked by the A1 receptor antagonist DPCPX, which implicates an A1–A2A receptor interaction.

citation: SUMOylation regulates USP5-Cav3.2 calcium channel interactions (PMID: 31455361)
summary: USP5 is SUMO2/3-modified at K113 in dorsal root ganglia, and this modification falls after peripheral nerve injury. SUMO2/3 modification reduces USP5 affinity for Cav3.2, since the SUMO-resistant K113R mutant bound Cav3.2 more strongly.

citation: Targeting SUMO2 reverses aberrant epigenetic rewiring driven by SS18::SSX fusion oncoproteins and impairs sarcomagenesis (PMID: 40804185)
summary: A CRISPR screen identified SUMO2 as a strong, selective dependency in synovial sarcoma, in vitro and in vivo. Genetic depletion or TAK-981 inhibition reduced SS18::SSX expression and chromatin occupancy and H2AK119ub, and reversed the fusion-driven transcriptional program.

citation: Astragaloside IV combined with ligustrazine ameliorates abnormal mitochondrial dynamics via Drp1 SUMO/deSUMOylation in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (PMID: 38615367)
summary: In rat MCAO and SH-SY5Y OGD/R models, SUMO2/3 overexpression suppressed mitochondrial fission, whereas SUMO1 promoted it. The treatment increased Drp1 SUMO2/3 binding, which was protective.

citation: Acetylation of SUMO2 at lysine 11 favors the formation of non-canonical SUMO chains (PMID: 30201799)
summary: SUMO2/3 K11 is reversibly acetylated, with SIRT1 as the deacetylase. Acetylation impairs chain formation in vitro, and in cells a K11 acetyl-mimic favors K5- and K35-linked chains over K7 and K21 linkages.

citation: Noncovalent structure of SENP1 in complex with SUMO2 (PMID: 31045562)
summary: A 2.62 Å crystal structure of the SENP1–SUMO2 complex shows that binding is driven mainly by polar interactions. The SUMO2 C-terminal QQTGG motif inserts into the SENP1 catalytic triad, which explains SUMO maturation and deSUMOylation.

citation: Gene expression and cell growth are modified by silencing SUMO2 and SUMO3 expression (PMID: 19275883)
summary: Stable miRNA silencing of SUMO2/3 in B35 neuroblastoma cells up-regulated 105 genes and down-regulated 58 genes. About 20% of these were linked to growth and differentiation, and cell division was suppressed.

citation: ASHG 2022 - Maternally Inherited novel SUMO2 variant associated with a complex phenotype
summary: A maternally inherited heterozygous start-loss variant in SUMO2 (c.2T>A, p.Met1?) was found in a proband and his mother. Both have limb malformations (tibial agenesis, syndactyly) and the proband also has congenital heart defects. SUMO2 knockdown in animal studies altered CDX2, OCT4 and NANOG expression and caused embryonic lethality.

citation: Vagal stimulation ameliorates murine colitis by regulating SUMOylation (PMID: 39565873)
summary: SUMO2 and SUMO3 were increased in colonic biopsies from IBD patients and in mouse colitis models during active disease. Sumo3 knockout protected against colitis, and the SUMO E1 inhibitor TAK-981 ameliorated colitis in three mouse models.

citation: Improved Diagnostic Yield in Recessive Intellectual Disability Utilizing Systematic Whole Exome Sequencing Data Reanalysis (PMID: 39748273)
variant_detail: Not specified in abstract; MAZ listed as a novel candidate gene identified in a consanguineous family with recessive ID (co-segregating variant; likely homozygous rather than heterozygous)
phenotype: intellectual disability
diagnostic_reason: Novel candidate gene supported by segregation analysis and bioinformatic functional annotation (recessive inheritance in the family)
center_country: Iran (Genetics Research Center, University of Social Welfare and Rehabilitation Sciences, Tehran)

citation: The transcription factor Maz is essential for normal eye development (PMID: 32571845)
variant_detail: Copy-number variations of MAZ (16p11.2 CNVs) identified in humans with abnormal ocular development
phenotype: abnormal ocular development; eye malformations
diagnostic_reason: Mouse Maz knockout produced eye defects; human MAZ CNVs and SNVs associated with ocular phenotypes; supports MAZ as a contributor to eye comorbidities of 16p11.2 CNVs

citation: The transcription factor Maz is essential for normal eye development (PMID: 32571845)
variant_detail: Single-nucleotide variants of MAZ (specific variants not given in abstract)
phenotype: abnormal ocular development; eye malformations
diagnostic_reason: Mouse Maz knockout produced eye defects; human MAZ CNVs and SNVs associated with ocular phenotypes; supports MAZ as a contributor to eye comorbidities of 16p11.2 CNVs

citation: ASHG 2022 - The benefits and yields of whole exome sequencing data reanalysis in Iranian undiagnosed patients with intellectual disability
variant_detail: Not specified; MAZ listed as a novel candidate gene in the ARID cohort (likely recessive)
phenotype: intellectual disability
diagnostic_reason: Novel candidate gene identified on WES reanalysis in consanguineous families
center_country: Iran (Genetics Research Center, University of Social Welfare and Rehabilitation Sciences, Tehran)

citation: ASHG 2014 - The role of MAZ in the regulation of genitourinary development via modulation of WNT signaling
variant_detail: MAZ copy-number variants (deletions/duplications within 16p11.2) detected by qPCR in about 6% of 258 GU-abnormal patients (0% of 57 controls)
phenotype: genitourinary malformations; cryptorchidism; hypospadias; bladder exstrophy-epispadias complex; ambiguous genitalia; congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract
diagnostic_reason: MAZ was the only gene covered by all mapped 16p11.2 CNVs in GU-defect patients; MAZ CNVs were enriched in patients versus controls; MAZ knockdown/overexpression altered WNT pathway genes

citation: Maz is essential for normal eye development (PMID: 32571845)
phenotype: Developmental eye defects with abnormal peripheral eye / ciliary margin formation; Reduced proliferation of progenitor cells in the peripheral eye region; Increased expression of Wnt pathway genes Sfrp2, Wnt2b and Fzd4; Downregulation of the Wnt reporter TCF-Lef1 in Maz-deficient eyes; Disrupted ciliary margin patterning; Human MAZ CNVs and SNVs associated with abnormal ocular development

citation: Maz is a dosage-sensitive regulator of genitourinary development: 16p11.2 transcription factor MAZ (PMID: 29432158)
phenotype: Perinatal lethality with survival dependent on Maz copy number; High penetrance of congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT) in homozygous mutants; Haploinsufficiency for normal bladder development; Ubiquitous Maz expression
knockout_type: full knockout (CRISPR-Cas9 deletion; homozygous and heterozygous)
mendelian_ratio: sub-Mendelian (survival dependent on Maz copy number)

citation: CRISPR and biochemical screens identify MAZ as a cofactor in CTCF-mediated insulation at Hox clusters (PMID: 35145304)
phenotype: MAZ KO disrupts gene expression and local contacts within topologically associating domains (cell lines); MAZ motif deletions derepress posterior Hox genes immediately after CTCF boundaries upon differentiation; Homeotic transformations in mouse
knockout_type: other (MAZ motif deletions at the Hox cluster in mouse; MAZ KO in cell lines)

citation: Kyriacou et al. 1992 (original MAZ cloning) - MAZ, a zinc finger protein, binds to c-MYC and C2 gene sequences regulating transcriptional initiation and termination (PMID: 1502157)
summary: MAZ was cloned as a 477-aa Cys2His2 zinc finger protein that binds the ME1a1 site and GA-box (GGGAGGG) elements in the c-MYC P2 promoter, the P2 attenuator and the C2 gene termination site, so it may act in both transcription initiation and termination. Its mRNA was present in all human tissues tested except kidney, as ~2.5 and 2.7 kb transcripts.

citation: Identification of the transcription factor MAZ as a regulator of erythropoiesis (PMID: 34351390)
summary: DNA affinity purification with mass spectrometry identified MAZ as binding the α-globin promoter. In primary human erythroid cells MAZ occupies active promoters and GATA1-bound enhancers. MAZ knockdown reduced α-globin expression in K562 cells and impaired differentiation of primary erythroid cells. MAZ locus variants are associated with erythroid traits.

citation: MAZ regulates fetal hemoglobin repression by activating MYB transcription (PMID: 41331317)
summary: MAZ depletion in HUDEP-2 and β-thalassemia patient-derived cells induced γ-globin mRNA and protein and raised HbF. MAZ occupies the MYB promoter, and MAZ loss reduced MYB. Restoring MYB re-silenced HBG, defining a MAZ-MYB axis.

citation: MAZ promotes tumor proliferation and immune evasion in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 39424990)
summary: MAZ is upregulated in LUAD tissue and its expression inversely correlates with patient survival. MAZ transcriptionally regulates KRAS and activates AKT-NF-κB signaling. Silencing MAZ reduced proliferation, pro-tumorigenic chemokines and Galectin-9, and enhanced immune checkpoint blockade efficacy in vivo.

citation: Akt phosphorylates myc-associated zinc finger protein (MAZ), releases P-MAZ from the p53 promoter, and activates p53 transcription (PMID: 26902421)
summary: MAZ is a transcriptional repressor of the p53 promoter. Akt phosphorylates MAZ at Thr385, which releases it from the p53 promoter and activates p53 transcription during oncogene activation.

citation: TUG1/MAZ/FTH1 Axis Attenuates the Antiglioma Effect of Dihydroartemisinin by Inhibiting Ferroptosis (PMID: 36164395)
summary: ChIP showed MAZ binds the FTH1 promoter and activates FTH1, a negative regulator of ferroptosis. Luciferase assays identified MAZ as a direct target of lncRNA TUG1. In dihydroartemisinin-treated glioma cells TUG1 was down and MAZ up, and TUG1 overexpression enhanced the drug's antiglioma effect in vitro and in vivo.

citation: Phenylethanolamine N-methyltransferase gene expression. Sp1 and MAZ potential for tissue-specific expression (PMID: 10085109)
summary: In Neuro2A cells MAZ competes with Sp1 for DNA sequences 3' to the -48 Sp1 site on the PNMT promoter, preventing Sp1 binding and induction. This Sp1-MAZ competition may add tissue-specific control of PNMT expression.

citation: ASHG 2014 - The role of MAZ in the regulation of genitourinary development via modulation of WNT signaling
summary: MAZ was the only gene covered by all 16p11.2 CNVs in patients with genitourinary defects. Maz is expressed in mouse kidneys, ureters, testes, bladder and genital tubercle.
