MAZ CNVs were found in 6% of GU-abnormal patients versus 0% of controls. MAZ knockdown or overexpression in HEK293 cells altered WNT pathway genes (DKK1/2/4, LRP5/6, FZD, WNT4, WNT11, GSK3A).

citation: ASHG 2018 - An exome-wide association study identifies candidate susceptibility genes for congenital obstructive uropathy
sample_size: 292 COU cases and 8,541 controls (WES); 398 cases and 8,197 controls (GWAS)
significance: rare P=3.58x10-5; common P=7.06x10-3 to 6.96x10-4; joint P=4.6x10-7
summary: Exome collapsing analysis found a rare-variant burden of dominant missense variants in MAZ in congenital obstructive uropathy. Common variants in the GWAS cross-annotation supported the association.

citation: ASHG 2018 - Genome-wide analysis of G4 sequences overlapped with SP1/MAZ binding sites in the human genome and their roles in gene regulation of the proto-oncogene Bcl3
summary: MAZ and SP1 bind a G-quadruplex (PU24WT) in the Bcl3 promoter by ChIP. The G4 ligand TMPyP4 reduced MAZ/SP1 binding, Bcl3 promoter activity and Bcl3 RNA in breast cancer cells.

citation: ASHG 2022 - Systematic analysis of nonsense-mediated decay escaping protein-truncating variants in 97,728 clinical exomes identifies new Mendelian disease genes (R. Torene et al.)
variant_detail: De novo protein-truncating variants in the NMD-escape region (3' end) of HDAC2; specific variant notation not provided
phenotype: syndromic neurodevelopmental disorder
diagnostic_reason: De novo PTV in the NMD-escape region; the gene was significantly enriched for PTVesc DNMs. HDAC2 showed high phenotypic similarity (phenopy) among patients, and is a histone modifier, a known NDD mechanism. Presented as a novel candidate gene.

citation: ASHG 2015 - Aggregated analysis of developmental disorders reveals novel risk genes and improves genetic diagnosis (K. Retterer et al.)
variant_detail: De novo likely gene-disrupting or damaging missense variants in HDAC2; specific variants and patient count not provided
phenotype: undiagnosed developmental disorder / neurodevelopmental disorder
diagnostic_reason: HDAC2 was identified as a potentially novel candidate risk gene by aggregated de novo mutation analysis in trios (≥2 LGD or damaging missense de novo variants); proposed mechanism is histone modification.

citation: 2025 - HDAC2 enhances the antimicrobial activity of neutrophils by promoting the formation of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in sepsis (PMID: 40850685)
phenotype: HDAC2 knockout or inhibition reduced inflammation and improved organ function in non-infectious (LPS-induced) sepsis; HDAC2 knockout decreased survival in infectious (CLP) sepsis; Knockout or inhibition significantly reduced NETs formation; Impaired antimicrobial activity against E. coli infection; Mechanism involves H3K18 acetylation and CARM1-mediated H3R17 methylation/citrullination; Dual HDAC2/CARM1 inhibition improved survival in CLP sepsis

citation: 2021 - HDAC1/2 Control Proliferation and Survival in Adult Epidermis and Pre-Basal Cell Carcinoma through p16 and p53 (PMID: 34284046)
phenotype: Epidermal codeletion of Hdac1 and Hdac2 in adult mouse epidermis reduced basal cell proliferation; Increased apoptosis; Inappropriate differentiation; Eventual loss of Hdac1/2-null keratinocytes; Elevated acetylated p53 and increased p16 expression; p53 loss partially restored proliferation; p16 deletion promoted long-term survival of null keratinocytes; In GLI2ΔN-driven pre-basal cell carcinoma, Hdac1/2 deletion reduced proliferation and increased apoptosis

citation: 2025 - The deacetylases HDAC1/HDAC2 control JAK2(V617F)-STAT signaling through the ubiquitin ligase SIAH2 (PMID: 40877230)
phenotype: Genetic depletion of HDAC1/HDAC2 induced apoptosis and long-term growth arrest of JAK2V617F MPN cells in vitro and in vivo; Spared normal hematopoietic stem cells; Did not compromise blood cell differentiation

citation: 2019 - Opposite regulation of Wnt/β-catenin and Shh signaling pathways by Rack1 controls mammalian cerebellar development (PMID: 30765517)
phenotype: Rack1 deletion in NSCs or GNPs caused severe cerebellar morphogenesis defects with impaired folia and fissure formation; Rack1 loss destabilized HDAC1/HDAC2 and reduced Shh signaling; Suppression of HDAC1/HDAC2 activity in the developing cerebellum phenocopied the Rack1 mutant

citation: 2021 - HDAC2 Facilitates Pancreatic Cancer Metastasis (PMID: 34903606)
phenotype: HDAC2 deficiency in PDAC cells impaired cell cycle progression in vitro; Impaired metastasis formation in vivo, particularly for mesenchymal/undifferentiated PDAC cells; Altered expression of PDGFRα, PDGFRβ and EGFR; Disabled the tumor-suppressive arm of TGFβ signaling

citation: GPR126 regulates colorectal cancer cell proliferation by mediating HDAC2 and GLI2 expression (PMID: 33629464)
summary: GPR126 knockdown reduced HDAC2 transcription and translation in colorectal cancer cells. Ectopic HDAC2 restored viability, proliferation and GLI2 reporter activity, and reduced G1 arrest. HDAC2 regulated GLI2 expression, and HDAC2 and GLI2 both bound the PTCH1 promoter by ChIP, placing HDAC2 in Hedgehog/GLI signaling.

citation: ARHGAP4 regulates the cell migration and invasion of pancreatic cancer by the HDAC2/β-catenin signaling pathway (PMID: 30958531)
summary: ARHGAP4 interacts with and ubiquitinates HDAC2, which inhibits β-catenin activation. The HDAC2 inhibitor CAY10683 and the Wnt inhibitor XAV939 attenuated the effects of ARHGAP4 silencing on invasion and migration, and on MMP2/MMP9 expression, in pancreatic cancer cells. This places HDAC2 in the Wnt/β-catenin pathway.

citation: E3 ligase RCHY1 negatively regulates HDAC2 (PMID: 31630802)
summary: RCHY1 directly interacts with HDAC2, and ectopic RCHY1 lowered HDAC2 levels in p53 wild-type, mutant and null cancer cells. RCHY1 knockdown raised HDAC2 levels, and the RING mutant lacked this effect. RCHY1 and HDAC2 levels were inversely correlated in tumor tissue in a meta-analysis of six datasets.

citation: N6-methyladenosine-modified SENP1, identified by IGF2BP3, ... activating AKT signal via de-SUMOylating HDAC2 (PMID: 38822351)
summary: Co-IP showed SENP1 binds HDAC2 in AML cells, and SENP1 de-SUMOylates HDAC2. This enhances EGFR transcription (ChIP-qPCR) and activates AKT/mTOR signaling, promoting AML proliferation and anti-apoptosis.

citation: HDAC2 Induces DNA Methyltransferase DNMT3B Expression to Regulate the Wnt Signaling Pathway and Thus Promotes Glioma Development and Progression (PMID: 36267089)
summary: ChIP showed HDAC2 is enriched on the DNMT3B promoter and activates its transcription. DNMT3B in turn represses Bcl2 and promotes Wnt pathway activity. HDAC2 and DNMT3B are highly expressed in glioma and associated with poor prognosis, and the axis promotes glioma activity in vitro and in vivo.

citation: MiR-646 prevents proliferation and progression of human breast cancer cell lines by suppressing HDAC2 expression (PMID: 32777446)
sample_size: 30 tumor/30 adjacent normal tissues; 3 breast cancer cell lines
summary: HDAC2 was significantly upregulated in breast cancer tissues and cell lines compared with adjacent non-cancerous tissue and a normal cell line. miR-646 directly targets HDAC2. HDAC2 knockout or miR-646 overexpression inhibited growth and promoted cell death.

citation: Inactivation of HDAC1 or HDAC2 induces gamma globin expression without altering cell cycle or proliferation (PMID: 25808664)
summary: shRNA knockdown of HDAC2 or HDAC1 in human erythroid progenitors induced gamma globin without changing proliferation or cell cycle. HDAC2 knockdown combined with hydroxyurea gave a further increase in gamma globin. The HDAC1/2/3 inhibitor MS-275 was additive with hydroxyurea in CD34+ cells.

citation: Neural stem cell differentiation is dictated by distinct actions of nuclear receptor corepressors and histone deacetylases (PMID: 25241747)
summary: Genome-wide analysis showed HDAC2 and HDAC3 have overlapping and distinct promoter occupancy at neuronal and oligodendrocyte genes in neural stem cells. HDAC2 directly represses Sox8 and Sox10. Loss of HDAC2 or NCOR with T3 increased oligodendrocyte gene expression, whereas HDAC3 loss, but not HDAC2 loss, initiated neuronal differentiation.

citation: YTHDC1 is downregulated by the YY1/HDAC2 complex and controls the sensitivity of ccRCC to sunitinib by targeting the ANXA1-MAPK pathway (PMID: 35974388)
summary: HDAC2 acts in a YY1/HDAC2 complex that downregulates YTHDC1 in ccRCC, defining a YY1/HDAC2/YTHDC1/ANXA1 axis. HDAC2 inhibitors resensitized ccRCC cells to tyrosine kinase inhibitors such as sunitinib.

citation: ASHG 2022 - Systematic analysis of nonsense-mediated decay escaping protein-truncating variants in 97,728 clinical exomes identifies new Mendelian disease genes
summary: Two patients with syndromic neurodevelopmental disorder carried de novo NMD-escaping protein-truncating variants in HDAC2. HDAC2 was identified as a candidate novel disease gene, consistent with histone modifiers being a known NDD mechanism.

citation: Rolandic epilepsies CNV study - A subset of genomic alterations detected in rolandic epilepsies contains candidate or known epilepsy genes including GRIN2A and PRRT2 (PMID: 24372385)
variant_detail: Rare CNV (microdeletion/microduplication) comprising or disrupting PRKCE; exact coordinates and copy-number state not given in abstract
phenotype: Rolandic epilepsy (childhood focal epilepsy); Possible cognitive, speech, language, reading or behavioral comorbidity (not specified for this patient)
diagnostic_reason: PRKCE was listed among strong candidate genes for epilepsy and neurodevelopmental disorders disrupted by rare CNVs. The authors state that only a subset of the CNVs may contribute to the phenotype, and inheritance for this CNV is not specified in the abstract.

citation: Contiguous gene deletion of chromosome 2p16.3-p21 as a cause of Lynch syndrome (PMID: 28555354)
variant_detail: 4.8 Mb heterozygous deletion at 2p16.3-p21 (SNP array) spanning MSH2, MSH6, EPCAM, NRXN1, CALM2, FBXO11, PRKCE and other genes
phenotype: Lynch syndrome; Prostatic adenocarcinoma; Synchronous sigmoid adenocarcinoma with MSH2/MSH6 loss; Intellectual disability; Short stature; Brachycephaly; Narrow forehead; Short philtrum; Brachydactyly; Palmar transverse crease; Broad small feet; Sole hyperpigmentation
diagnostic_reason: Lynch syndrome was attributed to deletion of MSH2, MSH6 and EPCAM. PRKCE was only one of many co-deleted genes, so its specific contribution is unknown. Family history was unrevealing.

citation: ASHG 2018 - A copy number variation map of pediatric neuropsychiatric traits
variant_detail: Rare CNVs affecting PRKCE (details not specified)
phenotype: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) traits
diagnostic_reason: PRKCE was named as one of the genes driving the OCD-trait association signal in the burden and locus analyses of rare CNVs and SNVs/indels. This is a statistical association, not individual-level pathogenicity.
center_country: The Hospital for Sick Children, Toronto, Canada (Spit for Science cohort)

citation: Association between de novo variants of nuclear-encoded mitochondrial-related genes and undiagnosed developmental disorder and autism (PMID: 37930872)
variant_detail: De novo variant(s) in PRKCE among published UDD/ASD cohorts. The table appears to show about 1 de novo variant per category, but variant details are not given.
phenotype: Undiagnosed developmental disorder; Autism spectrum disorder
diagnostic_reason: PRKCE was among the nuclear-encoded mitochondrial-related genes tested with the TADA-denovo model for excess de novo variants. The PRKCE row is not clearly a prioritized gene, and no per-patient phenotyping is given.

citation: Construction of copy number variation landscape and characterization of associated genes in a Bangladeshi cohort of neurodevelopmental disorders (PMID: 36959829)
variant_detail: Rare CNV(s) encompassing PRKCE, listed among 18 critical-exon genes in smaller CNVs
phenotype: Neurodevelopmental disorder (autism/intellectual disability spectrum)
diagnostic_reason: PRKCE was a critical-exon gene (gene constraint metric) located within pathogenic or VUS CNVs. It was not prioritized as a candidate, because PSMC3 was selected instead.

citation: 2025 - Deletion of the SHORT Syndrome Gene Prkce Results in Brain Atrophy and Cognitive and Motor Behavior Deficits in Mice (PMID: 40914752)
phenotype: cerebral atrophy; cerebellar atrophy; motor deficits; social deficits; cognitive deficits; down-regulated VEGF/PI3K-induced AKT activation; abnormal brain development

citation: Maternal Prkce expression in mature oocytes is critical for the first cleavage facilitating maternal-to-zygotic transition in mouse early embryos (PMID: 35582855)
phenotype: reduced 2-cell rate of embryos from Prkce-/- oocytes (32.4% vs 80.1% in wild type); rescued by Prkce cRNA injection (76.7%); 143 differentially expressed genes, enriched in cell cycle regulation; impaired first cleavage and maternal-to-zygotic transition

citation: Identification of Myeloid Protein Kinase C Epsilon as a Novel Atheroprotective Gene (PMID: 40703062)
phenotype: larger atherosclerotic plaques; larger foam cells; larger necrotic regions; thinner collagen caps; increased macrophage cholesterol and lipid droplet retention; higher expression of endocytosis genes; more lipid-containing endosomes; global PKCε knockout bone marrow-derived macrophages also tested for lipid retention and cytokine secretion

citation: PKCε phosphorylates α4β2 nicotinic ACh receptors and promotes recovery from desensitization (PMID: 26103136)
phenotype: reduced α4 nAChR subunit phosphorylation in synaptosomes; more severe and prolonged sazetidine-A-induced hypothermia; prolonged nicotinic receptor desensitization

citation: Protein kinase C epsilon modulates nicotine consumption and dopamine reward signals in the nucleus accumbens (PMID: 21911393)
phenotype: decreased nicotine self-administration; decreased conditioned place preference for nicotine; reduced α6 and β3 nicotinic receptor subunit mRNA in ventral midbrain and striatum; deficit in cholinergic modulation of dopamine release in nucleus accumbens

citation: Novel Small-Molecule Inhibitors of Protein Kinase C Epsilon Reduce Ethanol Consumption in Mice (PMID: 29198469)
phenotype: PKCε inhibitors reduced ethanol consumption in wild-type but not Prkce-/- mice; off-target locomotor impairment and prolonged loss of righting recovery persisted in Prkce-/- mice; Prkce-/- mice used as genetic control

citation: Time-dependent effects of Prkce deletion on glucose homeostasis and hepatic lipid metabolism on dietary lipid oversupply in mice (PMID: 21347625)
phenotype: protected from high-fat-diet-induced glucose intolerance (normal glucose and insulin at 1 week); increased liver triacylglycerol in fat-fed mice; altered hepatic lipid partitioning with increased fatty acid esterification; no fat-diet-induced rise in oxygen consumption or liver mitochondrial respiration; reduced ROS production in hepatocytes with palmitate; increased glucose-stimulated insulin secretion after 16 weeks of fat feeding

citation: Deletion of protein kinase Cε in mice has limited effects on liver metabolite levels but alters fasting ketogenesis and gluconeogenesis (PMID: 22814763)
phenotype: reduced liver 4-hydroxyproline and aspartate, increased glutamate; better maintenance of blood glucose on fasting; lower β-hydroxybutyrate on fasting; lower liver and plasma lipids on fasting; smaller reduction in fat pad mass on fasting

citation: Diverse roles for protein kinase C delta and protein kinase C epsilon in the generation of high-fat-diet-induced glucose intolerance in mice: regulation of lipogenesis by protein kinase C delta (PMID: 19809797)
phenotype: protected against high-fat-diet-induced glucose intolerance via enhanced insulin availability; enhanced PKCδ activation in muscle

citation: Wang et al. 2021 - FAIM regulates autophagy through glutaminolysis in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 34720024)
summary: FAIM promotes GAC (glutaminase C) tetramer formation by increasing PRKCE/PKCε-mediated phosphorylation of GAC. This raises α-ketoglutarate production and activates MTOR, suppressing autophagy. PKCε therefore acts as a GAC kinase within the glutaminolysis–MTOR–autophagy axis in lung adenocarcinoma cells.

citation: SHORT syndrome due to a novel de novo mutation in PRKCE (Protein Kinase Cɛ) impairing TORC2-dependent AKT activation (PMID: 28934384)
sample_size: 1 proband plus parents; patient lymphoblastoid cell lines, HEK293 cells
summary: A de novo PRKCE variant was found by exome sequencing in a child with SHORT syndrome who had no PIK3R1 mutation. Kinase assays showed partial loss of function. The mutant kept its PDK1 and SIN1 interactions, but bound SIN1 with higher affinity and had altered mTORC2-dependent priming. It impaired mTORC2-dependent pAKT-S473, and patient lymphoblasts showed reduced pFOXO1-S256 and pS6-S240/244.

citation: Maternal Prkce expression in mature oocytes is critical for the first cleavage facilitating maternal-to-zygotic transition in mouse early embryos (PMID: 35582855)
summary: Prkce transcript level in mature oocytes correlates with 2-cell rate across inbred mouse strains. Prkce knockout oocytes had a reduced 2-cell rate (32.4% vs 80.1%), which Prkce cRNA injection rescued (76.7%). Knockout caused 143 DEGs enriched for cell cycle regulation.

citation: Time-dependent effects of Prkce deletion on glucose homeostasis and hepatic lipid metabolism on dietary lipid oversupply in mice (PMID: 21347625)
summary: Prkce-/- mice were protected from high-fat-diet-induced glucose intolerance. Early protection was linked to altered hepatic lipid partitioning (increased esterification, higher liver triacylglycerol), lack of diet-induced mitochondrial oxygen consumption and reduced ROS. Later protection was linked to enhanced glucose-stimulated insulin secretion.

citation: MicroRNA-146a targets PRKCE to modulate papillary thyroid tumor development (PMID: 23457043)
summary: A luciferase reporter assay confirmed that miR-146a directly binds the PRKCE 3'-UTR. miR-146a overexpression lowered PKCε levels in NPA-187 PTC cells and increased apoptosis. It also inhibited xenograft tumor growth, implicating PKCε in Ras/Raf-1 signaling, anti-apoptosis and NF-κB feedback.

citation: miR-21-5p/PRKCE axis implicated in immune infiltration and poor prognosis of kidney renal clear cell carcinoma (PMID: 36186442)
sample_size: TCGA/GEO cohorts; ACHN and Caki-1 cells
summary: PRKCE expression is decreased in KIRC tumors compared with normal tissue, and low expression is associated with poor survival and advanced stage. High PRKCE promoter methylation and miR-21-5p may explain the low expression. PRKCE overexpression suppressed proliferation, migration and invasion of ACHN and Caki-1 cells, and PRKCE correlates with immune infiltration.

citation: Fetal exposure to cocaine causes programming of Prkce gene repression in the left ventricle of adult rat offspring (PMID: 18945988)
summary: Prenatal cocaine decreased Prkce mRNA in the left ventricle of adult male offspring. Methylation of the Sp1 binding sites (-346 and -268) in the Prkce promoter increased, which reduced SP1 binding. Reporter assays showed these Sp1 sites strongly stimulate Prkce promoter activity, so the repression is epigenetic.

citation: DNA methylation analysis in nonalcoholic fatty liver disease suggests distinct disease-specific and remodeling signatures after bariatric surgery (PMID: 23931760)
summary: PRKCE showed NAFLD-specific DNA methylation and mRNA expression differences in liver. This was replicated by bisulfite pyrosequencing, and PRKCE is grouped with insulin/IGF signaling genes (IGF1, IGFBP2).

citation: A systematic review and meta-analysis of genetic association studies for the role of inflammation and the immune system in diabetic nephropathy (PMID: 28616206)
sample_size: 103 association studies in the review overall
summary: In a meta-analysis of genetic association studies, PRKCE variants were associated with increased risk of diabetic nephropathy.

citation: Genes associated with cognitive performance in the Morris water maze: an RNA-seq study (PMID: 33328525)
summary: Hippocampal Prkce expression was higher in high-performing than low-performing Morris water maze mice. It is grouped with AMPA receptor signaling and glutamatergic transmission/LTP genes.

citation: Array-Based Comparative Genomic Hybridization Analysis in Children with Developmental Delay/Intellectual Disability (PMID: 36249514)
variant_detail: De novo multi-gene CNV (copy-number type not stated in the available text) that includes ATRN together with PTPRA, GNRH2, MRPS26, OXT, AVP, LZTS3, ITPA, SLC4A11, ADAM33, SIGLEC1 and HSPA12B (case 30, F-4). ATRN is not specifically implicated.
phenotype: Developmental delay/intellectual disability (cohort inclusion criterion; individual features not given in the available text)
diagnostic_reason: Classified as a de novo variant of uncertain significance (VUS) with no subclassification. The CNV spans many genes and ATRN is not singled out as causal.
center_country: Not stated in the available text (likely Turkey)

citation: Post-developmental extracellular proteoglycan maintenance in attractin-deficient mice (PMID: 32580758)
phenotype: Severe loss of extracellular proteoglycan between kidney tubules; Loss of glycosylated material in the intratubular brush border; Depleted extracellular matrix between hepatocytes in the liver; Swollen liver sinuses; Aberrant proteoglycan-dependent space of Disse; Generalized defect in extracellular proteoglycan deposition (consistent with a secretory vesicle pathway defect)

citation: Attractin Participates in Schizophrenia by Affecting Testosterone Levels (PMID: 34869343)
phenotype: More pronounced attack behavior in adult atrn-/- fish in tracking analysis; Elevated testosterone levels; Upregulation of cyp51 and hsd17b7 (testosterone synthesis genes) in brains of adults and larvae

citation: Agouti protein, mahogunin, and attractin in pheomelanogenesis and melanoblast-like alteration of melanocytes: a cAMP-independent pathway (PMID: 19493315)
phenotype: Atrn-null melanocytes still responded to ASIP and ASIP-YY with reduced cAMP; Only ASIP, not ASIP-YY, altered proliferation and (in part) shape of Atrn-null melanocytes; Supports a cAMP-independent ASIP-MC1R pathway requiring attractin and mahogunin
knockout_type: other (spontaneous mutant Atrn mg-3J/mg-3J melanocyte line, in vitro)

citation: Alkbh4 and Atrn Act Maternally to Regulate Zebrafish Epiboly (PMID: 28924386)
phenotype: Maternal Atrn plays a role similar to Alkbh4 in embryonic morphogenesis; Regulates actomyosin formation; Regulates epiboly during gastrulation (epiboly defects); Atrn interacts with active Alkbh4 to regulate actin demethylation

citation: Mitochondrial dysfunction precedes neurodegeneration in mahogunin (Mgrn1) mutant mice (PMID: 17720281)
phenotype: Mitochondrial dysfunction in Atrn mutant brains; Increased oxidative stress in Atrn mutant brains; Age-dependent spongiform neurodegeneration in Atrn- and Mgrn1-deficient mice
knockout_type: other (spontaneous Atrn mutant mice, studied alongside Mgrn1 mutants)

citation: RML prions act through Mahogunin and Attractin-independent pathways (PMID: 23787699)
phenotype: Atrn null mice accumulate brain vacuoles resembling prion disease, but without protease-resistant PrP-scrapie accumulation and without becoming sick; Loss of ATRN had no effect on onset or progression of RML prion disease after intracerebral inoculation

citation: Absence-like and tonic seizures in aspartoacylase/attractin double-mutant mice (PMID: 17460362)
phenotype: Absence-like and tonic seizures; 5-7 Hz spike-wave-like complexes and low voltage fast waves on EEG; Simultaneous loss of Aspa and Atrn causes epileptic seizures
knockout_type: other (Aspa knockout combined with Atrn mg-3J mutant allele, double homozygous)

citation: Biochemical and genetic studies of pigment-type switching (PMID: 11041357)
phenotype: mahogany (Atrn) mutation suppresses the pigmentary effects of Agouti; mahogany suppresses the effects of Ay on pigmentation and body weight; mg is genetically upstream of Mc1r

citation: Positional cloning of rat mutant genes reveals new functions of these genes (PMID: 36058846)
phenotype: Marked reduction of membrane-bound Atrn expression in zitter rat brain; Neurological impairments and neurodegenerative changes; Darkened coat color when introduced into agouti rats; Myelination-related abnormalities
knockout_type: other (spontaneous zitter mutation, 8-bp splice donor deletion in Atrn)

citation: Mutation of the attractin gene impairs working memory in rats (PMID: 36621889)
summary: CRISPR/Cas9 ATRN-G505C knock-in rats showed longer latency and distance to the escape platform in the Morris water maze working-memory test. Myelin basic protein (MBP) expression was reduced on western blot, suggesting that ATRN mutation impairs spatial cognition through reduced MBP.

citation: Attractin Gene Deficiency in Rats Leads to Impairments in Both Activity and Spatial Learning and Memory (PMID: 34000322)
summary: ATRN-G505C knock-in rats (exon 9) showed impaired Morris water maze performance and reduced open field distance. BDNF expression was significantly reduced by western blot and immunohistochemistry, linking ATRN to learning, memory and neurodegeneration-related changes.

citation: Post-developmental extracellular proteoglycan maintenance in attractin-deficient mice (PMID: 32580758)
summary: Atrn-mutant mice lose extracellular proteoglycan in kidney and liver and show disrupted space of Disse. This supports a role for transmembrane attractin in the secretory vesicle/proteoglycan deposition pathway.

citation: The neuroprotective role of attractin in neurodegeneration (PMID: 16860906)
summary: Atrn knockdown worsened and Atrn overexpression protected against neuronal death induced by MPP+ and lactacystin. Atrn also modulated cytochrome c and AIF release, implicating it in mitochondrial function. Most mouse dopaminergic neurons express Atrn, and expression declines with age.

citation: Genetic analysis of attractin homologs (PMID: 18064672)
summary: Atrn-null mice show dark fur, spongiform neurodegeneration, hypomyelination, tremor and reduced adiposity. Atrnl1 mutants are normal, but a beta-actin-driven Atrnl1 transgene rescues the agouti banding and delays neurodegeneration in Atrn-null mice. The two paralogs are therefore redundant in gain-of-function but not loss-of-function settings.

citation: The myelin vacuolation (mv) rat with a null mutation in the attractin gene (PMID: 12379762)
summary: The mv rat has a genomic deletion including Atrn exon 1 and no Atrn mRNA in brain. It shows tremor and CNS myelin vacuolation with splitting of myelin lamellae. The phenotype maps to the Atrn locus and is allelic with zitter.

citation: Does human attractin have DP4 activity? (PMID: 17261078)
summary: Attractin purified from human plasma has no intrinsic DP4 (dipeptidyl peptidase 4) activity; the activity came from a DP4 impurity. Recombinant attractin isoforms also lacked DP4 activity, so attractin likely acts as a receptor or adhesion protein rather than a protease.

citation: Molecular and phenotypic analysis of Attractin mutant mice (PMID: 11514456)
summary: Three Atrn alleles (mg-3J, mg, mg-L) cause loss-of-function pigmentation and neurodegeneration phenotypes, with severity tracking normal Atrn mRNA levels. Mutants have reduced body weight and adiposity and increased locomotor activity despite normal food intake, suggesting increased energy expenditure. Pigmentation is more sensitive to Atrn mRNA levels than the other phenotypes.

citation: Attractin Participates in Schizophrenia by Affecting Testosterone Levels (PMID: 34869343)
sample_size: 9,008 psychiatric patients, 247 controls; 14 ATRN mutation carriers
summary: atrn-/- zebrafish show increased attack behavior, elevated testosterone, and upregulated cyp51 and hsd17b7 in the brain. In patients, ATRN expression was reduced in a subset of extreme-phenotype subjects. Fourteen subjects carrying ATRN mutations all had abnormal testosterone, linking ATRN to sex-dimorphic psychiatric phenotypes.

citation: Agouti protein, mahogunin, and attractin in pheomelanogenesis and melanoblast-like alteration of melanocytes: a cAMP-independent pathway (PMID: 19493315)
summary: Atrn-null (mg-3J) melanocytes still showed the cAMP response to ASIP but lacked its effects on proliferation and shape. This places attractin, together with mahogunin, in a cAMP-independent branch of ASIP-MC1R signaling.

citation: Clinical, molecular and glycophenotype insights in SLC39A8-CDG (PMID: 34246313)

diagnostic_reason: Novel biallelic SLC39A8 variants in two siblings with a phenotype consistent with SLC39A8-CDG (clinical, MRI and glycomic features). Homozygous A391T in a third patient with overlapping features.

phenotype: severe developmental disability; dystonic postural pattern and dyskinesia; Leigh syndrome-like neuroimaging (basal ganglia, thalami, white matter); cerebral and cerebellar atrophy; variable or near-normal transferrin IEF; undergalactosylated and undersialylated serum N-glycans
diagnostic_reason: Novel biallelic SLC39A8 variants in two siblings with a phenotype consistent with SLC39A8-CDG (clinical, MRI and glycomic features). Homozygous A391T in a third patient with overlapping features.

diagnostic_reason: Novel biallelic SLC39A8 variants in two siblings with a phenotype consistent with SLC39A8-CDG (clinical, MRI and glycomic features). Homozygous A391T in a third patient with overlapping features.

citation: The schizophrenia risk locus in SLC39A8 alters brain metal transport and plasma glycosylation (PMID: 32753748)
variant_detail: p.Ala391Thr (rs13107325), common missense allele; human carriers (dose-dependent, including heterozygotes)
phenotype: dose-dependent change in brain MRI T2w/T1w signal ratio in several regions; specific reduction of serum manganese; reduced complexity and branching of plasma N-glycans; schizophrenia risk allele
diagnostic_reason: Common schizophrenia-associated missense variant shown to be hypofunctional: lower serum Mn, altered plasma N-glycome and brain MRI changes in carriers. Two individuals with SLC39A8-CDG were also profiled and had more severe glycosylation changes that improved with Mn supplementation.

citation: A missense variant in SLC39A8 is associated with severe idiopathic scoliosis (PMID: 30301978)
variant_detail: p.Ala391Thr (rs13107325), minor allele carriers (largely heterozygous)
phenotype: severe adolescent idiopathic scoliosis; greater spinal curvature; decreased height; increased BMI; lower plasma manganese
diagnostic_reason: Exome-wide association in 457 severe AIS cases (discovery) plus 841 cases (replication) versus controls (combined P = 7.02e-14, OR 1.94); reduced Mn influx by the variant in functional studies; slc39a8 mutant zebrafish show vertebral abnormalities.

citation: Lin et al. 2018 - Zinc transporter Slc39a8 is essential for cardiac ventricular compaction (PMID: 29337306)
phenotype: Homozygous null embryos do not survive embryogenesis; Cardiac phenotype similar to human left ventricular noncompaction (excessive trabeculation, impaired compaction); Slc39a8 expressed in endothelial cells of the developing heart, where it maintains cellular Zn levels; Marked ECM accumulation in null hearts; Reduced expression of several Adamts metalloproteinases; SLC39A8 knockdown in HUVECs decreased ADAMTS1 transcription via reduced Zn uptake and MTF1 activity

citation: In utero gene expression in the Slc39a8(neo/neo) knockdown mouse (PMID: 30013175)
phenotype: ZIP8 mRNA and protein at 10-15% of wild-type; Stunted growth; Neonatal lethality; Multi-organ dysmorphogenesis; Dysregulated hematopoiesis with severe anemia; RNA-seq of GD13.5 yolk sac/placenta and GD16.5 tissues showed 29 unique DEGs enriched for hematopoiesis, hypoxia, complement and coagulation categories; Altered zinc-finger/GATA-related transcription factor targets, predominantly in yolk sac

citation: Generation of a Slc39a8 hypomorph mouse: markedly decreased ZIP8 Zn2+/(HCO3-)2 transporter expression (PMID: 21658371)
phenotype: Slc39a8(neo) hypomorphic allele; Slc39a8(neo/neo) homozygotes show dramatically decreased ZIP8 expression in embryo, fetus and visceral yolk sac; Cre recombinase did not function in the intact mouse

citation: Metal-ion transporter SLC39A8 is required for brain manganese uptake and accumulation (PMID: 37482277)
phenotype: Inducible global Slc39a8 KO crossed with Slc39a14 KO; Markedly decreased brain Mn loading despite systemic hypermanganesemia and increased bone and kidney Mn; Other divalent metals in brain unaffected; 54Mn uptake impaired in brain but not most other tissues; Slc39a8 inactivation efficient in brain microvessels but not choroid plexus, suggesting blood-brain barrier uptake

citation: Neuronal SLC39A8 deficiency impairs cerebellar development by altering manganese homeostasis (PMID: 39435657)
phenotype: Neuron-specific KO (Slc39a8-NSKO) with markedly decreased Mn in whole brain, especially cerebellum; Impaired brain 54Mn uptake; Cerebellar morphological defects; Abnormal Purkinje cell dendritic arborization; Reduced neurogenesis and increased apoptosis in the external granular layer; Motor dysfunction; Downregulation of neurodevelopment, synaptic plasticity and cAMP signaling pathway genes

citation: The manganese transporter SLC39A8 links alkaline ceramidase 1 to inflammatory bowel disease (PMID: 38839750)
phenotype: Intestinal epithelial cell-specific KO with markedly decreased Mn in blood and most organs; Impaired intestinal absorption of dietary Mn; Barrier dysfunction; Upregulated alkaline ceramidase 1 (ACER1); ACER1 inhibitor attenuated colitis

citation: A missense variant in SLC39A8 is associated with severe idiopathic scoliosis (PMID: 30301978)
phenotype: slc39a8 mutant zebrafish show vertebral abnormalities; Impaired growth; Decreased motor activity

citation: A mouse model characterizes the roles of ZIP8 in systemic iron recycling and lung inflammation and infection (PMID: 36260707)
phenotype: Global inducible ZIP8 KO; Elevated spleen iron and decreased serum iron, suggesting a role in iron recycling; ZIP8 expressed on lung distal airspace epithelial cells and transports iron from airway into lung tissue; No effect on severity of LPS-induced acute lung injury; No effect on outcome of Klebsiella pneumoniae infection

citation: Intestinal ZIP8 Regulates Tissue Manganese Distribution and Modifies Manganese Overload in ZIP14 Deficiency (PMID: 41394108)
phenotype: Intestine-specific Zip8 KO did not change basal blood Mn; Reduced liver and bone Mn; In Zip14-/- background, reduced blood and brain Mn in female double KO mice only (sex-specific); Bone Mn remained elevated in all groups

citation: SLC39A8-mediated zinc dyshomeostasis potentiates kidney disease (PMID: 40956895)
phenotype: Kidney-specific Slc39a8 KO (and A391T knock-in) showed reduced renal zinc accumulation; Reduced susceptibility to kidney injury and disease progression; Activation of zinc-AKT-FOXO1-G6PC axis; EDTA zinc chelation recapitulated protection

citation: Wang et al. 2025 - SLC39A8-mediated zinc dyshomeostasis potentiates kidney disease (PMID: 40956895)
summary: Large-cohort screening identified the SLC39A8 A391T variant (rs13107325) as a shared modifier of multiple kidney diseases. A391T knock-in and kidney-specific Slc39a8 knockout mice had reduced renal zinc and were protected from kidney injury, acting through the zinc-AKT-FOXO1-G6PC axis. EDTA zinc chelation reproduced the protection in acute and chronic kidney disease models.

citation: The ZIP8/SIRT1 axis regulates alveolar progenitor cell renewal in aging and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (PMID: 35389887)
summary: ZIP8 expression was reduced in AEC2s from IPF lungs and aged mouse lungs. AEC2-specific Zip8 deletion impaired renewal, increased bleomycin sensitivity and caused spontaneous fibrosis. ZIP8 acts through SIRT1, and zinc plus SIRT1 activation restored AEC2 self-renewal in cells from IPF patients and old mice.

citation: SLC39A8 deficiency: biochemical correction and major clinical improvement by manganese therapy (PMID: 28749473)
summary: SLC39A8 deficiency causes manganese deficiency and a congenital disorder of glycosylation because Mn-dependent β-1,4-galactosyltransferases fail. High-dose MnSO4 in two patients normalized the glycosylation enzyme defects and improved motor, hearing and neurological function.

citation: The schizophrenia-associated variant in SLC39A8 alters protein glycosylation in the mouse brain (PMID: 35260802)
summary: In A391T homozygous knock-in mice, brain N-glycosylation was impaired in a region-dependent manner, and about one-third of detected cortical glycoproteins were differentially N-glycosylated. These included cell adhesion molecules and neurotransmitter receptors. RNAseq showed little regional change, pointing to altered glycosylation enzyme activity rather than altered gene expression.

citation: The schizophrenia risk locus in SLC39A8 alters brain metal transport and plasma glycosylation (PMID: 32753748)
summary: Carriers of the common SLC39A8 missense allele (A391T) showed a dose-dependent change in brain MRI T2w/T1w signal ratio, a specific reduction in serum Mn, and reduced complexity and branching of plasma N-glycans. Two SLC39A8-CDG patients had similar but more severe glycan changes that improved with Mn supplementation, suggesting a spectrum of hypofunction.

citation: Co-expression analysis reveals interpretable gene modules controlled by trans-acting genetic variants (PMID: 32880574)
sample_size: 226-710 individuals across six blood cell types
summary: A trans-eQTL near SLC39A8 regulates a metallothionein gene module in LPS-stimulated monocytes. The effect is mediated by a transient cis-eQTL present only in early LPS response.

citation: Identification of mouse SLC39A8 as the transporter responsible for cadmium-induced toxicity in the testis (PMID: 15722412)
summary: ZIP8 expression in mouse fetal fibroblasts increased Cd influx more than 10-fold and Cd-induced cell death sensitivity 30-fold. In situ hybridization showed ZIP8 mRNA in testicular vascular endothelial cells of Cd-sensitive mouse strains but not resistant strains, identifying Slc39a8 as the Cdm locus.

citation: Generation of a Slc39a8 hypomorph mouse: markedly decreased ZIP8 Zn²⁺/(HCO₃⁻)₂ transporter expression (PMID: 21658371)
summary: ZIP8 functions as an electroneutral Zn2+/(HCO3-)2 symporter. The Slc39a8(neo) hypomorphic allele greatly reduced ZIP8 expression in embryo, fetus and visceral yolk sac of homozygous mice.

citation: MicroRNA-488 regulates zinc transporter SLC39A8/ZIP8 during pathogenesis of osteoarthritis (PMID: 23688035)
summary: miR-488 targets ZIP8 and is decreased in OA chondrocytes. IL-1β suppresses miR-488 while TGF-β3 induces it. Suppressing ZIP8 in an OA animal model reduced cartilage degradation, and miR-488 inhibits MMP-13 activity through ZIP8.

citation: Calcium and the Ca-ATPase SPCA1 modulate plasma membrane abundance of ZIP8 and ZIP14 to regulate Mn(II) uptake in brain microvascular endothelial cells (PMID: 35787370)
summary: In human brain microvascular endothelial cells, SPCA1 knockdown raised cytoplasmic Ca2+, which increased plasma membrane localization of ZIP8 and ZIP14 and 54Mn uptake. SPCA1 overexpression and Ca2+ chelation had the opposite effect, showing that Ca2+ and SPCA1 regulate ZIP8 membrane cycling.

phenotype: severe anxiety; obsessive-compulsive behaviors; developmental delay; autism; intellectual disability; hyperphagia; obesity; macrocephaly; dysmorphic features
diagnostic_reason: De novo heterozygous nonsense variant identified by exome sequencing, predicted to cause loss of normal protein function; supported by animal models and CNVs encompassing NLGN2

diagnostic_reason: De novo missense mutation in NLGN2 in a patient with ASD and catatonia; considered pathogenic by authors
center_country: Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center, USA

citation: A child with febrile and atypical absence seizures caused by a NLGN2 variant (PMID: 37506563)

phenotype: febrile seizures; atypical absence seizures
diagnostic_reason: Title attributes seizures to an NLGN2 variant; no abstract available to confirm details

variant_detail: additional de novo variant in NLGN2 (specific change not provided) in one TAOK1 patient
phenotype: neurodevelopmental phenotype (in context of TAOK1 variant; unclear NLGN2 contribution)
diagnostic_reason: NLGN2 listed as a candidate gene with a second de novo variant; unclear whether it contributes to the phenotype

citation: Babaev et al. 2016 - Neuroligin 2 deletion alters inhibitory synapse function and anxiety-associated neuronal activation in the amygdala (PMID: 26142252)

citation: Hoon/Schmitt et al. 2021 - Altered theta and beta oscillatory synchrony in a genetic mouse model of pathological anxiety (PMID: 33960026)
phenotype: Increased center avoidance in open field; Profoundly increased vHPC LFP power; Abnormal theta synchrony in the vHPC-mPFC-BLA circuit; Increased beta and gamma synchrony across the network; vHPC deletion linked to immobility; BLA deletion linked to reduced exploratory activity
knockout_type: full knockout and local (region-specific) conditional deletion in vHPC and BLA

citation: Hoon et al. 2017/2018 - IgSF9b regulates anxiety behaviors through effects on centromedial amygdala inhibitory synapses (PMID: 30573727)
phenotype: Nlgn2 KO mice show anxiety-related behaviors and altered neural processing; IgSF9b deletion normalizes anxiety behaviors and neural processing in Nlgn2 KO mice; Differential effects of Nlgn2 and IgSF9b at inhibitory synapses in basal amygdala vs centromedial amygdala; CeM IgSF9b deletion in adult Nlgn2 KO has an anxiolytic effect
knockout_type: full knockout (Nlgn2 KO, with IgSF9b double deletion and CeM-specific deletion in adult Nlgn2 KO)

citation: Ferrer et al. 2018 - The effect of Neuroligin-2 absence on sleep architecture and electroencephalographic activity in mice (PMID: 30231918)
phenotype: More wakefulness and less NREM and REM sleep, especially in the dark period; Altered number and duration of wake/sleep episodes (state consolidation changes); Widespread EEG spectral changes in all states; Abnormal hypersynchronized EEG events during wakefulness and REM sleep; Altered daily time course of NREM delta activity (sleep homeostasis)

citation: Wöhr et al. 2013 - Developmental delays and reduced pup ultrasonic vocalizations but normal sociability in mice lacking the postsynaptic cell adhesion protein neuroligin2 (PMID: 22820233)
phenotype: Reduced breeding efficiency; High reactivity to handling; Normal social behavior; Reduced exploratory activity; Impaired rotarod performance; Delays in several developmental milestones; No stereotypies or repetitive behaviors; Normal sensory processing and sensorimotor gating; Fewer pup ultrasonic vocalizations and less calling time
sample_size: low numbers of adult Nlgn2-/- mice available

citation: Liang et al. 2015 - Conditional neuroligin-2 knockout in adult medial prefrontal cortex links chronic changes in synaptic inhibition to cognitive impairments (PMID: 25824299)
phenotype: Nlgn2 protein undetectable 2-3 weeks after cKO; Major reductions in synaptic inhibition after 6-7 weeks; Impaired anxiety behavior; Impaired fear memory; Impaired social interaction; Impaired behavioral stimulation of immediate-early gene expression in the mPFC

phenotype: Homozygotes viable and fertile; Growth retardation; Anxiety-like behavior; Increased prepulse inhibition; Impaired spatial learning and memory; No NLGN2 protein expression in homozygotes; Sex-by-genotype interaction in elevated plus maze
knockout_type: knock-in (R215H; homozygotes lack NLGN2 protein, resembling KO)

citation: Crescenzo et al. 2018 - Modulation of Angiopoietin 2 release from endothelial cells and angiogenesis by the synaptic protein Neuroligin 2 (PMID: 29709479)
phenotype: Immature retinal vasculature; Immature vasculature in tumor xenografts grown in NLGN2-null mice; Lower pericyte coverage; Lower Tie2 phosphorylation; In vitro silencing reduced Angiopoietin 2 release and increased Weibel-Palade body retention
knockout_type: full knockout (plus in vitro knockdown in endothelial cells)

citation: Cell-type-specific role for nucleus accumbens neuroligin-2 in depression and stress susceptibility (PMID: 29339486)
summary: NLGN2 expression is reduced in the nucleus accumbens of patients with major depressive disorder. Chronic social defeat stress lowers Nlgn2 selectively in D1-positive cells of stress-susceptible mice. Cell-type-specific knockdown gave opposite effects: D1 knockdown promoted subordination and stress susceptibility, while D2 knockdown promoted active defensive behavior.

citation: A neuroligin-2-YAP axis regulates progression of pancreatic intraepithelial neoplasia (PMID: 38413734)
summary: NLGN2 is expressed in pancreatic exocrine cells and localizes to tight junctions in acinar cells. It is lost in high-grade PanINs and many advanced PDACs. NLGN2 is needed to form the PALS1/PATJ complex, which reduces YAP function and induces contact inhibition and epithelial polarity.

citation: Physical Interactions and Functional Relationships of Neuroligin 2 and Midbrain Serotonin Transporters (PMID: 26793096)
summary: NLGN2 co-immunoprecipitates with SERT in mouse midbrain, together with NRXN and gephyrin. The interaction is Ca2+-independent, consistent with a cis interaction in somatodendritic compartments, and is absent in hippocampus. Tph2 and Nlgn2 mRNA are co-expressed in dorsal raphe. Nlgn2 null mice show reduced SERT expression and function, reduced raphe 5-HT neuron excitability, loss of GABAA IPSCs, increased 5-HT1A autoreceptor sensitivity, and behavioral changes.

citation: Identification and functional characterization of rare mutations of the neuroligin-2 gene (NLGN2) associated with schizophrenia (PMID: 21551456)
summary: Sequencing NLGN2 found 19 variants, including six rare missense mutations. The R215H mutant is a loss-of-function variant for GABAergic synaptogenesis in cell assays and electrophysiology. It is retained in the ER and not trafficked to the cell membrane. Incomplete penetrance was seen in the family.

citation: Neuroligin 2 deletion alters inhibitory synapse function and anxiety-associated neuronal activation in the amygdala (PMID: 26142252)
summary: Nlgn2 is present at most inhibitory synapses in the basal amygdala. Its deletion disrupts perisomatic postsynaptic structures and impairs inhibitory transmission onto projection neurons. Knockout mice show anxiety and exaggerated cFOS induction in CaMKII-positive projection neurons.

citation: GABAergic deficits and schizophrenia-like behaviors in a mouse model carrying patient-derived neuroligin-2 R215H mutation (PMID: 29859117)
summary: R215H knock-in mice show a marked loss of NL2 protein in vivo, reduced GABAergic transmission, and impaired hippocampal activation. They display anxiety-like behavior, impaired PPI, cognitive deficits, and abnormal stress responses, modeling schizophrenia-like phenotypes.

citation: Chronic stress induces depression through MDGA1-Neuroligin2 mediated suppression of inhibitory synapses in the lateral habenula (PMID: 39897557)
summary: MDGA1 and Nlgn2 interact selectively in the lateral habenula, and the interaction increases after chronic restraint stress. An Nlgn2 variant unable to bind MDGA1 increases GABAergic transmission and synapse density and confers resistance to stress-induced depressive behaviors. MDGA1 therefore suppresses Nlgn2-mediated inhibitory synapse formation.

citation: Whole-genome expression analysis reveals genes associated with treatment response to escitalopram in major depression (PMID: 27461515)
summary: In peripheral blood expression profiling, baseline NLGN2 expression predicted escitalopram treatment outcome. It distinguished low-dose responders from treatment-resistant patients.

citation: PSD-95 deficiency alters GABAergic inhibition in the prefrontal cortex (PMID: 32818520)
summary: In PSD-95+/- mice, NLGN2 is upregulated and shows increased trafficking, together with reduced GSK3β activity (tyr-216 phosphorylation). This is associated with enhanced GABAergic inhibition in the mPFC, linking NLGN2 to the PSD-95/GSK3β regulation of inhibitory synapses.

citation: Expression and structural analysis of human neuroligin 2 and neuroligin 3 implicated in autism spectrum disorders (PMID: 36479216)
summary: Cryo-EM structures of human NLGN2 and NLGN3 were solved. The two protomers in each homodimer are rotated relative to each other, which may influence interactions with MDGAs. Expression of NLGN2 and NLGN3 was also compared across brain regions and in a streptozotocin-induced maternal diabetes ASD mouse model.

citation: H2AX promotes replication fork degradation and chemosensitivity in BRCA-deficient tumours (PMID: 38789420)
summary: γH2AX drives drug-induced replication fork degradation in BRCA1/2-deficient mammary tumours by suppressing CtIP-mediated fork protection. H2AX loss restores fork stability and PARPi chemoresistance without restoring RAD51 foci or homology-directed repair. ATM inhibition, but not ATR inhibition, resensitizes H2AX-deficient tumours. This is a role separable from classical DSB signalling.

citation: H2AX mRNA expression reflects DNA repair, cell proliferation, metastasis, and worse survival in breast cancer (PMID: 35261802)
significance: Associated with survival in two independent cohorts (p-values not given in abstract)
summary: High H2AX mRNA in breast tumours is associated with worse disease-free, disease-specific and overall survival, upregulated DNA repair, DNA replication and MYC-target gene sets, and higher MKI67. H2AX is higher in metastatic clones and metastatic tumours, and is downregulated after effective chemotherapy. H2AX knockdown reduced cell proliferation.

citation: Histone H2AX and Fanconi anemia FANCD2 function in the same pathway to maintain chromosome stability (PMID: 17304220)
summary: H2AX is a component of the FA/BRCA pathway. γH2AX is required to recruit FANCD2 to chromatin at stalled replication forks, and FANCD2 binding to γH2AX is BRCA1-dependent. H2AX-deficient cells (knockout or S136A/S139A mutant) show an FA-like phenotype with excess chromatid aberrations and MMC hypersensitivity. This sensitivity is not further increased by FANCD2 depletion, which places the two in the same pathway.

citation: H2AX deficiency is associated with erythroid dysplasia and compromised haematopoietic stem cell function (PMID: 26791933)
summary: H2AX knockout mice show cell-autonomous anaemia and erythroid dysplasia with decreased enucleation. H2AX-deficient hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells lose quiescence and engraft poorly. MDS patients with 11q23 deletion, where H2AX is located, show increased dyserythropoiesis.

citation: Histone H2AX promotes neuronal health by controlling mitochondrial homeostasis (PMID: 30910969)
summary: H2AX loss in MEFs and mouse striatum reduces mitochondrial respiratory complex subunits, disrupts mitochondrial shape, and represses PGC-1α. Ectopic PGC-1α rescues the complexes and reduces cell death. H2AX knockout mice show increased neuronal death after 3-nitropropionic acid, which supports a neuroprotective role in mitochondrial homeostasis.

citation: Acetylation-Dependent Histone H2AX Exchange Suppresses Pathological Senescence via MDC1 Degradation (PMID: 41494686)
summary: TIP60, in complex with the chaperone FACT, acetylates H2AX at K5 and drives its dynamic exchange on chromatin. This exchange promotes MDC1 degradation via a DNA-PKcs-p97 axis. Disrupting it causes MDC1 accumulation, a shift to error-prone NHEJ and a pathological senescent state.

citation: High expression of H2AX/γ-H2AX is associated with distinct biological pathway alterations and shorter survival in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (PMID: 39756240)
significance: mRNA HR 4.77, p=0.04; protein HR 2.24, p=0.03 (HPV-negative HR 3.67, p=0.007)
summary: High H2AX mRNA in TCGA OPSCC is associated with shorter overall survival and upregulation of DNA repair and cell cycle genes (CDK1, CCNB1, ZWINT). High γ-H2AX protein by IHC is associated with HPV-negative disease and is an independent predictor of poor survival.

citation: Evolved histone tail regulates 53BP1 recruitment at damaged chromatin (PMID: 38821984)
summary: The H2AX C-terminal linker region with S139 phosphorylation recruits 53BP1 independently of the MDC1-RNF8-RNF168 pathway. The recruitment is mediated by the interaction of the H2AX C-terminal tail with the 53BP1 oligomerization-Tudor domains. This γH2AX-linker-mediated recruitment confers camptothecin resistance in H2AX knockout cells.

citation: ASHG 2010 - γH2AX in pluripotent stem cells: more than a DNA damage response signal?
summary: Mouse ESCs, mouse iPSCs and blastocyst inner cell masses have high basal γH2AX without genotoxic exposure. Human ESCs have low basal γH2AX. In mESCs, γH2AX decreases with differentiation, which suggests a role beyond DNA damage signalling in pluripotency.

citation: Merkel Cell Polyomavirus Small T Antigen Induces DNA Damage Response (PMID: 31401636)
summary: MCPyV-positive human MCC cells show H2AX hyperphosphorylation. Overexpression of MCPyV sT antigen induces H2AX phosphorylation together with ATM activation and phosphorylation of 53BP1 and CHK2. This links viral sT to ATM-H2AX DDR signalling.

citation: Identification of a novel LATS1 variant associated with familial cerebral cavernous malformations in a Chinese family (PMID: 35986120)
variant_detail: c.821C>T, p.Thr274Ile
phenotype: Familial cerebral cavernous malformations (CCMs) on MRI; Five-generation Chinese Han family with nine members affected; No CCM1-3 variants detected
diagnostic_reason: Identified by WES after exclusion of CCM1-3 variants. Co-segregated with the CCM phenotype in the family (Sanger sequencing). Predicted damaging in silico. Impaired angiogenesis in HUVEC assays supported a functional effect.

citation: Hippo pathway links adipocyte plasticity to adipose tissue fibrosis (PMID: 36229481)
phenotype: Lats1/2-knockout adipocytes dedifferentiated into DPP4+ progenitor cells; Lats1/2-knockout adipocytes converted to DPP4- myofibroblasts upon TGFβ stimulation; Hippo pathway inhibition impaired adipocyte identity and promoted ECM remodeling; Adipose tissue fibrosis, which was relieved by YAP/TAZ inhibition in obese mice with improved metabolic homeostasis

citation: Hippo-Yap Signaling Maintains Sinoatrial Node Homeostasis (PMID: 36317529)
phenotype: Lats1/2 inactivation in the cardiac conduction system (Hcn4CreERT2) caused severe sinus node dysfunction; Dysregulated calcium handling; Increased SAN fibrosis; Decreased Ryr2 expression; Increased Tgfb1 and Tgfb3 expression; Phenotype rescued by Yap/Taz deletion, with normal sinus rhythm and reduced fibrosis

citation: YAP-Induced Glycolysis Drives Fibroinflammation and Disrupts Fibroblast Fidelity (PMID: 41165345)
phenotype: Lats1/2 inactivation in cardiac fibroblasts activated glycolysis and drove fibroinflammation and fibrosis; Increased fibroblast proliferation; Fibroblasts shifted to a SOX9+ osteochondroprogenitor state; CSF1-mediated macrophage expansion; Macrophage IGF1 signaling enhanced fibroblast proliferation; Fibrosis reduced by glycolysis inhibition or blocking macrophage expansion

citation: YAP/TAZ-CDC42 signaling regulates vascular tip cell migration (PMID: 28973878)
phenotype: Endothelial Lats1/2 deletion caused nuclear YAP/TAZ translocation; Blocked endothelial migration during retinal angiogenesis; Phenocopied Yap/Taz-deficient mutants

citation: Wnt and Src signals converge on YAP-TEAD to drive intestinal regeneration (PMID: 33950519)
phenotype: Lats1/2 conditional knockout (YAP gain of activity) was sufficient to drive crypt hyperproliferation in the intestine

citation: Regulation of the Hippo-YAP pathway by G-protein-coupled receptor signaling (PMID: 22863277)
summary: LPA and S1P act through G12/13-coupled receptors to inhibit the Hippo kinases Lats1/2, which activates YAP/TAZ. Gs-coupled receptor stimulation by glucagon or epinephrine instead activates Lats1/2 kinase activity and inhibits YAP. This places LATS1/2 downstream of GPCR signaling.

citation: Liquid-Liquid Phase Separation of DDR1 Counteracts the Hippo Pathway to Orchestrate Arterial Stiffening (PMID: 36475898)
summary: DDR1 undergoes stiffness/collagen-induced liquid-liquid phase separation and co-condenses with LATS1 through its C-terminus. This competitively blocks MOB1 binding to LATS1 and prevents LATS1 phosphorylation, inactivating LATS1 and activating YAP. In mice, LATS1 inhibition reactivated YAP in Ddr1-deficient vessels and abrogated the arterial softening.

citation: The Hippo pathway mediates Semaphorin signaling (PMID: 35613278)
summary: Class 3 Semaphorins activate the core Hippo kinases LATS1/2 through PlexinA and p190RhoGAP. This suppresses lung cancer cell growth (SEMA3B restoration) and inhibits angiogenesis.

citation: RIPK4 promotes epidermal differentiation through phase separation and activation of LATS1/2 (PMID: 40570855)
summary: A kinome library screen identified RIPK4 as an alternative upstream kinase of LATS1/2. RIPK4 recruits LATS1/2 into liquid condensates and directly phosphorylates them. Ripk4 knockout mice show Yap/Taz activation in the epidermal granular layer, and disease-derived RIPK4 mutants fail to activate LATS1/2.

citation: LATS1/2 loss promote tumor immune evasion in endometrial cancer through downregulating MHC-I expression (PMID: 38383447)
sample_size: TCGA cohort plus in-house EC sample cohort
summary: LATS1/2 are frequently mutated and downregulated in endometrial cancer. In CRISPR knockout cells, LATS1/2 loss lowered MHC-I independently of YAP. LATS1/2 directly bind and phosphorylate STAT1 at Ser727, promoting its nuclear accumulation and IRF1/NLRC5-driven MHC-I transcription, so loss of LATS1/2 confers resistance to immune-cell killing.

citation: Methylation-associated inactivation of LATS1 and its effect on demethylation or overexpression on YAP and cell biological function in human renal cell carcinoma (PMID: 25270913)
summary: LATS1 expression is reduced in RCC tissue (46.7% positive vs 76.7% in normal kidney) and correlates with grade and stage. The promoter is hypermethylated (97.5%) in 786-O cells. 5-Aza demethylation or LATS1 overexpression restored LATS1, reduced YAP, inhibited proliferation, and induced apoptosis and G1 arrest.

citation: Lats1/2 Sustain Intestinal Stem Cells and Wnt Activation through TEAD-Dependent and Independent Transcription (PMID: 32259481)
summary: In mouse intestine, Lats1/2 deletion causes loss of intestinal stem cells and Wnt-uncoupled crypt expansion. The Wnt inhibition is YAP/TAZ dependent but TEAD independent, because nuclear YAP/TAZ interact with TLE to block TCF-mediated transcription.

citation: Hippo-Yap Signaling Maintains Sinoatrial Node Homeostasis (PMID: 36317529)
summary: Conditional Lats1/2 inactivation in the sinoatrial node (Hcn4CreERT2) caused severe sinus node dysfunction, disrupted calcium handling with reduced Ryr2, and increased fibrosis with higher Tgfb1/3. Deleting Yap/Taz rescued the phenotype, so Lats1/2 act through Yap/Taz.

citation: Expression of LATS1 in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma and its effect on tumor cell proliferation and invasion (PMID: 36029506)
summary: LATS1 protein expression fell from 59.3% in normal epithelium to 11.3% in HNSCC on tissue microarray. LATS1 overexpression in B88 cells inhibited proliferation, migration, invasion and EMT, consistent with tumor suppressor activity.

citation: LATS1-Beclin1 mediates a non-canonical connection between the Hippo pathway and autophagy (PMID: 32944618)
summary: LATS1, but not LATS2, regulates sorafenib-induced lethal autophagy in HCC independently of its kinase activity, through a LATS1-specific domain. This is coupled to K27-linked ubiquitination and self-dimerization of Beclin-1 (BECN1).

citation: Recurrent deletions and reciprocal duplications of 10q11.21q11.23 including CHAT and SLC18A3 are likely mediated by complex low-copy repeats (PMID: 21948486)
variant_detail: Heterozygous 10q11.21q11.23 (10q11.21q21.1) deletions, 0.3–12 Mb, encompassing CHAT and SLC18A3 (SLC18A3 lies in the first intron of CHAT). 24 unrelated individuals with deletions, 20 clinically evaluated; 19 deletions flanked by directly oriented segmental duplications (NAHR). 9 individuals also had additional copy number changes. A separate group of 17 individuals had reciprocal duplications.
phenotype: developmental delay; intellectual disability; hypotonia; sleep apnea; chronic constipation; gastroesophageal reflux; vesicoureteral reflux; epilepsy; ataxia; dysphagia; nystagmus; ptosis; variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance (deletion also found in apparently normal carrier parents)
diagnostic_reason: Recurrent NAHR-mediated deletions detected by chromosomal microarray that include CHAT and SLC18A3. The authors suggest that hypotonia, ptosis, dysphagia and related features may result from deletion of these cholinergic genes. Penetrance is incomplete and expressivity variable, so causality is not established for SLC18A3 specifically.

citation: Epilepsy phenotype and gene ontology analysis of the 129 genes in a large neurodevelopmental disorders cohort (PMID: 37645600)
variant_detail: Not specified. SLC18A3 is named only in the full text, as one of 13 genes in the 'NDD-genes' group without definite reports of seizure-related phenotypes. These are genes with causative variants identified by exome sequencing in NDD patients with epilepsy. Zygosity and variant details are not given.
phenotype: neurodevelopmental disorder; epilepsy
diagnostic_reason: Variant classified as causative by exome sequencing in a pediatric NDD cohort. Per-patient details are not provided.

citation: Vesicular acetylcholine transporter defect underlies devastating congenital myasthenia syndrome (PMID: 28188302)
sample_size: 2 affected brothers; carrier frequency 1:30 in Yemeni Jews
summary: Homozygous SLC18A3 p.Gly360Arg was found by exome sequencing in two brothers with severe hypotonia, arthrogryposis and respiratory failure, a presynaptic congenital myasthenic syndrome. In stably transfected PC12A123.7 cells the mutant VAChT had normal mRNA but undetectable protein, consistent with post-translational degradation and loss of function.

citation: SLC18A3 promoted renal cancer development through acetylcholine/cAMP signaling (PMID: 36225635)
summary: SLC18A3 is upregulated in renal cancer patients. It enhances ACh uptake, which activates PKA/CREB signaling and drives cancer cell proliferation and invasive migration. SLC18A3 overexpression increased tumor growth and lung metastases in A489-bearing mice.

citation: Inhibition of cholinergic signaling causes apoptosis in human bronchioalveolar carcinoma (PMID: 23222296)
summary: Human BACs express VAChT (SLC18A3) along with other cholinergic factors, and nicotine upregulates ChAT and VAChT. The VAChT antagonist vesamicol induced apoptosis in cell culture and nude mouse models, and siRNA knockdown of VAChT reversed this effect. Vesamicol also inhibited Akt phosphorylation, and constitutively active Akt rescued the apoptosis.

citation: The cholinergic system in rat testis is of non-neuronal origin (PMID: 21482687)
summary: Non-neuronal cells in the rat testis parenchyma express Slc18a3 mRNA, together with Chat, Slc5a7 and Slc22a2, in regions lacking innervation. This points to a non-neuronal cholinergic system, possibly involved in germ cell differentiation.

citation: Oxidized/unmodified-polyethylene microplastics neurotoxicity in mice: Perspective from microbiota-gut-brain axis (PMID: 38484610)
significance: significant down-regulation (p-values not given in abstract)
summary: Slc18a3 mRNA and protein in the brain cholinergic synaptic pathway (with Chat and Slc5a7) were significantly down-regulated by LDPE or Ox-LDPE microplastic exposure in mice. This was accompanied by reduced acetylcholine and cognitive dysfunction, and DP189&GOS treatment rescued ACh release.

citation: Arsenic Impairs Differentiation of Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells into Cholinergic Motor Neurons (PMID: 37624150)
summary: In human iPSC-derived motor neurons, 0.5 μM arsenic impaired the cholinergic synapse pathway. SLC18A3 transcripts were downregulated at day 18, together with CHAT, SLC5A7 and ACHE.

citation: Spatial transcriptomic profiling of human paravertebral sympathetic chain ganglia reveals diabetes-induced neuroplasticity (PMID: 40667173)
summary: SLC18A3 expression defined the cholinergic neuronal population in human lumbar sympathetic ganglia, distinct from the TH-defined noradrenergic populations. In diabetic ganglia, cholinergic neurons shifted toward a noradrenergic identity.

citation: Gene expression profiles in peripheral blood mononuclear cells of Asian obstructive sleep apnea patients (PMID: 24732660)
summary: SLC18A3 was differentially expressed in PBMCs of OSA patients versus controls by microarray. Its expression was a possible marker of severe OSA (RDI>30).

citation: Identifying genetic variants for heart rate variability in the acetylcholine pathway (PMID: 25384021)
summary: A candidate gene association study tested 443 variants in eight acetylcholine pathway genes, including SLC18A3, for association with RMSSD heart rate variability. No SNP was significant after multiple testing correction, so SLC18A3 showed no common-variant association.

citation: Transcriptome-scale spatial gene expression in rat arcuate nucleus during puberty (PMID: 35063020)
summary: In the rat arcuate nucleus, the Kiss1-expressing neuronal subcluster could be isolated using SLC18A3 as a unique membrane surface biomarker, showing SLC18A3 is enriched in kisspeptin neurons.

citation: A unique de novo gain-of-function variant in CAMK4 associated with intellectual disability and hyperkinetic movement disorder (PMID: 30262571)
variant_detail: c.981+1G>A (essential splice-site; 77-nt out-of-frame deletion in the transcript, p.Lys303Serfs*28)
phenotype: milestone delay; intellectual disability; autism; ataxia; mixed hyperkinetic movement disorder; severe generalized dystonia
diagnostic_reason: De novo on trio exome sequencing. The variant is absent from variant catalogs, and variants depleting the regulatory domain are unobserved in the population. cDNA analysis showed a stable transcript with a premature stop codon in the last exon, losing the C-terminal regulatory domain. Proband-derived cells showed increased CaMKIV activity, consistent with gain of function.

citation: A Neurodevelopmental Disorder With Dystonia and Chorea Resulting From Clustering CAMK4 Variants (PMID: 33211350)
variant_detail: Clustering CAMK4 variants (specific notation not available in the provided text)
phenotype: neurodevelopmental disorder; dystonia; chorea
diagnostic_reason: The variants cluster in the gene, and the phenotype is shared across patients and similar to the previously reported CAMK4 case. Details are not given in the provided text. The missense type is inferred, not stated.

citation: CAMK4-related Case of Hyperkinetic Movement Disorder (PMID: 37070062)
variant_detail: Not available in the provided text
phenotype: hyperkinetic movement disorder
diagnostic_reason: Not stated in the provided text; the title indicates a CAMK4-related case report.

citation: Genetic Etiologies of Dystonia with Anarthria/Aphonia (PMID: 42817183)
variant_detail: Pathogenic CAMK4 variant (previously published; notation not given in the provided text)
phenotype: dystonia with anarthria/aphonia; developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; ataxia
diagnostic_reason: Described as a known pathogenic CAMK4 variant in a previously published case.
center_country: The Hospital for Sick Children and Toronto Western Hospital, Toronto, Canada

citation: Copy number variations in a Brazilian cohort with autism spectrum disorders highlight the contribution of cell adhesion genes (PMID: 34664255)
variant_detail: Rare CNV encompassing CAMK4 (specific coordinates and type not given in the abstract)
phenotype: autism spectrum disorder
diagnostic_reason: The CNV was classified as a VUS, but recurrence of CAMK4-containing CNVs in the Brazilian NDD, MSSNG and TCAG cohorts strengthened the gene's candidacy.

citation: Two independent families with de novo whole APC gene deletion and intellectual disability: a case report (PMID: 39780213)
variant_detail: 15.4 Mb de novo heterozygous deletion at 5q21.2-q22.3 (includes CAMK4 and APC)
phenotype: familial adenomatous polyposis (>500 colorectal polyps); gastric fundic gland polyposis; duodenal adenomas; mild intellectual disability
diagnostic_reason: De novo contiguous deletions on copy-number trio analysis. CAMK4 is one of 22 genes in the narrowed common deleted region that may explain the intellectual disability. Causality for CAMK4 itself is not established.

citation: Two independent families with de novo whole APC gene deletion and intellectual disability: a case report (PMID: 39780213)
variant_detail: 9.8 Mb de novo heterozygous deletion at 5q22.1-q23.1 (includes CAMK4 and APC)
phenotype: familial adenomatous polyposis (~50 colorectal polyps); fundic gland polyposis; duodenal adenomas; mild intellectual disability
diagnostic_reason: De novo contiguous deletions on copy-number trio analysis. CAMK4 is one of 22 genes in the narrowed common deleted region that may explain the intellectual disability. Causality for CAMK4 itself is not established.

citation: Wilson Wong et al. 2000 - Spermiogenesis and exchange of basic nuclear proteins are impaired in male germ cells lacking Camk4 (PMID: 10932193)
phenotype: Male infertility; Impaired spermiogenesis in late elongating spermatids; Disrupted sequential deposition of sperm basic nuclear proteins on chromatin; Specific loss of protamine-2; Prolonged retention of transition protein-2 (Tnp2) in step-15 spermatids

citation: Cerebellar defects in Ca2+/calmodulin kinase IV-deficient mice (PMID: 11069976)
phenotype: Locomotor defects consistent with altered cerebellar function; Normal overall cerebellar cytoarchitecture; Reduced number of mature Purkinje neurons; Reduced calbindin D28k expression in Purkinje neurons; Reduced CREB Ser133 phosphorylation in cerebellum; Altered neurotransmission at excitatory synapses in Purkinje cells; Multiple climbing fiber innervation and enhanced parallel fiber synaptic currents, indicating immature Purkinje cell development
significance: significant reduction in Purkinje neuron number and CREB phosphorylation (p-values not given in abstract)

citation: Impaired CAMK4 Activity Limits Atherosclerosis and Reprograms Myelopoiesis (PMID: 40336480)
phenotype: Smaller and more stable atherosclerotic lesions in hypercholesterolemic mice (AAV8-PCSK9 plus high-fat/high-cholesterol diet); Peripheral monocytosis with skewing toward nonclassical Ly6clow monocytes; Markedly more myeloid progenitors in response to hypercholesterolemia; Higher Nr4a1 and myeloid differentiation gene expression in monocytes; Impaired monocyte trafficking in vitro and in vivo; Proreparative bone marrow-derived macrophage phenotype

citation: Calmodulin-dependent protein kinase IV regulates hematopoietic stem cell maintenance (PMID: 16020540)
phenotype: Hematopoietic failure; Diminished KLS (c-Kit+ Sca1+ Lin-/low) progenitor cell population; Inability to reconstitute blood cells upon serial transplantation; Increased apoptosis and proliferation of KLS cells; Decreased CREB Ser133 phosphorylation, CBP and Bcl-2 levels; Rescue of proliferation defects and CBP/Bcl-2 levels by CaMKIV re-expression

citation: Calcium/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase IV promotes imiquimod-induced psoriatic inflammation via macrophages and keratinocytes in mice (PMID: 35869084)
phenotype: Reduced severity of imiquimod-induced psoriasis in Camk4-/- mice; More macrophages and fewer IL-17A+ γδ TCR+ cells in skin; Increased IL-10 production by macrophages; Macrophage-specific Camk4 deletion alleviated psoriatic inflammation

citation: CaMK4-dependent activation of AKT/mTOR and CREM-α underlies autoimmunity-associated Th17 imbalance (PMID: 24667640)
phenotype: Naive T cells from Camk4-/- mice did not produce IL-17; Decreased frequency of IL-17-producing T cells; Ameliorated EAE and lupus-like disease with genetic or pharmacologic CaMK4 inhibition; Reduced CREM-α activation and AKT/mTOR signaling

citation: Regulation of osteoclast differentiation and function by the CaMK-CREB pathway (PMID: 17128269)
phenotype: Reduced CREB phosphorylation in Camk4-deficient cells; Downregulated c-Fos and impaired NFATc1 induction; Impaired osteoclast differentiation and function

citation: Calmodulin-dependent kinase IV links Toll-like receptor 4 signaling with survival pathway of activated dendritic cells (PMID: 17909078)
phenotype: Decreased number of dendritic cells in lymphoid tissues; Failure to accumulate mature DCs in spleen after in vivo LPS exposure; Camk4-/- DCs matured and released normal cytokines but failed to accumulate pCREB, Bcl-2 and Bcl-xL and did not survive; Bcl-2 transgene rescued DC survival

citation: CAMKK2-CAMK4 signaling regulates transferrin trafficking, turnover, and iron homeostasis (PMID: 32460794)
phenotype: Abnormal post-translational modifications and turnover of transferrin in cerebellum and liver; Iron dyshomeostasis in cerebellum and liver

citation: Calcium calmodulin kinase IV deficiency in podocytes prevents the development of lupus nephritis (PMID: 39793862)
phenotype: Podocyte-specific Camk4 deletion in B6.lpr mice did not affect systemic autoimmunity; Reduced glomerular pathology with less mesangial cell proliferation; Diminished kidney immune complex deposition; Decreased albuminuria and improved creatinine; Increased immune complex deposition in the liver

citation: Lung cancer stem cell study - TIPRL Regulates Stemness and Survival in Lung Cancer Stem Cells through CaMKK2-CaMK4-CREB Feedback Loop Activation (PMID: 39076120)
summary: In lung cancer stem cells, TIPRL binds CaMKK2 and sustains CaMKK2-mediated activation of CaMK4. CaMK4 phosphorylates CREB at Ser129/Ser133, driving expression of Bcl2 and HMG20A. CREB in turn activates TIPRL transcription, forming a positive feedback loop that supports stemness, survival and drug resistance.

citation: Camk4-/- imiquimod psoriasis study - Calcium/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase IV promotes imiquimod-induced psoriatic inflammation via macrophages and keratinocytes in mice (PMID: 35869084)
summary: CaMK4 expression is increased in psoriatic human skin and in IMQ-treated mouse skin. Camk4-/- mice and macrophage-specific Camk4 deletion show reduced psoriasis severity. CaMK4 suppresses macrophage IL-10 production and, in keratinocytes, inhibits apoptosis and promotes proliferation and S100A8/CAMP expression.

citation: CaMK4 in acute lung injury - CaMK4 Promotes Acute Lung Injury Through NLRP3 Inflammasome Activation in Type II Alveolar Epithelial Cell (PMID: 35734175)
summary: CaMK4 phosphorylation is increased in the lungs of LPS-induced ALI mice. In A549 AEC II cells, KN-93 or CaMK4 siRNA reduced NLRP3 inflammasome activation, caspase-1 p20 and IL-1β/IL-18 production. KN-93 ameliorated lung injury in mice.

citation: CaMK4 downstream of α1G T-type channel - CaMK4 is a downstream effector of the α(1G) T-type calcium channel to determine the angiogenic potential of pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells (PMID: 34586897)
summary: CaMK4 is expressed in pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells. Blocking or knocking down the α1G channel reduced CaMK4 phosphorylation but not CaMK2 phosphorylation. CaMK4 inhibition or knockdown reduced proliferation, migration and network formation without altering Akt phosphorylation, so α1G-Ca2+-CaMK4 acts independently of the Akt pathway.

citation: RNAi screen of host kinases - RNA Interference Screening Reveals Host CaMK4 as a Regulator of Cryptococcal Uptake and Pathogenesis (PMID: 28970273)
summary: An siRNA screen of 868 kinases and phosphatases identified CaMK4 as a specific regulator of C. neoformans uptake by host cells. Pharmacological inhibition of CaMK4 reproduced the phagocytosis defect. CaMK4-deficient mice survived longer after infection, with reduced pattern recognition receptor expression on phagocytes.

citation: Uygur hypertension association - CAMK4 gene variation is associated with hypertension in a Uygur population (PMID: 26909912)
sample_size: 1224 hypertensive patients and 967 controls (Han, Kazak, Uygur)
summary: The CAMK4 variant rs10491334 was associated with hypertension in the Uygur group: T-allele frequency was 12.5% in cases vs 6.38% in controls. No association was found in the Han or Kazak groups.

citation: CAMKK2-CAMK4 and transferrin trafficking (PMID: 32460794)
summary: CAMK4 acts downstream of CAMKK2 and overlaps with it in expression in mouse brain. In Camk4-/- mice, loss of CAMK4 caused abnormal post-translational modification and turnover of transferrin in cerebellum and liver, with iron dyshomeostasis. In CRISPR-edited HEK293 clones, CAMKK2-CAMK4 deficiency altered intracellular Ca2+ homeostasis and transferrin/TFRC complex interactions.

citation: CaMK4 in atherosclerosis - Impaired CAMK4 Activity Limits Atherosclerosis and Reprograms Myelopoiesis (PMID: 40336480)
summary: CaMK4 expression is increased in advanced/unstable human carotid plaque and in plaque macrophages. Camk4-/- mice developed smaller, more stable lesions, with monocytosis skewed to Ly6c-low monocytes and more myeloid progenitors. Higher Nr4a1 and ATF6-dependent transcription were seen, and CaMK4 silencing in human monocytes recapitulated the phenotype.

citation: CaMK4 in abortion-related Th17 imbalance (PMID: 32738170)
summary: CaMK4 is upregulated in the uteroplacental complex and spleen in LPS-induced abortion in mice. The inhibitor KN-93 reduced Th17 infiltration and function and reversed fetal resorption. CaMK4 acts through the AKT/mTOR pathway to promote Th17 expansion.

citation: Anti-PLA2R antibodies and podocyte damage (PMID: 35333675)
summary: Anti-PLA2R antibody stimulation of human podocytes increased calcium levels and CaMK4 expression, alongside apoptosis and cytoskeletal damage.
